title: Configured skills.paths are not exposed to LouiseLM agents
description:
## Problem

LouiseLM no longer appears to discover or expose skills from the configured global `skills.paths`. A `louiselm.lua` configuration points at a directory containing 34 skills, but asking the active LouiseLM agent which skills are available reports only one unrelated built-in/session skill. Skill loading previously worked with this configuration.

This suggests the configured skill catalog is being dropped between setup, discovery, chat construction, and agent context/native loading.

## Investigation

- Reproduce through the normal `louiselm.setup()` plus `:Louiselm` chat path, not only by calling `require("louiselm.skills").discover()` directly.
- Determine whether the regression is specific to `skills.policy = "native"`, `"inject"`, or both.
- Compare `:checkhealth louiselm` discovery results with the skills actually made available in the resulting session/chat.
- Preserve and surface discovery errors instead of silently reducing the catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a configured `skills.paths` directory containing multiple valid `SKILL.md` entries, a newly opened LouiseLM chat makes every valid discovered skill available according to the effective skills policy.
2. The normal setup/command integration path is covered by a regression test using multiple skills; coverage must fail if the catalog is omitted or reduced to a single skill.
3. Invalid skill entries do not hide valid siblings, and actionable discovery errors identify rejected paths/metadata.
4. `:checkhealth louiselm` and the session/chat behavior agree on whether configured skills were discovered and are available.
5. Focused tests and the full project quality gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed configured skill discovery end to end: follow SKILL.md symlinks after resolving targets, ignore unconsumed optional YAML metadata while validating required fields, remove the unused lyaml dependency gate, keep valid-sibling counts visible in checkhealth, and cover setup-to-chat injection of multiple skills. The real configured generated tree now reports 34 skills and 0 errors. Verification: focused red-green tests; full MiniTest 150/150; stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; git diff --check passed.

title: Write the first louiselm blog post and design blog.css theme
description:
Content and visual design for the first post published through louiselm-r1k's publishing pipeline, once that tooling exists.

## Scope

- Author blog/post-<name>/blog.md: prose plus literalinclude excerpts drawn from the conversations that inspired the pipeline itself (the permission-deadlock bug investigation and fix, session claude/71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea already sits at the louiselm repo root as a manually-copied buffer scrape — re-export it properly via LouiselmToMarkdown once that command exists, do not reuse the lossy manual copy).
- Choose which line ranges to literalinclude and from which source conversations (may span more than one session/tool, e.g. a claude session and a codex session).
- Design blog/blog.css — the actual visual theme for the blog prose (separate from the Neovim-rendered transcript theme, which is not a design decision, it is whatever the author's real Neovim config already looks like).

## Explicitly not this bead

- Any of the tooling itself (export command, scaffold script, render script, MyST/CI scaffold) — that is louiselm-r1k.

## Why deferred

Author-only work by explicit request — content and visual design are not something to hand to an agent. Filed so it is not forgotten once the tooling in louiselm-r1k lands, not because there is a decision being deferred.

title: QA round: native ACP command invocation (louiselm-2w4)
description:
# Manual QA review — native ACP command invocation (louiselm-2w4)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `9322523` (main). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: louiselm-2w4 made the skill picker invoke adapter-native slash
commands (Codex `$name`, Claude bare `name`) instead of always injecting the
full `SKILL.md` body. Everything shipped with full mock/unit coverage, but all
of it uses hand-typed ACP fixtures. Before running a single human case, I
inspected real ACP debug logs already on this machine (this very session runs
through `claude-agent-acp`) and found a confirmed bug: Claude's real adapter
appends `" (user)"` to every advertised command description sourced from a
configured skill path, which broke exact-match description correlation for
every skill, every time. Filed and fixed as **louiselm-s88** (see Findings)
before this round started. What's left needs a live interactive Neovim, which
I can't drive myself:

- Does the fix actually work against the real `claude-agent-acp` end to end?
- What does the real `codex-acp` actually advertise — is the `$name`
  assumption (never observed in the available logs) correct at all?
- Chip rendering / cursor position in a real buffer.
- The "pick before any `available_commands_update` has arrived" race.

**Second finding, also before any human case ran:** asked for the skill
picker to be invoked and there was nothing to invoke it with — `pick_skill`
(and its siblings `pick_file`/`mention_buffer`/`send_selection`) had no
command, keymap, or reachable instance from the documented
`Louiselm.setup()` + `:LouiselmChat` path at all. Filed and fixed as
**louiselm-j8j** (see Findings) — `:LouiselmPickSkill` now exists.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Native pick + submit round-trips through real Claude | **passed** — `claude/8d6e76d1-e4e8-4a13-9bad-0337bbae6ea5`: response opens "I'll start by understanding the current state of louiselm before interviewing you on the rewrite decision," then reads AGENTS.md, explores lua/capture-service/android trees, checks `br list` — grill-me's own documented behavior verbatim |
| 2 | Native pick + submit round-trips through real Codex | **passed** — `codex/01a01ea6-c458-70f0-9140-d51d52ae42a6`: `available_commands_update` advertised `$grill-me` (first real observation, confirms the dollar-prefix assumption); response narrates "Using `grill-me` for the invocation test," with a `tool_call` reading the real `grill-me/SKILL.md` |
| 3 | Picking immediately after opening chat, before commands arrive | **not human-testable** — real adapter responds too fast to race by hand; already covered deterministically by `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` ("re-resolves a queued native command against the latest cache only when the turn releases it" et al.) |

## Setup

1. Pull the new commits into the installed plugin (it's a `vim.pack` clone
   pinned to a rev, not a live symlink):

   ```
   :lua vim.pack.update({"louiselm.nvim"})
   ```

   Confirm the running copy matches source:

   ```sh
   git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse HEAD
   python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('/home/lotso/.config/nvim/nvim-pack-lock.json'))['plugins']['louiselm.nvim']['rev'])"
   ```

   Both must print `35a83fb...`. If `vim.pack.update` reports nothing to do,
   restart Neovim after it — pack updates on a running instance don't always
   reload already-loaded Lua modules.

2. Clear stale ACP debug logs so the evidence check below only sees this
   round's sessions:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs && mv ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*.log /tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs/ 2>/dev/null
   ```

3. Skill fixture already exists at `~/.config/agentskills/generated/grill-me/SKILL.md`
   (`disable-model-invocation: true`, so it's picker-only — expected, that's
   what native mode is for). No changes needed there.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `grill-me` has `disable-model-invocation: true`. That's fine for native
  mode (explicit-only skills stay picker-visible), don't read it as a config
  error if you see it in the SKILL.md.
- Both `codex` and `claude` agents in `~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`
  leave `skills.policy` unset, so they inherit the global `native` default —
  no config change needed to test either.
- ACP debug logs land in `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<ts>-<pid>-<binary>-<label>-stdout-jsonrpc.log`,
  one pair (stdout+stderr) per spawned adapter process. `label` is the
  backend name for multi-backend agents; codex/claude sessions get no label,
  just `-codex-acp-` / `-claude-agent-acp-` in the filename.
- **`acp-debug.sh` only tees the adapter's stdout (its replies to us), never
  its stdin (what we send it).** The original "Evidence check" below assumed
  `session/prompt` requests would show up in the log — they never can, since
  that request travels the direction this script doesn't capture. Judge cases
  1/2 from the *response* side (does the reply read like the skill actually
  engaged), not from grepping for the outgoing request.
- **"just say hi and stop" is not a discriminating test prompt.** A Claude
  that correctly loaded grill-me and honored an explicit stop-override says
  "Hi," and so does a Claude that never saw `/grill-me` at all and just
  complied with the literal plain-text instruction — both paths produce
  identical output, so a bare "Hi" proves nothing either way. Use a prompt
  that would look obviously different if the skill engaged (e.g. "we should
  rewrite louiselm in Rust" — grill-me should start interrogating that claim
  one question at a time, unprompted).

## Cases

### 1. Native pick + submit round-trips through real Claude

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` (`Chat:pick_skill`, `build_content`,
`submit_prompt`) and `lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua`'s fixed
`description_matches`.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `claude`
> wait for the session to become ready (status line stops saying "starting")
> `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`
> confirm the buffer shows `[context: skill: grill-me]` in the prompt line
> type `we should rewrite louiselm in Rust` and submit (not "just say hi and
> stop" — see Ground rules, that prompt can't distinguish success from
> failure)

Expect: the chip disappears, the prompt line shows your typed text (not the
resolved command — that's expected, see Ground rules), and Claude starts
interrogating the Rust-rewrite claim one question at a time, unprompted —
grill-me's own documented behavior, not a normal direct answer.

Failure signature: notification `louiselm: advertised command 'grill-me'
description does not match the skill`, or a response that just answers/
discusses the claim directly instead of interviewing you about it.

**Status: passed**, `claude/8d6e76d1-e4e8-4a13-9bad-0337bbae6ea5` — see
Status table for the evidence.

### 2. Native pick + submit round-trips through real Codex

Exercises the same code path, but this is the **first-ever observation** of
what `codex-acp` actually sends for `available_commands_update` — every log
available to me from this machine only had a 1-line (`initialize`-only)
codex-acp transcript, so the `$name`-prefix assumption in
`native_command.lua` (`dollar_name = "$" .. skill.name`) is unverified
against a real payload.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `codex`
> wait for ready
> `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`, same as case 1
> type `we should rewrite louiselm in Rust` and submit

Expect: same as case 1 — chip clears, Codex responds as if `/grill-me` (or
whatever it actually names the command) were invoked.

Failure signature: same notification as case 1.

**Status: passed**, `codex/01a01ea6-c458-70f0-9140-d51d52ae42a6` — see Status
table for the evidence. This was also the first real observation of what
`codex-acp` advertises: confirmed `$grill-me` (dollar-prefixed), validating
the `native_command.lua` assumption.

### 3. Picking immediately after opening chat, before commands arrive

Exercises AC6 from louiselm-2w4: "picker activation before advertisement
waits safely and is late-bound at submission" — i.e. picking a skill in the
gap before the agent has sent its first `available_commands_update` should
not error or hang, just defer.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `claude` (or `codex`)
> as fast as possible after the command opens the buffer (before "Session:
> status=ready" settles), run `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`
> then type text and submit

Expect: either it resolves fine (if the update already arrived by the time
you typed and hit submit — likely, given how fast this is), or if you
genuinely submit before any advertisement, you get the "no advertised
command matches" notification with your text and chip preserved — not a
hang, not a crash, not lost input.

Failure signature: Neovim hangs, an unrelated Lua error, or the typed text
disappears.

## Evidence check

`acp-debug.sh` cannot show the outgoing `session/prompt` request (see Ground
rules — it only tees stdout). Judge from the response side instead: find the
session's log by its ACP session id (visible via `:LouiselmSessionId` or in
whatever you paste back to me), then dump what the agent actually said and
did:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json, sys
path = sys.argv[1]
for line in open(path):
    try:
        msg = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    params = msg.get('params', {})
    update = params.get('update', {}) if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
    su = update.get('sessionUpdate')
    if su == 'available_commands_update':
        names = [c['name'] for c in update['availableCommands']]
        print('available_commands_update: grill-me as', [n for n in names if 'grill' in n])
    elif su == 'agent_message_chunk':
        print('text:', repr(update.get('content', {}).get('text', '')))
    elif su in ('tool_call', 'tool_call_update'):
        print(su, update.get('title'), update.get('status'))
" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<the-matching-file>-stdout-jsonrpc.log
```

Pass condition: `available_commands_update` shows the expected command name
shape (`$grill-me` for Codex, bare `grill-me` for Claude), and the assembled
response text/tool calls read like the skill actually engaged (interrogating
the claim one question at a time, or in Codex's case an explicit `tool_call`
reading `grill-me/SKILL.md`) — not a direct answer to the literal prompt
text. This cannot prove the exact wire text sent; it proves what the agent
did in response, which is what actually matters.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Old logs stashed in `/tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs/` can be deleted.
- No other fixtures or state created this round beyond the two already-closed
  beads (louiselm-2w4, louiselm-s88).

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, what you saw, and paste (or point me at) the
relevant `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-stdout-jsonrpc.log` file if
something looks wrong — I'll pull the evidence myself. If something's broken
I'll fix it and you'll need to redo Setup step 1 before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Native bare-name matching never resolved against the real Claude
adapter** (`louiselm-s88`, fixed in `c230f8c`). `description_matches()` in
`lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua` required exact whitespace-normalized
equality between the advertised and local skill description. Real
`claude-agent-acp` appends `" (user)"` to every command sourced from a
user-configured skill path, so the comparison always failed — verified
against all 76 commands in a real `available_commands_update` payload from
this session's own ACP transcript, 27 of which are user skills, all 27
carrying the suffix. Found by reading a pre-existing debug log before running
any human case, not by a live test. Fixed by matching on the advertised
description *starting with* the local one instead of equaling it. Regression
test added using the real captured description pair.

**F2 — No command/keymap reached the context-picker API at all**
(`louiselm-j8j`, fixed in `9e553a1`). `pick_skill`/`pick_file`/
`mention_buffer`/`send_selection` were defined on `Chat` but never wired into
`command.lua`, and the `Chat` instance `:LouiselmChat` builds was never
exposed, so nothing following the documented `Louiselm.setup()` +
`:LouiselmChat` setup could ever reach them — including this QA round.
Discovered when asked to invoke the skill picker and there was nothing to
invoke. Fixed by adding `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile`,
`:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, `:LouiselmSendSelection`; README updated.
close_reason: Round complete. Cases 1 (real Claude) and 2 (real Codex) both passed with strong evidence pulled from real ACP debug logs (see description). Case 3 (early-pick race) is not human-testable — real adapters respond too fast to race by hand — and is already covered deterministically by tests/ui/chat_spec.lua. Two findings surfaced and fixed before this round finished: louiselm-s88 (Claude's scope-annotation suffix broke bare-name matching) and louiselm-j8j (no command reached the context-picker API at all). Both children closed and parented under this issue.

title: Preserve multiline chat prompts entered with Shift+Enter
description:
## Problem

In the Markdown chat buffer, Shift+Enter can insert a continuation line while editing the `> ` prompt. Pressing Enter afterward submits only the tracked first line. The continuation is omitted from the ACP prompt, remains visible below the newly inserted response/prompt area, and the model begins responding to incomplete input.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a louiselm chat session and type the first line in the `> ` prompt.
2. Press Shift+Enter to create a new line inside the Markdown quote block.
3. Type a second line.
4. Press Enter to submit.

## Observed

Only the first line is sent to the session. The second line remains stranded at the bottom of the chat buffer while the model responds.

## Expected

The submitted prompt contains every line in the editable prompt block, in order, with intentional newlines preserved. After a successful submit, no submitted continuation line remains as an orphaned draft.

## Code evidence

`Chat:submit()` reads only `view.prompt_line` via `nvim_buf_get_lines(..., view.prompt_line, view.prompt_line + 1, ...)`. `submit_prompt()` then inserts the response separator and next prompt immediately after that one line, so any continuation lines are shifted below the new chat area rather than consumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A two-line prompt entered with Shift+Enter is sent as one prompt containing both lines and their newline.
- All submitted prompt lines are rendered as transcript history and removed from the editable prompt region.
- The next `> ` prompt appears after the response area; no continuation text is left below it.
- Single-line submission and queued-prompt behavior remain unchanged.
- Headless UI tests cover multiline submission through the buffer-facing behavior, including the sent payload and resulting buffer layout.
close_reason: Fixed multiline chat prompt submission by reading and rendering the full prompt block. Added a headless regression test covering payload and buffer layout. Verification: focused chat suite 35/35, full mini.test suite 127/127, stylua --check passed, lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics, git diff --check passed.

title: Cancelling a turn leaves a zombie diff review and a blocked chat
description:
Predicted while writing the QA recipe, confirmed manually in session claude/8ee77329-247a-4f60-914f-9cb38bfed818 (case 5).

:LouiselmCancel during an open diff review works at the protocol level - the log shows PERMISSION id=2 kind=edit followed by TURN END cancelled, so the agent is released - but the UI is left broken:

- the review buffer stays on screen
- q and d appear to do nothing, because send_response only clears the review when the response succeeds and the request was already answered
- a opens the lifetime picker, and answering it fails the same way
- chat.decision_active stays set, so every guarded command keeps refusing with "a louiselm permission decision is open; answer it first"

Cause: Session:cancel answers outstanding requests through the raw ACP responder in cancel_permissions (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua), which the chat never sees. The chat wrapper that owns the decision slot is downstream of the session responder, so the session cannot call it.

Fix: the session emits a typed permission_cancelled event carrying the request ids it answered; the chat marks those decisions answered, closes an open review, releases the slot and pumps the queue. The decision slot is now compared by identity so a stale picker answering late cannot release the decision that replaced it.

An open picker still cannot be closed programmatically - vim.ui.select has no cancel handle - so answering a stale picker reports "permission decision was already answered". That is accepted.
close_reason: Fixed in c0ae0aa. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua asserts the permission_cancelled event carries both request ids; tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'closes a review and frees the chat when its request is cancelled' and 'drops queued decisions whose requests were cancelled'. Full suite 203 cases, stylua and lua-language-server clean. Needs a live retest of QA case 5.

title: Health check permanently reports codex as outdated even when versions match
description:
`:checkhealth louiselm` permanently reported `codex` as outdated even
immediately after upgrading it to the exact version npm reports as latest —
"— @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0 (latest 1.6.0 available)" with both
numbers identical.

## Observed

Live user report after upgrading via `npm install -g
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@latest` and confirming `codex-acp --version`
prints `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0`:

```
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0 (latest 1.6.0 available)
```

Reproduced directly against the real binaries with `Health.check`:

```
{ ..., latest_version = "1.6.0", outdated = false, version = "@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0" }
```
(after the fix; before it, `outdated` was unconditionally `true`).

`claude` never showed this symptom — `claude-agent-acp --version` prints a
bare `0.70.0` with no name prefix, which happens to already match npm's bare
`0.70.0` output as a raw string.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua`, the `outdated` computation inside `M.check`'s
`finish()` (previously line ~205): `health_result.outdated =
health_result.version ~= latest_version` — direct string equality between
the installed-version banner and the latest-version check's output. These
are apples to oranges for `codex-acp`: its own `--version` banner is
`"@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0"` while `npm view
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp version` returns the bare `"1.6.0"`. Those
strings can never be equal, so `outdated` was unconditionally `true` for any
agent whose version banner carries a name prefix, regardless of actual
version — a permanent false positive, not something an upgrade could ever
clear.

## Why it was not caught

Every existing "matches" test used a *bare* installed-version string
(`"1.3.0"`) against a bare latest-version string (`"1.3.0"`) — never the
"banner has a name prefix, latest check does not" shape that `codex-acp`
actually exhibits. The only test with a prefixed installed version
(`"codex-agent-acp 1.3.0"`) paired it with a genuinely different latest
version (`"1.4.0"`), so raw inequality was still the correct answer there
and never exposed the false-positive/prefix issue.

## Fix

Added `extract_version(value)` (`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua`): pulls the
trailing semver-looking token out of a version string via a Lua pattern
(`v?(%d[%d%.%-%+%w]*)%s*$`), falling back to the whole string when no such
token is found. `outdated` now compares `extract_version(health_result.version)
~= extract_version(latest_version)` instead of the raw strings. The
*displayed* message still shows the full raw banner — only the comparison is
normalized.

## Acceptance

- `tests/agent/health_spec.lua`: new case "reports outdated false when the
  installed banner carries a name prefix the latest check doesn't" — fails
  (`outdated=true`) before the fix, passes after.
- All prior latest-version tests unchanged and still passing (genuinely
  outdated and genuinely-bare-matching cases both still correct).
- Verified against the real binaries: `Health.check` with `codex-acp`'s real
  `--version` output and a live `npm view` result now returns
  `outdated = false`.
- Full suite 277/277 (was 276 before this new test), `stylua --check` and
  `lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning` clean.

## Not covered

`extract_version`'s pattern is a heuristic (last digit-leading token), not a
full semver parser — a version banner with no digits at all, or digits
embedded in unrelated trailing text, could still compare incorrectly. Not
observed in practice for any agent in this codebase's test fixtures or the
user's real config; not hardened further per the existing file's lightweight
string-matching style (see `first_line`).
close_reason: Fixed in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua: added extract_version() to pull the trailing semver token out of a version banner before comparing, instead of raw string equality. Verified against the real codex-acp binary (1.6.0) and live npm registry query (1.6.0): outdated now correctly reports false. Test: tests/agent/health_spec.lua 'reports outdated false when the installed banner carries a name prefix the latest check doesn't'. Full suite 277/277, stylua/lua-language-server clean.

title: health.check --version drops normalized.args, breaking wrapper-script agents
description:
In lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, M.check's primary --version check builds
its command as:

    local command = { normalized.command, "--version" }

This drops normalized.args entirely. For any agent definition where
`command` is a wrapper script that expects an argument selecting the real
binary (e.g. real-world usage: command = "acp-debug.sh", args =
{"codex-acp"}), the check actually runs `acp-debug.sh --version` instead of
`acp-debug.sh codex-acp --version`.

Confirmed by hand: acp-debug.sh --version makes the wrapper's own
`basename "$1"` call receive the literal string "--version", which GNU
basename interprets as its own --version flag, so the wrapper prints
"basename (GNU coreutils) 9.7" (and license text) to stdout instead of
running the wrapped binary at all. The health check then reports that
garbage as the "installed version" -- both in :checkhealth louiselm and in
the outdated-version warning added in commit ee59c4b, which depends on this
same version string.

Confirmed via `git show fde8c6a:lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua` that this bug
predates ee59c4b -- it is not a regression from today's work, just newly
visible because of it.

Fix: build the command as normalized.command followed by all of
normalized.args, then "--version", matching how start_latest_check in the
same file already does it correctly.
close_reason: Fixed: M.check now builds the --version command as normalized.command + normalized.args + '--version', matching start_latest_check. Verified by hand against the real acp-debug.sh wrapper (reports @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 instead of basename's own version string) and added tests/agent/health_spec.lua case 'includes wrapper args before --version' using the deferred async vim.system stub. Full mini.test suite green (266 cases), stylua/lua-language-server clean on touched files.

title: Warn when configured agents are outdated (checkhealth + chat open)
description:
Agents (codex-acp, claude-agent-acp, etc.) are npm-installed binaries with no
auto-update mechanism. louiselm already checks each agent's own --version
(lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, lua/louiselm/health/init.lua). Add an optional
"latest available version" check per agent, and a warning when the installed
version doesn't match, surfaced both in :checkhealth and when a chat session
opens (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua ensure_chat()).

Design:
1. lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua: optional `latest` key on an agent
   definition, structurally identical to command/args/env (reuse
   copy_args/copy_env). Add `louiselm.agent.LatestCheck` LuaCATS type.
   Vendor-agnostic: "how to find latest version" is just another arbitrary
   command (e.g. `npm view <pkg> version`), same pattern as the existing
   --version check. No npm-specific code in louiselm.nvim.
2. lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua: when definition.latest is present,
   M.check also spawns that command via vim.system and compares its
   output (first line, trimmed) against --version. Extend HealthResult
   with latest_version?/outdated?. Two independent async vim.system
   calls must coordinate so on_result fires exactly once (AGENTS.md

title: QA round: AGENTS.md resource_link injection (louiselm-ce6.20)
description:
# Manual QA review — AGENTS.md resource_link injection

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `fde8c6a` (feat(context): attach project instructions as
an ACP resource_link, closes louiselm-ce6.20), repo now at `6b2a69f` (two
later commits are unrelated agent health-check work, not part of this
feature's scope). **Restart Neovim after any fix** — this is a plugin loaded
from source, there is no build step, but Lua modules are cached per-process.

Origin: on a brand-new ACP session's first prompt, louiselm now attaches a
`resource_link` content block (name + URI, not the file body) pointing at a
configured project-instructions file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`), when
`context.instructions_file` is set and the file exists at the project root.
The automated suite (251/251 mini.test cases, including one real-wire-bytes
test via a fake ACP process) proves the block is *sent* correctly. It cannot
prove a real agent *does anything* with it, and it cannot show you what the
chat buffer actually looks like — that's this round.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | A real agent actually reads the linked file | **passed** — session `claude/25ef1772-…`, log `20260820-082942-635200-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`: first action is a native `Read` tool call on `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md`, answer cites AGENTS.md:229-239 verbatim-correct |
| 2 | Visible context chip on a brand-new session | **passed** — session `claude/8fe8fd28-…`, cursor lands after the chip |
| 3 | No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions | **passed** — user-confirmed, no duplication/leakage |
| 4 | Resumed session never gets the link | **passed** — session `claude/1dec0a6e-…` resumed, no `[context: ...]` chip |

## Setup

Add this to wherever you already call `require("louiselm").setup(...)` in
your Neovim config (I don't have that path — tell me if you want me to look):

```lua
require("louiselm").setup({
  -- ...your existing agents/skills/etc...
  context = { instructions_file = "AGENTS.md" },
})
```

Restart Neovim fully (`:qa` and relaunch) so the new commit's Lua is loaded
fresh, not the cached previous version. Confirm the running copy matches
source: `:lua print(require("louiselm.instructions") ~= nil)` should print
`true` with no error — that module didn't exist before this commit, so an
error here means you're still on stale Lua.

Run all cases from a project whose root already has `AGENTS.md` — this repo
(`/home/lotso/code/louiselm`) qualifies, since it has one. Open Neovim with
`cwd` set to this repo for that reason (`cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm && nvim`).

## Ground rules learned the hard way

(empty so far — append here whenever a case misses for an environmental
reason rather than a code reason)

## Cases

### 1. A real agent actually reads the linked file

Exercises the entire point of `fde8c6a` — a mock ACP process can prove the
bytes were sent, it cannot prove any real agent binary honors a
`resource_link`. Also worth knowing going in: louiselm's ACP client currently
advertises `fs = { readTextFile = false }` (`lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:195`,
predates this commit) — so a strictly spec-compliant agent should not even
attempt to fetch the link *through the ACP protocol*. The only way this can
work today is if the agent opens the local `file://` path directly off disk
itself. That's a real uncertainty this case is meant to settle, not a
predicted bug — some agents may ignore `resource_link` blocks entirely.

Steps:

> Open `:LouiselmChat` (or `:LouiselmNewSession`) against whichever real,
> responsive agent you normally dogfood with. As the very first prompt of
> the new session, type something that only makes sense if the agent has
> actually read this repo's `AGENTS.md`, e.g.:
>
> `> Without me telling you, name one thing this project's AGENTS.md says agents must do before finishing a code task.`

Expect: the agent's answer names something real from this repo's `AGENTS.md`
(e.g. "run stylua/lua-language-server/mini.test before handoff", "use
red-green-refactor", "don't add compatibility shims").

Failure signature: the agent says it doesn't have access to that file, asks
you to paste it, answers generically/incorrectly, or answers about a
*different* AGENTS.md-style convention it already knows from training rather
than this repo's actual content.

Evidence: if your agent is the default DeepSeek-backed
`acp-llm-adapter` wrapped by `acp-debug.sh`, its **stdout** (agent→client
direction) is logged to
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<timestamp>-<pid>-*-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(newest file for this run — match by the timestamp printed at session start,
not "most recent," since old logs pile up). That log will *not* show the
`resource_link` louiselm sent (that's client→agent, unlogged by this script)
but it will show whether the agent issued an `fs/read_text_file` request back
— which it shouldn't, given the capability is off — and whatever `session/prompt`-adjacent
traffic it produces. For any other agent: there's no log, so this case rests
on what you read in its answer. Say so plainly when you report back.

### 2. Visible context chip on a brand-new session

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` `Chat:new_session` (queues
`instructions_context`) and `queue_context`'s `context_prefix` rendering.
Purely synchronous UI state — doesn't need the agent to ever respond.

Steps:

> Run `:LouiselmNewSession` (or `:LouiselmChat` for the first session). Look
> at the prompt line before typing anything.

Expect: the prompt line reads `> [context: AGENTS.md] ` — one clean chip,
cursor positioned right after it, ready to type. Type `hi` and look again:
`> [context: AGENTS.md] hi`, chip text not duplicated, not overwriting itself.

Failure signature: chip missing entirely, chip text garbled/duplicated,
cursor lands before the chip instead of after it, or typing overwrites part
of the `[context: AGENTS.md]` marker itself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer. No file/log needed for this one.

### 3. No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions

Exercises the once-per-new-session gating in `Chat:new_session` — automated
coverage only exercises a single session per test process, never two created
back-to-back sharing one `Chat` instance.

Steps:

> With the chat UI already open from case 2, run `:LouiselmNewSession` again
> to create a second, sibling session (don't resume/switch to the first).
> Look at its prompt line. Then switch back to the first session
> (`:LouiselmSwitchSession`) and look at its prompt line again.

Expect: the second session's prompt line also shows exactly one
`[context: AGENTS.md]` chip. The first session's line is unaffected by the
second session's creation (still whatever you left it at in case 2 — one
chip, not two).

Failure signature: either session shows the chip twice concatenated, the
second session shows no chip at all, or the first session's chip
duplicates/changes after the second session is created.

Evidence: what you see in each session's buffer, switching between them.

### 4. Resumed session never gets the link

Exercises the `Chat:resume_session`/`load_session` path, which — unlike
`Chat:new_session` — never queues `instructions_context`. This is the
mechanism AC #4 relies on; automated coverage only asserts it for a directly
`attach`-ed fake session, never through the real discovery/picker UI.

Steps:

> Close the chat UI (`:LouiselmCloseSession` or just `:qa` and relaunch
> Neovim). Run `:LouiselmResume` (or `:LouiselmResume!` for all workspaces)
> and pick one of the sessions created in cases 2/3 from the picker.

Expect: the resumed session's prompt line shows no `[context: ...]` chip at
all — plain `> `.

Failure signature: a `[context: AGENTS.md]` chip appears on a resumed
session's prompt line before you've typed or queued anything yourself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer right after resume, before typing.

## Evidence check

There's no single command that verifies all four cases — 2 through 4 are
pure UI-state observations (that's the point: things a mock-ACP unit test
cannot see), and case 1 has a log only if you're on the default DeepSeek
agent. Report what you saw for each; I'll flag anything that sounds like a
recipe issue (wrong cwd, stale Lua) versus a real product bug before we
record it.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures created outside your own Neovim session state (no files written,
no repo state changed). Nothing to revert beyond closing the chat sessions
you opened for cases 2–4.

## Reporting back

Tell me which case, what you saw, and anything surprising — especially for
case 1, since "the agent answered correctly" only proves the happy path;
tell me if it hedged, refused, or answered from training data instead of the
actual file. I'll pull whatever log evidence exists myself before we call a
case passed or failed.

## Findings this round

**F1 — cursor landed before the queued context chip, not after** (`louiselm-muo`,
closed, fixed in `e15a846`). `Chat:attach` sets the cursor once at
`ui/chat/init.lua:1441` before `Chat:new_session` queues any automatic context;
`queue_context` rewrote the prompt line to prepend the chip but never moved the
cursor, so it stayed at the pre-chip column regardless of chip length. Affects
skill-catalog inject mode too, not just this feature — pre-existing bug this
round's case 2 was the first thing to exercise. Fixed: `queue_context` now
repositions the cursor to just past the full `context_prefix` after rewriting
the line. Regression test: `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` "positions the cursor
after queued context, not before it" (failed `{6,1}` vs expected `{6,27}`
before the fix). Full suite 267/267, stylua/lua-language-server clean.
Confirmed live by user in session `claude/8fe8fd28-ac0c-4293-bc77-5fc605d432ea`.
close_reason: 4/4 cases passed. Case 1 (real agent honors the resource_link) and case 2 (visible chip) each got direct session-log/user evidence; 1 real bug found and fixed (louiselm-muo, cursor position). Cases 3 and 4 confirmed by direct user observation per the working file's own evidence design (no artifact for pure UI-state cases).

title: Invoke native skills through advertised ACP commands
description:
## Goal

Make the local skill picker invoke adapter-native skills exactly once through current ACP command advertisement.

## Scope

- In scope: handle `available_commands_update` per session; every valid update replaces the cache, an empty update clears it, malformed entries are skipped and diagnosed, and duplicate entries remain visible to ambiguity detection.
- In scope: correlate only locally discovered configured skills. Prefer exact `$<skill-name>`; otherwise allow exact `<skill-name>` only when the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description or OpenAI short description.
- In scope: make `$name` win over a colliding built-in `name`; reject ambiguous matches.
- In scope: keep picker selections pending when no command update exists, without guesses or timeouts; re-resolve against the latest cache at actual submission and queued-prompt release.
- In scope: if a command disappears or becomes ambiguous, send nothing and preserve the user's prompt and skill chip with an actionable error.
- In scope: send the advertised command and task as one first text block, such as `/$grill-me stress-test this` for Codex or `/grill-me stress-test this` for Claude.
- In scope: send no LouiseLM catalog or skill body in native mode and leave user-authored slash commands untouched.
- Out of scope: a general ACP command browser, adapter-name heuristics, and injected discovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Command state always reflects the latest valid update and recovers on later updates.
2. Malformed entries do not preserve a stale previous command list.
3. Codex-style dollar commands and Claude-style exact commands resolve using the strict agreed rules.
4. A built-in `plan` cannot steal a local `plan` skill when `$plan` is advertised.
5. Duplicate or weak description-only matches never trigger a command.
6. Picker activation before advertisement waits safely and is late-bound at submission.
7. Disappearing/ambiguous commands preserve unsent user input.
8. Mock ACP tests cover replacement, empty/malformed updates, duplicates, collisions, pending selection, queued release, command formatting, manual slash passthrough, and no-double-send behavior.

## Testing

Drive session command updates and captured prompt blocks through the mock ACP agent. Installed Codex/Claude adapters are manual smoke tests, not authenticated CI dependencies.
close_reason: Implemented native command invocation with full test coverage across session state, skill correlation, picker/submit wiring, and mock ACP integration. All 8 acceptance criteria met; full suite green (286 cases), stylua/lua-language-server clean.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Implemented in four layers, all TDD with mini.test:

1. Session state (lua/louiselm/session/{lifecycle,validation,events}.lua): new available_commands_update notification branch. Validation.available_commands() always replaces the cache (nil/malformed top-level -> empty, never a hard fail like config_option_update), skips malformed individual entries with a diagnostic message, and preserves duplicates for ambiguity detection downstream. New commands_changed event.

2. Correlation module (lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua, wired via skills/init.lua as Skills.resolve_command): unique $name (Codex) always wins and is never even compared against a colliding bare name (AC4's built-in-plan protection). Bare name (Claude) only resolves when its advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description or the new short_description field (lua/louiselm/skills/metadata.lua, sourced from metadata.short-description). Any name with >1 advertised entry (dollar or bare) is ambiguous and never resolves; duplicates are not collapsed first.

3. Picker + submit wiring (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua): native picks now set view.pending_skill instead of queuing resolved content immediately. build_content() (replacing prompt_content()) resolves the pending skill against the session's *current* command cache only at actual dispatch time -- called from both submit_prompt (immediate) and release_queued_prompt (deferred) -- so both paths always see the freshest cache, never one snapshotted when the picker ran. Resolution failure (disappeared/ambiguous) notifies and returns without touching the buffer, contexts, or pending_skill, preserving the user's typed text and the visible skill chip. Successful native mode sends one merged text block, e.g. "/$grill-me stress-test this", never a separate catalog/skill-body block.

4. Mock ACP coverage: tests/session/api_spec.lua (wire-level replace/empty/malformed/duplicate), tests/skills_spec.lua (resolve_command correlation matrix), tests/ui/chat_spec.lua (full picker->submit->queue->release flow, manual slash passthrough, no-double-send), tests/mock/agent_spec.lua (real subprocess mock agent now supports LOUISELM_MOCK_AVAILABLE_COMMANDS, proving the notification survives an actual process boundary).

All 8 acceptance criteria covered. Full suite green (286 cases), stylua and lua-language-server clean on all touched files.

Refs claude/

title: Resolve static per-agent skill policies and migrate configuration
description:
## Goal

Make `native`, `inject`, and `off` explicit, session-static Agent Skills policies with a native default and no inferred fallback.

## Scope

- In scope: keep skill paths global; add global `skills.policy = "native"` and permit only a per-agent `skills.policy` override.
- In scope: validate policy values through the existing configuration schema and expose the effective policy to session setup, UI status, help, and health.
- In scope: snapshot policy at session creation; never infer it from adapter names, command advertisement, filesystem capabilities, or runtime failures.
- In scope: remove `full_content` with a targeted migration error and remove the dormant `native_supported` automatic-fallback API.
- In scope: `off` disables the local picker and all LouiseLM skill automation; `native` does not require `lyaml` to start but local picker/validation is unavailable without it; `inject` is blocked without it.
- In scope: preserve user-authored slash commands in every policy.
- Out of scope: catalog formatting, native command correlation, runtime profile switching, and per-agent path overrides.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An agent with no override uses `native`.
2. DeepSeek/GLM-style agents can opt into `inject` without affecting Codex/Claude sessions.
3. Unknown policy values and per-agent path overrides fail validation clearly.
4. Legacy `full_content` configuration fails with exact replacement guidance.
5. No runtime event changes an existing session's policy.
6. Missing `lyaml` has the agreed profile-specific effects.
7. UI status can show a simple `skills: on` state while technical policy remains available in help/health.
8. MiniTest covers defaults, overrides, invalid/legacy keys, session snapshotting, dependency gating, off behavior, and lack of fallback.

## Testing

Exercise the declarative schema and session-facing policy API. Do not add adapter-name heuristics to tests or production code.
close_reason: Implemented static native/inject/off per-agent skill policies, lyaml gating, UI/health visibility, migration errors, docs, and deterministic MiniTest coverage; all 147 tests, StyLua, and lua-language-server pass

title: Grill-me needed: what documentation should louiselm.nvim provide, and how does Neovim's own diagnostics/LSP self-reflection factor in
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as explicit "food for thought" on 2026-08-20, while closing out a QA
round for louiselm-2w4/louiselm-s88/louiselm-j8j. The user explicitly asked
that this be filed in beads rather than kept in an agent's private memory --
louiselm is meant to be cross-adapter, and a note only one adapter's memory
can see is exactly the kind of context AGENTS.md says does not belong there.

## The question

What documentation should louiselm.nvim actually provide, for humans and for
agents, and does Neovim's own self-reflective diagnostic/LSP surface factor
into how that documentation gets authored, validated, or consumed?

## Evidence from the session that raised it

Checked during the QA round: there is no `doc/louiselm.txt` at all -- only
README.md. The only vimdoc-adjacent code, `lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua`,
generates config-schema field fragments (types, defaults) only; it produces
nothing for commands, workflows, or `:help` tag anchors. Nothing currently
generates or maintains a real `:help louiselm` experience.

## Threads worth pulling

- Human vs. agent audiences may want different artifacts, not one document
  wearing two hats: a real `:help louiselm.txt` (tag-jumping, `gq`-wrapped,
  kept in sync with commands/schema somehow) versus something built for
  agents to consume, closer to this project's own AGENTS.md pattern or an
  llms.txt-style reference. Decide whether that's one source, two
  generated outputs, or genuinely two hand-maintained documents.
- Neovim's own self-reflective capabilities -- `vim.diagnostic`, LSP client
  introspection, `:checkhealth` -- as a second, related thread: could/should
  louiselm's documentation lean on or expose these (e.g. health checks as
  living documentation, diagnostics as a way to validate config against docs,
  LSP-style hover/signature info for louiselm's own config schema)? Not
  pre-decided whether this belongs in the same artifact as the human/agent
  docs question above or is a separate concern entirely -- that's exactly
  what the grill should surface.
- `gen_vimdoc.lua` already exists and already generates *something* from the
  schema -- worth understanding its current scope and whether it's the
  right foundation to extend, versus a fresh mechanism.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.

title: Render submitted prompt contexts as native Neovim folds
description:
## Goal

Keep pre-send chat uncluttered while making every LouiseLM-attached prompt context exactly inspectable after submission.

## Scope

- In scope: before submission, represent manually selected skills and other contexts as compact chips; never display the automatic injected catalog as editable text or a marker.
- In scope: after an accepted prompt, render one closed native Neovim fold for that user turn containing every attached context in exact transport order and exact sent content.
- In scope: include concise context labels in the fold summary and preserve the ordinary visible user prompt.
- In scope: use normal Neovim fold commands and the existing chat buffer/context model; the fold is transcript representation only and must never be resent.
- In scope: retain chips and editable prompt on local send failure or blocked skill read.
- In scope: limit behavior to the live nofile, swap-disabled chat buffer; do not reconstruct folds after session load or Neovim restart.
- Out of scope: tool-call folding, transcript persistence, summary-only context storage, custom fold widgets, and a generic fold framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A pending automatic catalog produces no visible `[context: skill-index]` line.
2. One submitted turn with several contexts produces one closed fold with exact ordered contents.
3. Opening the fold reveals what ACP received, not a lossy summary.
4. The visible user prompt remains distinct from its attached context.
5. Failed local submissions keep pre-send chips and do not create a misleading submitted fold.
6. Reopening or closing folds cannot affect future prompt payloads.
7. MiniTest/headless UI tests cover fold boundaries, summary labels, exact contents/order, failure retention, and no resend.

## Testing

Use native fold APIs in a headless chat buffer and assert both buffer lines/fold ranges and captured ACP payloads.

## Notes

The current buffer is intentionally ephemeral and memory-resident. Documentation must explain that inspectability lasts only for the live chat.
close_reason: Completed live native context folds with exact ordered contents, failure retention, hidden-buffer scheduling coverage, and no-resend tests

TDD evidence: focused chat tests red then green; full MiniTest 309 cases, 0 failures; stylua --check lua tests and git diff --check pass; dependency graph has zero cycles. title: Concurrent ACP permission requests deadlock the session
description:
Two parallel tool calls in one agent turn produce two overlapping session/request_permission requests. louiselm opens one vim.ui.select picker per request with no serialization, so the second picker steals the first, the first is answered with outcome=cancelled without user input, and the second is never answered at all. The agent then blocks forever waiting on the permission response, and the session is unrecoverably stuck at status=prompting.

## Observed (session claude/25e0dc43-f1d6-4110-be74-e23b1d9920b7, 2026-08-16 19:45 UTC)

Agent JSON-RPC log ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260816-214042-74168-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:

- id=0  session/request_permission  find / -iname "*bc036951*"   -> answered (Always Allow), tool completed
- id=1  session/request_permission  wc -l ...gardening/....jsonl -> answered outcome=cancelled  (user did NOT choose this)
- id=2  session/request_permission  grep -n -i grill ...         -> NEVER answered

id=1 and id=2 were emitted back to back (19:45:12.63). Transcript
~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/25e0dc43-....jsonl records
"Tool permission request failed: Error: Tool use aborted" for toolu_01NgmPSjG8GXeMfmjuKrvfZZ (wc) 18ms after the grep tool_use, and has no tool_result at all for toolu_01K4jqsnByKAkCN5pJMRhRgU (grep).

Agent pid 74168 was still alive and blocked on id=2 more than 13 minutes later. The grep tool_call stayed "pending" forever; session/prompt never returned.

Proof the user never confirmed either choice: ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/permissions.json holds an always-rule for the find command only (mtime 19:45:04). Had the user actually confirmed "Always Allow" on the wc or grep picker, permission/store would have persisted a rule for it. It did not - the picker was dismissed programmatically, which is exactly what the user reported seeing ("a select picker that was pressed automatically and not by me").

## Symptoms

- Chat header shows "Model responding" forever; status=prompting.
- Typed input reports "Queued for next turn" and never runs, because Session:prompt requires status=="ready".
- One tool is reported to the model as aborted even though the user never denied it, so the model sees a bogus refusal.

## Root cause

1. lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:56 - every agent request is dispatched independently (nvim.schedule out of the fast event). No queue, no per-session serialization of session/request_permission.
2. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:732 prompt_permission -> lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua:11 calls vim.ui.select directly for each request. With an async provider (Snacks picker, which this setup uses) a second vim.ui.select while one is open tears down the first; its callback fires with nil -> cancel_permission responds outcome=cancelled to the wrong/first request, and the surviving picker never delivers a selection for the second request.
   Nothing tracks outstanding permission requests, so a request whose picker dies is never answered and never times out.
3. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:288 - permission_respond sets status back to "prompting" as soon as ANY single response is sent, regardless of other outstanding permission requests. That is why the UI showed "Model responding" instead of "Waiting for permission" while still blocking on id=2.

## Why tests miss it

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua stubs vim.ui.select with a synchronous callback (e.g. lines 172-188, 330-343), which serializes requests implicitly. Real async pickers do not.

## Fix direction

- Serialize permission prompts per session: queue incoming session/request_permission and open the next picker only after the previous one has been answered.
- Track every outstanding request id; guarantee exactly one response per request (fail-closed with outcome=cancelled on UI teardown/dispose so the agent is never left hanging).
- Keep status=="waiting_permission" while any permission request is still outstanding.
- Never let picker teardown cancel a request the user did not act on - prefer re-prompting or a queued prompt over a silent cancel.

## Acceptance

- Regression test with an async vim.ui.select stub that holds callbacks: two overlapping permission requests must produce two pickers shown one after the other and two responses, neither of them a spontaneous cancel.
- Test that disposing/closing while a permission is pending sends exactly one cancelled response per outstanding request.
- Test that status stays waiting_permission until all outstanding permission requests are answered.

## Recovery note

While stuck there is no documented way out except cancelling the turn; investigate whether Session:cancel actually unblocks an agent that is parked in session/request_permission.
close_reason: Fixed in c639f95. Sessions queue session/request_permission and publish one at a time (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua pump_permissions), status stays waiting_permission until the last outstanding request is answered, and a second response for the same request returns 'permission request was already answered'. Session:cancel now answers every outstanding request with outcome=cancelled, which is the recovery path the bug lacked. Remembered rules moved from arrival to publish time so an always choice covers requests already queued. Chat UI answers cancelled instead of dropping a choice made after view teardown. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua 'publishes overlapping permission requests one at a time', 'cancels every outstanding permission request when the turn is cancelled', 'applies a fresh always choice to permission requests already queued'; tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'cancels a queued permission choice after disposal'. Full suite 194 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. Deviation from the filed acceptance criteria: dispose clears the queue instead of writing cancelled responses, because dispose closes the ACP client and kills the agent process.

title: Permission picker Enter moves selection instead of confirming
description:
## Context

Observed in LouiseLM session codex/01a004ba-1d79-7a52-8d92-cec4cfdf1dc7 while committing. The permission picker displayed option 1 (Allow once) selected by default. Pressing Enter moved the option down in the picker instead of confirming it.

## Expected

Enter confirms the currently selected permission option and sends the ACP permission response.

## Actual

The selection/cursor moves down in the picker window; the permission is not immediately confirmed.

## Triage

LouiseLM delegates permission prompts to vim.ui.select. The current user Snacks config sets picker.sources.select.focus = "list" and enables wrap = true/linebreak = true. The recent permissions commit 757134a4 changed remembered-choice handling and option data, but did not change picker key handling. Likely interaction is in the Snacks select provider or its wrapping/focus configuration; reproduce with a minimal vim.ui.select containing the Codex options, then test with select wrapping disabled.

Relevant code: lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua prompt_permission() calls nvim.ui.select(options, ...).
Relevant docs: README.md explains Snacks select wrapping and recommends wrap = false for the select source when rows are not usable.
close_reason: Closed after reproducing with a very long permission option: Snacks vim.ui.select behaved correctly once picker source wrapping was disabled (wrap = false). The screenshot indicated keypresses had reached the underlying readonly chat buffer (E21), not a LouiseLM choice-handling failure. No LouiseLM bug reproduced.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Screenshot reproduction: Snacks picker shows 4/4 results but only two rows are visible in a very short list window; option 1 is highlighted. The underlying louiselm:// buffer reports E21 after attempting :verbose, which is expected because that buffer is nomodifiable; the command was not run in a command-line context. This points toward picker focus/list-window behavior or visual scrolling, not malformed permission choices.

title: Make reporting a session bug easy with a stable session identifier
description:
## Goal

Make it easy to report a louiselm bug against a specific session by telling the maintainer one stable identifier, instead of manually extracting context from the UI or conversation.

## Investigation

The current implementation has two different identifiers:

- The public session state exposes a local runtime id (`state.id`), which is not the ACP persistence id needed to correlate a resumed conversation.
- The agent-side ACP id is stored privately on the session (`acp_session_id`).
- The resume picker formats the title first and only falls back to the ACP id; the id is therefore not guaranteed to be the first visible item.

A bare ACP id may also be ambiguous when multiple configured agents can use the same id, so the most useful report token is the configured agent name plus the ACP session id (or an equivalent stable single-line representation).

## Proposed fix

Expose a deliberate, read-only report identity for the current session and make it easy to copy/quote:

1. Add a public session inspection field or method for the agent-side ACP session id/report identity, with LuaCATS documentation distinguishing it from the local runtime id.
2. Add a small user-facing command/action such as `:LouiselmSessionId` that reports the current session identifier and copies it to the Neovim clipboard when available; it should work for newly created and resumed sessions and fail clearly when no session is attached.
3. Put the report identifier first in the relevant session picker row, keeping title/workspace metadata available after it. Avoid exposing internal implementation fields directly or logging prompts/transcripts.
4. Document a short bug-report workflow: include the identifier, reproduction steps, and expected/actual behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can obtain one stable identifier for the currently displayed session with one command/action.
- The identifier remains useful after `:LouiselmResume` and identifies the ACP conversation, not merely the transient local session object.
- Agent identity is included when needed to avoid cross-agent ambiguity.
- The picker displays the report identifier as its first item/field.
- No prompt, tool payload, token, or other sensitive session content is copied or logged.
- Headless tests cover current-session, resumed-session, no-session, and picker-format behavior.
- README/help documentation explains how to include the identifier when reporting a bug.

## Follow-up

A separate grill-me session can stress-test whether a command, automatic bug-report template, or a richer session diagnostic bundle is the right UX before implementation expands beyond the minimal identifier workflow.
close_reason: Implemented stable agent-scoped ACP report identifiers. Public session snapshots expose acp_session_id; :LouiselmSessionId copies/reports <agent>/<ACP-id>; resume and attached-session picker rows lead with the report identity; README documents the bug-report workflow. TDD covered new, resumed, no-session, clipboard, and picker behavior. Full 131-case MiniTest suite passes; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server reports zero diagnostics; git diff --check passes; dependency graph has no cycles.

title: Document and diagnose Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Goal

Make Agent Skills configuration understandable and diagnosable for users of both known and unfamiliar ACP adapters.

## Scope

- In scope: update README skills/dogfooding sections, schema-generated help and annotations, migration guidance, and checkhealth.
- In scope: explain the three policies, native default, per-agent override, static sessions, natural-language versus picker activation, explicit-only skills, and the no-double-send contract.
- In scope: explain that Agent Skills specifies skill files, ACP is transport, and native command advertisement or Codex-like fallback behavior are host/adapter mechanisms rather than ACP skill specification features.
- In scope: document the fixed injected catalog behavior and 8,000-byte conservative Codex-inspired budget, including truncation/omission ordering and absolute-path privacy.
- In scope: provide platform-neutral `lyaml`/LibYAML installation guidance with common examples, Lua 5.1 ABI guidance for Neovim, no automatic install, and profile-specific missing-dependency effects.
- In scope: document root precedence, relative-path workspace trust, symlink aliases/escapes, skill-folder trust, `allowed-tools` permission limits, and the absence of automatic project roots or trust database.
- In scope: explain that injected implicit activation requires agent-side file access, picker-attached instruction-only skills may work without it, scripts/references/assets still need agent tools, and ACP does not standardize or let health verify this capability.
- In scope: show effective policy and detailed parser/discovery diagnostics in checkhealth, including shadowed/invalid skills, metadata conflicts, symlink escapes, line warnings, and catalog truncation/omission.
- In scope: document live-only fold contents and nofile/swap-disabled memory implications, plus manual installed Codex and Claude smoke procedures.
- Out of scope: authenticated adapter automation, a general ACP command UI, filesystem serving, and tool-call fold UX.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new user can choose `native`, `inject`, or `off` for an unfamiliar adapter from documentation alone.
2. Codex and Claude examples use native mode without duplicate injection; custom DeepSeek/GLM adapter examples show explicit inject overrides.
3. Old `full_content` users receive a direct migration explanation.
4. Checkhealth identifies actionable dependency, path, metadata, shadowing, and budget issues without claiming it can verify agent-side filesystem access.
5. Documentation explicitly labels the Codex-inspired budget/fallback as non-standard and leaves a future-spec reconsideration note.
6. Generated help/annotations and README configuration examples agree.
7. Manual smoke instructions verify native invocation with installed Codex and Claude adapters and injected behavior with a mock/custom adapter.

## Testing

Run documentation/schema consistency checks and health tests. Perform documented manual adapter smoke checks when credentials and installed adapters are available; do not make them CI requirements.
close_reason: Documented all Agent Skills profiles and trust/dependency behavior; added checkhealth catalog-budget diagnostics with tests.

comments.text: Completed Agent Skills profile documentation and diagnostics. README now explains Agent Skills vs ACP/host behavior, policy choice for unfamiliar adapters, native Codex/Claude and injected DeepSeek/GLM examples, static/no-double-send semantics, explicit-only behavior, lyaml/LibYAML installation and Lua 5.1 ABI, profile-specific dependency effects, root/symlink/workspace trust, absolute-path privacy, agent-side filesystem/tool limits, non-standard 8000-byte fallback, live folds, checkhealth, and manual native/inject smoke procedures. Schema descriptions feed matching policy text to vimdoc and LuaCATS. Checkhealth now reports inject catalog bytes and exact shortened/omitted names. Whole-tree StyLua and LuaLS remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua (louiselm-d7l; LuaLS 9 warnings there, none elsewhere). Installed adapter shims found for Codex, Claude, and acp-llm-adapter; existing manual evidence includes native Codex session codex/01a01f0d-a7c6-75d3-b749-a21b9d4f8d31 and three real injected Codex runs in louiselm-yik. Claude/custom procedures are documented; credentials were not probed and authenticated automation remains out of scope.

title: Permission picker treats Allow Once as Deny
description:
## Summary

After the fail-closed permission ordering fix, a user who selects the displayed second option, Allow Once, can still send the first option, Deny. Generic vim.ui.select providers may render numbered rows without interpreting a typed number as row selection.

## Reproduction

Session: claude/d0cb6393-4548-4533-937f-614160f5a2b5

1. Ask Claude to perform an operation requiring permission.
2. Deny the first request.
3. Ask Claude to retry and select displayed option 2, Allow Once.
4. Observe Claude receives User refused permission again.

The ACP trace advertised Deny as option 1 and Allow Once as option 2 on both requests.

## Expected

A deliberate Allow Once choice sends its exact ACP optionId. Rejecting, allowing, and cancelling must all be unambiguous regardless of the installed vim.ui provider.

## Actual

Typing the displayed option number can confirm the provider current row instead, so option 2 is interpreted as option 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The permission choice flow does not depend on provider-specific numbered-row key behavior.
2. Choosing Deny sends the deny optionId, and choosing Allow Once sends the allow optionId.
3. Invalid or dismissed choices cancel rather than approve.
4. Agent option labels and identifiers remain distinct and unmodified.
5. Scheduled UI handling and late-choice-after-disposal safety remain covered by headless tests.
close_reason: Replaced provider-dependent permission selection with explicit numbered input, preserving exact ACP option IDs. Added regression coverage for Claude's Deny/Allow Once options, invalid and dismissed input, distinct labels, scheduling, and disposal. Verification: 43 focused UI tests and 184 full MiniTest cases pass; installed Snacks input smoke returns typed 2; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Investigate diff edit approval UX
description:
## Context

After asking LouiseLM to create a file, the plugin opened a `louiselm-diff` buffer. The latest screenshot (`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0457_1920x1200_1786244259.png`) shows the target path, `--- original`, `+++ proposed`, and an otherwise empty buffer. No visible accept/reject/close actions or instructions are presented, and Neovim is in insert mode.

## Investigation

Determine the intended lifecycle for an agent-proposed file edit and whether this diff view is currently incomplete, incorrectly rendered, or intentionally only a review surface. Trace the permission/edit/diff flow and document how a user should:

- understand what changed;
- accept/apply the proposed edit;
- reject it;
- cancel or return to the conversation;
- handle an empty/new-file diff;
- recover if the diff buffer is closed or the proposed edit becomes stale.

Assess the UX from a first-time user perspective, including discoverability of keymaps/commands, mode choice, statusline/help text, and whether approval belongs in the diff view, a permission prompt, or both.

## Exit criteria

- Reproduce the flow with a deterministic test or documented local scenario.
- Identify the root cause of the empty/unactionable presentation, if it is a bug.
- State the intended user-facing contract and recommended minimal UX changes.
- Add implementation follow-up beads tasks if the investigation finds separate fixes.
- Add or update headless UI behavior coverage for the confirmed contract where practical.
close_reason: Added discoverable diff approval instructions and normal-mode focus; verified full test and quality gates.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Investigation complete. The diff controller already had buffer-local normal-mode mappings: a accepts, d/q reject. The screenshot was unfriendly because the review buffer provided no instructions and inherited insert mode from the chat prompt, making those mappings undiscoverable/unusable. The diff is a permission review; accept sends the ACP allow response and the agent performs the write. Added an explicit instruction line and return to normal mode on focus. Existing behavior tests plus the new render assertion pass; no separate apply bug was reproduced.

title: Restored chat crashes while rendering replayed history
description:
## Problem

Loading an existing ACP/Codex session works, but the chat UI crashes when replayed assistant history arrives. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:690` performs arithmetic on `view.transcript_tail`, which is nil for a newly attached restored session.

## Reproduction

1. Create a session with Codex ACP and exit Neovim.
2. Load the ACP session with `sessions:load_session(...)`.
3. Attach it to `Chat`.
4. Observe `vim.schedule callback ... chat/init.lua:690: attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Restored assistant history renders without an error.
- New-session streaming behavior remains unchanged.
- Add a focused regression test covering a replayed chunk on an attached restored session.
close_reason: Fixed restored assistant chunk rendering fallback and added regression coverage. Focused chat tests: 30 passed; full mini.test suite: 115 passed; stylua --check and lua-language-server diagnostics passed.

description: Reproduction A: from the repository root run nvim -u tests/minimal_init.lua, then execute :LouiselmChat (the reported spelling was :LouisLMChat). The chat buffer opens as '# default · session-1' but shows 'Error: ACP session/new failed: Invalid params' and an empty prompt.
