title: Inject AGENTS.md as an ACP resource_link on new session start
description:
## Problem Statement

Project instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, or an adapter's own convention like
`CLAUDE.md`) are currently discovered per-agent, by convention, outside the
protocol — each ACP agent binary decides for itself whether and when to read
one. Nothing at the louiselm/ACP layer surfaces "this project has a governing
instructions file" to whichever agent is on the other end of the session, so
adapters without their own convention never see it, and even adapters that do
have one only find it if the file happens to match their own naming/lookup
rules.

This surfaced from a live miss: an agent working in this repo executed
`bvr`/`br` triage without first reading `AGENTS.md`, violating its explicit
"prefer finishing in-progress work" rule, because nothing forced or even
hinted at loading the file before acting.

## Solution

On the first prompt of a new ACP session, if the project root contains an
`AGENTS.md` (or a configured equivalent), attach a `ContentBlock::ResourceLink`
(`{name, uri}`) pointing at it — not an `EmbeddedResource`/full-text block.
This is a near-zero-cost hint: the agent decides whether to fetch it via
`fs/read_text_file`. This is deliberately protocol-level and adapter-agnostic,
unlike each agent's private, per-implementation instruction-file convention.

Reuse the existing "attach hidden context to the first prompt of a new
session" injection pipeline being built for the Agent Skills catalog
(louiselm-c8v, under louiselm-cxh) rather than inventing a second one — same
new-session detection, same once-per-session consumption/no-double-send
semantics, same defer-across-slash-prompts behavior. The catalog is an
`EmbeddedResource`/text block; this is a `ResourceLink` — same delivery
lifecycle, different content-block variant.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. First accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, when `AGENTS.md` exists
   at the project root, includes exactly one `resource_link` content block
   naming it.
2. No resend on later turns of the same session; same no-double-send /
   accepted-request-id consumption semantics as the skill catalog injection.
3. Sessions without an `AGENTS.md` at the project root attach nothing extra.
4. Resumed/external sessions do not get a guessed/re-sent link (same rule as
   louiselm-c8v).
5. Configurable path/filename, not hardcoded to exactly `AGENTS.md`, so a repo
   using a different convention isn't excluded.
6. MiniTest/mock-ACP coverage asserts the resource_link is well-formed, sent
   exactly once, and absent when no file is present.

## Out of Scope

- Guaranteeing the agent actually reads the link (agent-side choice; ACP does
  not mandate honoring resource_link).
- Embedding the file's full content (that's the EmbeddedResource path,
  intentionally not used here — costs context on every session whether or not
  it's read).
- Any Claude-Code-specific or other single-adapter special-casing.

## Notes

Verified against the vendored `agent-client-protocol-schema` crate
(`src/v2/content.rs`): `ContentBlock` has `Text`, `Resource(EmbeddedResource)`,
and `ResourceLink(ResourceLink)` variants; ACP itself defines no
"auto-load project instructions" behavior — this task is what fills that gap
at the louiselm layer instead of relying on each adapter's own convention.
close_reason: Completed: lua/louiselm/instructions.lua (M.link) + wired through ui/chat/command.lua (configured_instructions) and ui/chat/init.lua (Chat.new/new_session/prompt_content) to attach an ACP resource_link on a brand-new session's first prompt, gated by config.context.instructions_file (default '' = off). Covered by tests/instructions_spec.lua, tests/ui/chat_spec.lua (queue/new_session/no-resend-on-attach), and an end-to-end tests/ui/command_spec.lua ACP-transport test. Full suite: 251/251 mini.test cases pass; stylua --check and lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning clean on all touched files. README documented.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Implementation note / deviation from the original issue text: shipped with
`context.instructions_file` defaulting to `""` (disabled), not `"AGENTS.md"`.

Reasoning: this repo's own project root always has an AGENTS.md, so a
default-enabled filename would have silently attached a resource_link to
every single chat session created anywhere in this codebase's test suite and
in real usage, changing ACP content-block shape by default for every existing
consumer with no opt-in. That mirrors the existing `skills.policy` precedent
(`native`, i.e. off, is the default; `inject` is opt-in). Users enable it
explicitly via `context = { instructions_file = "AGENTS.md" }` in `setup()`.

title: Multi-line tool titles break the markdown export's <sub> caption and inject fake ## sections
description:
A tool call whose title contains newlines — every multi-line shell command — breaks the markdown export's structure. The `` caption is emitted as a single concatenated string, so a multi-line title splits it across the document: the element is left unclosed for up to 150 lines, and every intervening line is emitted as raw markdown body text. Where that text contains `##` headings, the export gains fabricated sections indistinguishable from its own. ## Observed Real export from session `cae87c06-bd44-429f-823e-6b18a361129f`, produced by `:LouiselmToMarkdown` on build `cd37ab2` during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, 2026-08-20: `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-2-20260820-061038.md` (5543 lines, 680 KB, 120 tool calls). 12 of 120 `` captions span more than one line: ``` opened line 1262, closed line 1348 (span 87) opened line 2208, closed line 2352 (span 145) opened line 2825, closed line 2974 (span 150) opened line 3197, closed line 3208 (span 12) opened line 3698, closed line 3722 (span 25) opened line 5271, closed line 5407 (span 137) ... 6 more ``` Headings present in the export, counted by text: ``` 120 ## Tool <- real 41 ## Assistant <- real 14 ## User <- real 4 ## Observed <- fabricated 4 ## Symptoms <- fabricated 4 ## Root cause <- fabricated 4 ## Why it was not caught <- fabricated 4 ## Fix direction <- fabricated 4 ## Acceptance <- fabricated 4 ## Not covered <- fabricated ``` 28 fabricated `##` sections, all leaked out of `br create ... --description "$DESCRIPTION"` calls whose heredoc body became part of the tool title. A concrete block, at line 4434: ``` **ACTOR="${BR_ACTOR:-assistant}"; br comment add louiselm-euj --actor ... <- blank line, inside the element That is now two consecutive rounds finding it present and deliberately ... <- blank line
``` The `` opens on 4434 and closes on 4436, with document-level markdown in between. ## Symptoms - Rendered exports show a broken caption followed by loose body text where a one-line tool label was intended. - The document outline gains sections that were never in the conversation. - Any consumer that splits the export on `^## ` — which the format explicitly invites — mis-sections the document. ## Root cause `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:182-185`: ```lua "**" .. tostring(title) .. "** — " .. status .. "", ``` This is one element of the returned lines table, but `title` comes from `raw.title`, which for a Bash tool call is the literal command string and may contain newlines. `Chat:to_markdown` then runs the joined text through `split_lines`, so every embedded newline becomes a real line break inside what was supposed to be a single-line element. Nothing normalizes or escapes the title. `status` has the same exposure, though no observed payload puts a newline there. Not introduced by `14dbab6`, and that matters for triage: the previous format (`"## Tool: " .. title .. " (" .. status .. ")"`) had the identical flaw and would split the heading itself. `14dbab6` changed the shape of the breakage — an unclosed inline HTML element rather than a broken heading — and made the leaked text more prominent by collapsing the payload it sits next to. The bug is older than the commit the QA round was testing. ## Why it was not caught Every title in `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` is a short single-line literal ("Run tests", "tool-9"). The specs assert the caption's exact text with `markdown:find("**Run tests** — completed", 1, true)`, which is a substring search — it cannot notice that the surrounding element is unclosed, and it never sees a title that could break it. The fixtures were invented rather than captured, and the invented ones are all well-behaved. A single fixture carrying an embedded `\n` would have failed immediately. ## Fix direction Normalize the title (and status) before interpolation, in `render_entry`: collapse any run of whitespace containing a newline to a single space, so the caption is one line by construction. Truncation with an ellipsis past some width is worth considering alongside it — a 150-line shell command is not a useful caption at any length — but that is a separate judgement about presentation, and the correctness fix should not wait on it. Rejected: escaping newlines as `
`. It keeps the element well-formed but preserves a 150-line caption, which is not the intent of a `` label, and it puts raw HTML into a field that is already being interpolated into HTML. Rejected: moving the title inside the `
` payload. That discards the collapsed-block affordance `14dbab6` was added to provide. ## Acceptance - A regression test with a tool title containing `\n` (and ideally a `##` line, matching the real payload that exposed this) asserting the rendered caption occupies exactly one line and the export's `^## ` count equals the number of real blocks. - Re-exporting the session above yields 120 `## Tool`, 41 `## Assistant`, 14 `## User` and no other `##` headings. ## Not covered - Whether any other field interpolated into a single-line construct has the same exposure has not been audited; `status` is the obvious sibling. - The effect on the blog pipeline is unverified: `:lines: N-M` excerpt ranges are computed against this file's line numbers, so a 150-line caption makes ranges shift unpredictably between exports. QA cases 6-9 of this round have not been run yet.
close_reason: Fixed in a6484ea. render_entry interpolated raw.title straight into the single-line <sub> caption, so a multi-line shell command split the element across the document; title and status now go through single_line(), which collapses newline runs to a space and trims. Tests: 'keeps the caption on one line when the tool title spans several' (asserts every <sub> line ends with </sub> and that a '## Observed' inside the title does not become a section) and 'keeps the caption on one line when the tool status spans several'; both confirmed red before the fix, failing on the caption ending in '<<EOF'. Gates: mini.test 0 fails/0 notes, stylua clean on both changed files, lua-language-server no new warnings. Deviation from the filed acceptance criteria: truncation was considered and deliberately not implemented -- a 150-line command is still a poor caption even when it is one line, but that is a presentation decision, filed thinking only, not a correctness gap. Re-export verification by the tester is still pending.

title: State sole copyright and retained relicensing right in CONTRIBUTING
description:
Amend `CONTRIBUTING.md` to state the copyright and relicensing position plainly.

The existing no-merge policy already explains *why* outside code is not merged (review burden, product coherence). This adds the licensing consequence of that policy, which is currently unstated.

## Content to add

A short factual paragraph, not a threat and not a legal wall of text:

- Copyright in LouiseLM is held solely by the maintainer.
- No outside code is merged, so no CLA is required and none will be asked for.
- The maintainer retains the right to license future versions under different terms.

## Why stated rather than silent

Sole ownership is already inferable in ten seconds from the public no-merge policy, so concealment buys no real surprise. The community LouiseLM wants — people bringing workflows and judgment over years — punishes ambush hardest and forgives disclosed risk easily. A pre-announced possibility converts an eventual relicense from betrayal into a term everyone accepted going in.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` states all three points above.
- The tone matches the existing document: explicit about an unusual constraint, so nobody wastes effort or gets hurt feelings.
- Nothing elsewhere in the repo contradicts it by implying a perpetual open-source guarantee.

title: Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently injects one global skill index into every session, including adapters such as Codex and Claude that already provide native Agent Skills support. This exposes an implementation marker in chat, wastes context, can send a skill twice, and leaves users unable to understand which component discovers or invokes a skill.

## Solution

Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles. Global skill paths remain shared, the default policy is `native`, and an agent may override only `skills.policy` with `native`, `inject`, or `off`. Native mode delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter. Inject mode provides a hidden, bounded Agent Skills catalog and attaches a selected full SKILL.md only once per activation. Off disables LouiseLM skill automation and the picker. Never infer or switch policy at runtime.

## User Stories

1. As a Codex or Claude user, I want native skills used without LouiseLM reinjecting them, so that skills are not duplicated.
2. As a custom-adapter user, I want to opt one agent into injected discovery, so that natural-language skill matching still works.
3. As a user, I want a picker that invokes a known local skill safely in both native and injected profiles, so that explicit activation is predictable.
4. As a user, I want skill context hidden before submission but inspectable afterward, so that chat stays clean without concealing what was sent.
5. As a skill author, I want malformed, shadowed, explicit-only, truncated, or inaccessible skills diagnosed clearly, so that configuration failures are understandable.
6. As a user configuring an unfamiliar ACP adapter, I want documentation explaining Agent Skills, ACP transport, host responsibilities, and filesystem assumptions, so that I can choose the correct policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Global `skills.policy` defaults to `native`; agent definitions may override only the policy, while paths remain global and session-static.
2. `native` sends no automatic catalog or skill body. Picker activation resolves against the adapter's latest advertised command list and sends exactly one advertised command plus task.
3. `inject` sends one hidden catalog only on the first accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, then sends a selected complete SKILL.md once per deliberate activation. It never falls back to native or reinjects after uncertain accepted requests.
4. `off` sends no skill automation and disables the skill picker without intercepting user-authored slash commands.
5. The old `full_content` setting and dormant automatic-native-fallback API are removed with clear migration errors and documentation.
6. Agent Skills core metadata is parsed with `lyaml` and semantically validated; Codex and Claude invocation-control extensions are recognized without treating them as ACP requirements.
7. Missing `lyaml` blocks injected sessions and local native picker/validation, but does not block native sessions themselves or off sessions.
8. The injected catalog uses the agreed Agent Skills XML shape, fixed behavioral preamble, XML escaping, and an 8,000-byte UTF-8-safe total budget with deterministic diagnostics.
9. Submitted prompt contexts are represented as one closed Neovim fold containing exact sent content in order; automatic hidden catalog text never appears as a pre-send marker.
10. README, generated configuration help/annotations, checkhealth, and migration guidance explain policy selection, no-double-send behavior, dependency installation, trust/path rules, filesystem limits, and live-only fold persistence.
11. Automated tests cover configuration, discovery, YAML, invocation metadata, native command correlation, injection lifecycle, slash deferral, failures/cancellation, no-double-send invariants, and context folds. Installed Codex/Claude checks remain documented manual smoke tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Agent Skills defines the skill format; ACP transports prompts and command updates; LouiseLM is the host responsible for policy and injected discovery.
- Explicit-only wins when `disable-model-invocation: true` or OpenAI's `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` is present. Such skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs.
- Root order defines duplicate precedence; path handling is deterministic, symlink-aware, and diagnostic without adding a trust database.
- The 8,000-byte mechanism intentionally mimics Codex's conservative fallback behavior; it is not part of ACP or the Agent Skills specification.
- Use native Neovim folds and existing context transport. Do not introduce a generic fold framework.

## Testing Notes

Use MiniTest for module behavior and a mock ACP agent for command updates and prompt transport. Test public behavior and exact no-double-send invariants. Do not require authenticated live adapters in automated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Runtime policy switching or inference.
- A general UI for every ACP advertised command.
- A LouiseLM ACP filesystem service.
- Recursive embedding of skill resources.
- Persistent transcript reconstruction.
- Automatic dependency installation.
- Generic adapter-native skill implementation.
- Tool-call fold rendering; track that as a separate design question.

title: Diagnose installed lyaml outside Neovim search paths
description:
## Problem

Local skill discovery reports:

```
louiselm: lyaml is required for local skill discovery; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml`
```

However, LuaRocks confirms that lyaml is already installed for Lua 5.1. The actual failure is that the active Neovim process does not search the LuaRocks tree, so the message sends the user toward an installation command that will not fix the search-path mismatch.

## Reproduction evidence

- `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 show lyaml` succeeds with lyaml 6.2.9-2 under `$HOME/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/luarocks`.
- Neovim 0.12.2 embeds LuaJIT 2.1.
- In `nvim --headless -u NONE`, `pcall(require, "lyaml")` returns `module 'lyaml' not found`.
- Neovim's `package.path` and `package.cpath` contain system paths, but not the asdf LuaRocks share/lib paths reported by `luarocks path --lua-version 5.1`.

## Expected behavior

When lyaml cannot be loaded, LouiseLM should preserve enough of the loader failure to distinguish an absent installation from an installed-but-unreachable LuaRocks tree (and from native module load failures), then give a corrective action that matches the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user-facing/checkhealth diagnostic distinguishes at least package-not-found/search-path mismatch from a native loader failure instead of always saying to install lyaml.
2. Documentation gives a supported way to make a Lua 5.1 LuaRocks tree visible to Neovim, including non-system/asdf installs.
3. Tests cover the generic `require("lyaml")` failure mapping without depending on a real LuaRocks installation.
4. Diagnostics do not expose unrelated environment values or sensitive data.
close_reason: Shortened interactive lyaml failures to point at checkhealth, added detailed persistent zsh/asdf guidance to health and README, and covered both surfaces. Verified 181 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.

title: Resumed-session export silently drops nested/subagent tool calls
description:
`:LouiselmResume`'s replay of a prior ACP session silently drops nested/child
tool calls (a tool call made *by* a Task subagent, i.e. one carrying a
`parentToolUseId`), while still replaying the parent Task call's own summary
text. Anyone exporting a resumed session — including the blog publishing
pipeline, which exports whatever the agent replays on `session/load` — gets a
transcript that is missing subagent-internal tool-call detail, with no error
or signal that anything is missing.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features
(`4e4a58b`, `674939b`), case 4 ("resumed-session export vs live export"),
session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, 2026-08-18.

Prompt that produced the nested call (case 1 of the same round):
"Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on
the absolute path: `wc -l .../transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to
launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: 'List the
top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated
line.' (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found."

Original live export, captured right after that turn ended:
`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` (repo root at the time). Contains 3
tool-call blocks — Bash (`wc -l`), Task (`List top-level directories`), and a
nested Bash call made by the Task subagent:
```
toolCallId = "toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr"
parentToolUseId = "toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"  (the Task call)
title = "ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"
rawOutput = "android,assets,blog,capture-service,configured,lua,scripts,tests"
status = "completed"
```

Resumed export (`:LouiselmResume` on the same session, immediate
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, no other prompt sent first):
same acp session id (session/load reconnects rather than creating a new
session). Contains the parent `## Tool: List top-level directories
(completed)` block with its rawOutput summary intact, but grepping the full
573KB resumed export for the toolCallId `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr`, the
literal command text `paste -sd`, and `xargs -n1 basename` finds zero
tool-call blocks — those strings appear exactly once, incidentally, inside
unrelated later text content (a grep-output dump quoted in a much later
turn), not as a `## Tool:` entry.

Raw jsonrpc log:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260818-150022-1160867-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(818 lines). The nested `tool_call` event for
`toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` appears exactly once, at line 19, during the
original live turn:
```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384","update":{"_meta":{"claudeCode":{"toolName":"Bash","parentToolUseId":"toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"}},"toolCallId":"toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr","sessionUpdate":"tool_call","rawInput":{"command":"ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"},"status":"pending", ...}}}
```
No second occurrence appears later in the log during the replay burst
triggered by `session/load` — the agent process itself never re-emits this
event on replay.

Everything else about the resumed export checked out clean: 65 of the 66
total tool calls in the session (by then spanning many turns) present and in
correct relative order, and the case-1 `## User` block matches the typed
prompt verbatim. Only this one nested call is missing.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a resumed-session export (or a blog post built from one) that
  looks complete — full assistant text, the parent Task call's own summary —
  but is silently missing the detail of what the subagent actually did
  internally.
- System reports: nothing. No error, warning, or count mismatch anywhere;
  `Chat:to_markdown` and `create-blog.sh` both report success normally.

## Root cause

Unknown, and outside this repo (`louiselm.nvim`). `louiselm`'s own
`Transcript:record`/`Transcript.render` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua)
only records whatever `session/update` events it receives over ACP — the
live stream sent the nested tool_call event and louiselm recorded it
correctly (see the original export above); on replay, the same event simply
never arrives, so there is nothing to fix on this side.

Hypothesis (unverified): `claude-agent-acp`
(`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`, a sibling project) or the underlying
Claude Code SDK reconstructs the Task/subagent call tree differently when
replaying a resumed session's history than when streaming it live — possibly
only replaying top-level tool calls and treating subagent-internal calls as
already-summarized by the parent's own output. Nothing in this investigation
confirms which layer (adapter vs. upstream SDK) is responsible; that needs a
look at the adapter/SDK's own session/load implementation, not louiselm's.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua` and
`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` exercise `Transcript` against synthetic,
hand-built event fixtures for both the live and "loaded" replay paths — no
fixture in the suite includes a nested/subagent tool call in a replay
scenario, because nobody had a real payload to model one on. This QA round
was the first time a resumed session containing a Task-subagent call was
actually exported and diffed against its own live-captured original.

## Fix direction

Not in this repo. If the root cause is confirmed to be in
`claude-agent-acp`, the fix belongs there (ensure `session/load` replay
re-emits every historical `tool_call`/`tool_call_update`, including nested
ones with `parentToolUseId` set, not just top-level calls). If it turns out
to be inherent to how the upstream Claude Code SDK exposes subagent history
on resume, this may not be fixable without a scope change to what
`session/load` guarantees — in which case the practical mitigation is
documentation: warn blog-pipeline users that `create-blog.sh` on a resumed
session may omit subagent-internal tool-call detail, and recommend exporting
live when that detail matters.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in whichever repo owns the fix: replay a session
  containing a Task call with a nested tool call, and assert the replayed
  event stream includes the nested `tool_call`/`tool_call_update` events,
  not just the parent's.
- Re-run this round's case 4 comparison
  (`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` vs. a fresh `:LouiselmResume` +
  immediate `:LouiselmToMarkdown` export of the same session) and confirm
  `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` (or an equivalent nested call in a new
  repro) is present in the resumed export.

## Not covered

- Which of `claude-agent-acp` vs. the upstream Claude Code SDK is actually
  responsible — unverified, needs investigation in that repo, not this one.
- Whether the same gap exists for other nested-call shapes (e.g. a tool call
  made by a tool call, rather than by a Task subagent specifically) — only
  one nested-call example existed in the session under test.
- Whether `create-blog.sh` (case 5, not yet run at time of filing) actually
  reproduces the same gap end-to-end through the headless path — this bug is
  filed from the interactive `:LouiselmResume` path only; case 5 should
  re-check this once it runs.
close_reason: Fixed in owner repo /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp commit 041da5b; exact historical session headless export restores the missing nested tool call and parent attribution; full owner-repo gates pass.

title: stylua --check . fails on a clean tree because blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua is unformatted
description:
`stylua --check .` — the formatter gate AGENTS.md section 4 declares, unscoped
and whole-repo — exits 1 on a clean checkout of `main`. It has done so since
`674939b` (2026-08-18). Every contributor and every CI run that enforces the
documented gate fails on an untouched tree, which trains people to ignore the
gate.

## Observed

Found during setup of the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, on a clean tree at
`cd37ab2` (2026-08-20), before any case was run.

```
$ git status --porcelain
$ stylua --check .; echo "exit=$?"
Diff in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua:
26       |-vim.cmd('packadd nvim.tohtml')
    26   |+vim.cmd("packadd nvim.tohtml")
...
39       |-	io.stderr:write('tohtml-driver: ' .. msg .. '\n')
    39   |+  io.stderr:write("tohtml-driver: " .. msg .. "\n")
...
exit=1
```

`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is the only file that differs; every file under
`lua/` and `tests/` is clean.

## Symptoms

- `stylua --check .`, copied verbatim from AGENTS.md section 4, exits 1 with no
  local changes.
- The reported diff is entirely in private blog tooling, not in plugin code, so
  the failure looks unrelated to whatever the contributor is actually doing.

## Root cause

`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` was authored with tab indentation and
single-quoted strings, matching the shell scripts it sits beside rather than
`.stylua.toml` (`indent_type = "Spaces"`, `indent_width = 2`,
`quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`). It was added by `674939b` and has never
been run through StyLua. Concretely: lines 26, 32, 39-40, 43, 45-46, 49, 51-52,
54, 59-60, 64-91, 93, 96.

## Why it was not caught

Two gaps, both real:

- CI does not yet enforce the gates (AGENTS.md section 4: "CI must enforce all
  gates once their configuration/harness exists"), so nothing runs
  `stylua --check .` except a human choosing to.
- The QA round that had `674939b` in scope (`louiselm-vj0`) exercised the blog
  pipeline's behaviour end to end and never ran the formatter gate. Behavioural
  QA does not substitute for the gate, and the round plan did not list it.

## Fix direction

Two defensible options; this is a decision, not a lookup.

1. Format the file: `stylua blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua`. Narrowest, keeps
   the gate's whole-repo scope honest. Cost: this one Lua file stops matching
   the tab-indented shell scripts it lives with.
2. Add a `.styluaignore` for `blog/`, on the argument already made in
   `blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`'s header — that `AGENTS.md` governs
   `lua/`, not private blog tooling. Cost: makes the exclusion explicit and
   permanent, and future Lua under `blog/` is then unformatted by policy.

Rejected: narrowing the documented gate command to `stylua --check lua/ tests/`.
That silently shrinks a rule stated as whole-repo, and the next Lua file added
outside those two directories inherits the same invisible hole.

## Acceptance

- `stylua --check .` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- Whichever option is taken is recorded where the next person looks: either the
  file is formatted, or `.styluaignore` exists with a comment saying why.

## Not covered

- `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`, the other AGENTS.md
  gate, was not run during this round's setup — its status on a clean tree is
  unverified.
- Deferred deliberately: not fixed during the QA round, because the round's
  case 0 records the clean-tree gate result and editing the tree mid-round
  invalidates that premise. Fix after the round closes.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
The 'Not covered' item is now resolved, and it makes this worse than filed: blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua fails BOTH documented AGENTS.md section 4 gates, not just StyLua.

'lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning' on a clean tree at cd37ab2 reports 'Diagnosis complete, 9 problems found', all 9 in that one file, all 'Undefined global vim (undefined-global)' -- the file is a headless Neovim driver script, so it uses the vim global but sits outside whatever library/workspace config covers lua/ and tests/.

Verified during this round by running the gate before and after an unrelated fix: 11 problems in 2 files with a temporary vim.gsplit call in a test, 9 problems in 1 file once that was removed. Every file under lua/ and tests/ is clean.

This strengthens fix option 2 (a .styluaignore-style exclusion for blog/): whatever is decided, it should cover both gates, since a fix that only silences StyLua leaves the same file failing lua-language-server. Option 1 (format the file) does not address the undefined-global warnings at all -- those need either a workspace/library setting for blog/ or an exclusion.

title: Stack LouieLM transcript content in chronological order
description:
## Problem

In the latest screenshot of a LouieLM session, the transcript content feels split by type: the conversation text appears above while tool activity/status lines are grouped at the bottom near the prompt. This makes the sequence of the session awkward to follow.

## Desired behavior

Render each printed item in one chronological vertical stack, including model text, user text, tool calls, tool results, and status messages. New items should appear after the preceding item in the same transcript flow, with the composer/input area remaining at the bottom.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Model text, user text, tool activity, tool results, and status messages appear in a single chronological transcript order.
2. Tool output is positioned next to or directly after the event that produced it rather than in a separate bottom group.
3. The input/composer remains clearly separated from transcript history at the bottom.
4. Existing session header and chat behavior remain unchanged.

Source report: /tmp/nvim-wtu.md
close_reason: Reset streamed response cursor after tool and error transcript items so interleaved chat content remains chronological; added regression coverage. Verified focused and full mini.test suites, StyLua, LuaLS, and git diff --check.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown crashes with uncaught E482 instead of a clean write error
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` crashes with an uncaught Lua/Vimscript error instead of
the clean "could not write markdown file: ..." message when the destination's
parent directory does not exist.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b (blog publishing pipeline) and 4e4a58b
(session transcript export), case 2.2/2.3 in QA_REVIEW.md. User ran
`:LouiselmToMarkdown`, typed `~/tmp/qa-export.md` (nonexistent dir):

```
louiselm markdown path (blank for default): ~/tmp/qa-export.md
Lua :command callback: Vim:E482
: Can't open file ~/tmp/qa-export.md for writing: no such file or directory
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'writefile'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561: in function 'to_markdown'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:276: in function 'on_confirm'
        ...installs/neovim/0.12.2/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/ui.lua:114: in function 'input'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:272: in function <.../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266>
```

Reproduced identically with the absolute path `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md`
(missing dir), ruling out `~`-expansion as the sole cause — the real trigger
is any nonexistent parent directory.

## Symptoms

- User sees a raw `E482` Lua stack trace in `:messages`, not a `louiselm:`
  notification.
- The chat UI's own error path (`report_error`) never fires for this failure.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561`:

```lua
if nvim.fn.writefile(split_lines(markdown), destination) ~= 0 then
  return nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. destination
end
```

This assumes `writefile()` reports failure via a nonzero return. In Neovim,
when the destination cannot be opened at all (missing parent directory, no
permission), `writefile()` throws `E482` as a Lua error instead of returning
a value — so the `~= 0` check is dead code for this failure mode and the
error propagates uncaught through `Chat:to_markdown` ->
`command.lua:276 on_confirm` -> `vim.ui.input`.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers the success path, "no chat
session", "not attached", and "disposed" errors, but has no case where
`writefile` itself fails (e.g. destination inside a nonexistent directory).
The suite never exercises the real `writefile()` call against an unwritable
path.

## Fix direction

Wrap the `writefile` call in `pcall` in `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1561) so
any thrown error is caught and converted into the existing
`"could not write markdown file: " .. destination` return.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua that calls
  `to_markdown` with a path inside a nonexistent directory and asserts a
  clean `(nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. path)` return with no
  thrown error.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown` against a missing directory shows
  a `louiselm: could not write markdown file: ...` notification, no stack
  trace in `:messages`.

## Not covered

`~` is not expanded by `vim.fn.writefile` either (a second, separate
usability issue: paths starting with `~` will still fail even inside an
existing directory tree, just with a clean error now instead of a crash).
Not filing separately since the pcall fix already turns it into the correct
clean-error path; only worth a follow-up if users expect `~` to expand.
close_reason: Fixed in 6167df0. Root cause: nvim.fn.writefile throws E482 (Lua error) instead of returning nonzero when the destination directory doesn't exist, so Chat:to_markdown's `~= 0` check never caught the failure. Fix: wrapped the writefile call in pcall (init.lua:1561), converting any thrown error into the existing clean 'could not write markdown file: ...' return. Tests: added 'reports a clean error instead of crashing when the destination directory does not exist' to tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua -- failed with the exact E482 traceback before the fix, passes after. Gates: full mini.test suite (235/235 cases) and stylua --check on both changed files pass. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria.

title: Open every UI selector outside insert mode
description:
## Problem

Commit 1eb309a fixed permission selection by leaving insert mode immediately before vim.ui.select. That diagnosis is correct: Chat:attach enters insert mode, and list-focused select providers can otherwise receive the wrong mode and confirm or edit the wrong picker state.

The same bug remains in session configuration. Chat:attach schedules open_session_options after entering insert mode, while both the options overview and its nested model/value picker call vim.ui.select without normalizing mode. This affects the automatic first-session overview and can also affect :LouiselmSessionOptions when invoked from an insert-mode mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a ready session that advertises a model or boolean configuration option.
2. Let Chat:attach focus the prompt and enter insert mode.
3. Wait for the scheduled initial options overview, or invoke :LouiselmSessionOptions from an insert-mode mapping.
4. Observe that vim.ui.select is called while the inherited mode is insert; with a list-focused provider, navigation or confirmation targets the wrong picker state.
5. Select an option such as Model and observe the nested value picker has the same unnormalized boundary.

## Investigation

There are 12 vim.ui.select call sites across chat, context, and diff UI. In addition to session options, selectors that are asynchronous, nested, or exposed through public Chat methods can inherit insert mode: resumed-session selection, remembered-permission selection and confirmation, session switch/close, agent selection, and file/skill context selection. The permission picker is now protected. The diff-review selector is currently protected indirectly because the focused diff buffer exits insert mode before its normal-mode actions run.

## Scope

- Normalize mode at the narrowest shared LouiseLM selection boundary immediately before opening every vim.ui.select picker.
- Cover both stages of the session-options flow, especially the model/value picker opened by :LouiselmSessionOptions and the automatic picker scheduled by Chat:attach.
- Migrate or audit every raw vim.ui.select call in lua/louiselm/ui so no insert-mode-sensitive sibling remains.
- Preserve provider ownership of picker layout and interaction; do not detect or configure Snacks or another provider.
- Preserve selection values, cancellation behavior, asynchronous scheduling, and disposal guards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The automatically opened session-options overview is invoked outside insert mode after Chat:attach starts the prompt in insert mode.
2. The nested model/boolean value picker is also invoked outside insert mode.
3. Every LouiseLM vim.ui.select call either uses the shared normalization boundary or has a tested invariant proving insert mode cannot reach it.
4. The existing permission-picker mode regression remains green, and diff review remains in normal mode.
5. Headless behavioral tests cover the session-options regression and at least one representative shared/public or asynchronous selector path without relying on provider internals.
6. The focused UI tests, full MiniTest suite, StyLua check, and lua-language-server check pass.
close_reason: Normalized all 12 vim.ui.select call sites through one normal-mode picker boundary. Added red-green regressions for automatic/nested session options and file context selection. Verification: focused chat 44/44, context 5/5, diff 5/5; full MiniTest 185/185; StyLua and LuaLS passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Keep the chat header compact instead of dumping session metadata
description:
## Problem

The chat buffer header expands into a long Markdown heading containing every session option and context field. At normal split widths it wraps across visual rows, dominates the top of the conversation, and is difficult to scan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session whose agent reports several configuration options plus context or cost telemetry.
2. Display the chat in a typical narrow vertical split.
3. Observe that the level-one Markdown heading includes all metadata and wraps across multiple visual rows.

## Observed

A Codex session currently renders a heading such as:

`# codex · session-1 · ready · Mode=agent-full-access · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off · context=62585/258400 (24% normal) · Your turn`

The screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png` shows this heading wrapping in the chat split.

## Expected

The transcript heading remains a compact, stable summary of session identity and current turn state, for example `# codex · session-1 · ready · Your turn`. Detailed configuration and telemetry remain discoverable through session options or a separate secondary status surface instead of being concatenated into an unbounded Markdown heading.

## Likely Root Cause

`session_summary()` appends every `config_options` entry plus context and cost telemetry, and `session_header()` uses the complete summary as the level-one Markdown heading. The heading length therefore scales with agent capabilities and enabled metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level-one chat heading contains only concise session identity/lifecycle/turn information and stays readable at a typical vertical split width.
2. Static/default fields such as mode, collaboration mode, model, reasoning effort, and fast mode are not dumped into the transcript heading.
3. Detailed configuration remains accessible through the existing session-options flow or another clearly defined secondary surface; do not silently remove the ability to inspect or change supported options.
4. Useful dynamic telemetry such as context pressure or cost, if retained in the UI, is presented outside the primary Markdown heading and does not make that heading grow without bound.
5. Header updates for state changes, renamed sessions, loaded sessions, and turn transitions continue to work.
6. Add or update headless UI behavior tests using a session with several config options and context telemetry. Assert the compact buffer heading and continued access to configuration; use a manual narrow-split smoke check for wrapping rather than a pixel assertion.

## Scope

- In scope: chat header/status presentation and its behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP session metadata, removing configuration controls, or redesigning the rest of the transcript.
close_reason: Split compact session identity from the detailed switcher summary so chat headings contain only name/agent/id/lifecycle/turn while options and telemetry remain accessible. Verification: focused chat suite 27/27 passed; full mini.test suite 112/112 passed; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; 48-column headless smoke passed; git diff --check passed.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown prompts for a path before validating an explicit session id
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown <session_id>` prompts for a destination path before
checking whether `<session_id>` is actually attached, so an invalid id wastes
a full path-entry interaction before failing.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b/4e4a58b, case 2.4 in QA_REVIEW.md. User
ran `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id`, was shown the
"louiselm markdown path (blank for default):" prompt, typed a path, and only
then got the `louiselm: session is not attached` error. Expected (and every
other id-consuming failure in this command family gives) an immediate error
with no interactive prompt in between.

## Symptoms

- User types and confirms a file path for an export that was never going to
  happen.
- No data loss or crash — the eventual error message is correct — but the
  ordering is surprising and wastes an interaction.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266-282`:

```lua
nvim.api.nvim_create_user_command("LouiselmToMarkdown", function(arguments)
  ...
  local session_id = arguments.args ~= "" and arguments.args or nil
  nvim.ui.input({ prompt = "louiselm markdown path (blank for default): " }, function(path)
    ...
    local written_path, write_error = chat:to_markdown(session_id, path ~= "" and path or nil)
    ...
```

The session-id validity check lives inside `Chat:to_markdown`
(`init.lua:1553-1557`), which only runs after `vim.ui.input`'s callback
fires. `command.lua` has no way to check `session_id` validity up front
without reaching into `Chat`'s private `self.views` table.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers "not attached" at the
`Chat:to_markdown` level directly (bypassing the command layer), and
`tests/ui/command_spec.lua` stubs `vim.ui.input` so it never observes prompt
ordering relative to session validation. No test exercises the command's
real `vim.ui.input` flow with a bad session id end to end.

## Fix direction

Add a small public predicate, e.g. `Chat:is_attached(session_id)` (mirroring
the existing inline check in `Chat:switch`, init.lua:1444-1461), and have
`LouiselmToMarkdown` call it before opening the `vim.ui.input` prompt when an
explicit session id was given, reporting the error immediately instead.

Deliberately not fixing in the same pass as louiselm-dim, to keep that fix's
batch to the one crash bug; this is UX ordering, not a crash.

## Acceptance

- A test (likely in tests/ui/command_spec.lua, alongside its existing
  `vim.ui.input` stub) asserting that `:LouiselmToMarkdown <bad-id>` reports
  "session is not attached" without ever invoking the input prompt.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id` shows the error
  immediately, no path prompt.

## Not covered

Whether other future id-taking commands should share this predicate — only
`LouiselmToMarkdown` takes a raw typed session id today.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Reconfirmed on build cd37ab2 during the QA round covering ec19281..HEAD (2026-08-20). ':LouiselmToMarkdown nosuchsession' still prompts for a destination path before rejecting the unknown session id. Unchanged from the louiselm-vj0 round, where it was also reconfirmed and deferred.

That is now two consecutive rounds finding it present and deliberately not fixing it. Worth deciding rather than re-testing: either fix the ordering (validate the session id before calling vim.ui.input) or downgrade to wontfix, so a third round does not spend a step re-establishing a known state.

title: Write the example workflow document under docs/
description:
Write the maintainer's own workflow loop as an explicitly non-binding example document, at a `docs/` path.

This is the loop actually run today: **grill-me** (an idea gets direct attention and is interrogated one question at a time) → **to-beads** (the agreed plan becomes beads work items at the right abstraction level) → **sessions** (tasks get executed, automated or not) → **qa-review** (the maintainer manually tests what was just committed, and a defect found routes to `to-beads-bug`).

## Why this document exists

Two reasons, and both matter:

1. Other people, and other agents, may invent entirely different loops. Writing this one down as an *example* rather than a rule is what makes that possible without it reading as deviation from a contract.
2. louiselm intends to eventually ship this loop as an example **workflow config** — the maintainer's standing goal is that their workflow becomes expressible as configuration rather than convention. This document is the first draft of that spec. When the workflow-engine issues are picked up, this is what they implement against, rather than the loop being reconstructed from memory.

## What to write

Descriptive voice, not imperative — this describes what one person does, it does not instruct the reader. It must self-identify as a non-binding example in its opening, because the reader may arrive here without having read the link text in `AGENTS.md`.

Cover: what triggers each stage, what each stage hands to the next, and what "skill chaining" means here (one skill's output is designed to trigger another — grill-me ends by invoking to-beads; a qa-review defect invokes to-beads-bug).

Be honest about the known gap: a qa-review round can surface a *process* finding rather than a code bug, and there is currently no formalized route for that. It survives only by the maintainer noticing and calling for a grill-me session.

## Placement

A `docs/` path, not repo root. A root-level uppercase filename reads as law regardless of any disclaimer inside it, and that misreading is the specific thing this document must avoid. Do not create additional structure under `docs/` beyond what this one file needs.

## Acceptance criteria

- The document exists under `docs/` and declares itself a non-binding example within its opening lines.
- Each stage of the loop is described with its trigger and its handoff to the next stage.
- The unresolved process-finding gap is stated rather than papered over.
- It is written so that a future workflow-config implementation could use it as a starting spec, without committing to a config schema that does not exist yet.
- Voice is descriptive throughout; it never instructs the reader to adopt the loop.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: Chat buffer filetype=markdown lets image.nvim re-scan the whole transcript on every keystroke
description:
Typing in the louiselm chat buffer's prompt line is noticeably laggy, at rest
-- not during active LLM response streaming. Reported by the user mid-session
while typing with no chunks arriving.

## Observed

Session claude/6a76322f-4f96-430b-93f3-578808c4692c, 2026-08-20, connected
directly to the user's live `nvim --embed` instance over RPC
(`/run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0`) to inspect real state instead of guessing.

Ruled out with direct measurement, in order:
- `render-markdown.nvim` (installed in dotfiles) is not loaded at all:
  `luaeval('tostring(package.loaded["render-markdown"] ~= nil)')` -> `false`.
- Buffer size/decoration overhead is trivial: the chat buffer (bufnr 12,
  `louiselm://session-1`, filetype `markdown`) was 714 lines / 121121 bytes,
  with only 7 extmarks total (all in louiselm's own `louiselm.chat.header`
  namespace). Treesitter highlighter was active but on a buffer this small
  that's not a plausible lag source.
- System load: `uptime` showed load average 0.60/0.52/0.32 on a 16-core
  machine, `free -h` showed 20Gi available of 27Gi, 0B swap used. Not resource
  contention.
- No LSP clients attached to the chat buffer:
  `vim.lsp.get_clients({bufnr=12})` returned empty.

What IS confirmed present:
`nvim --server /run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0 --remote-expr
"luaeval('table.concat(vim.tbl_map(function(a) return a.event .. \"|\" ..
(a.group_name or \"-\") .. \"|\" .. (a.pattern or \"*\") .. \"|\" ..
tostring(a.buflocal) end,
vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event={\"InsertCharPre\",\"TextChangedI\",\"CursorMovedI\"}})),
\"\\n\")')"` listed, among 12 global autocmds on those three events:

  TextChangedI|image.nvim|*|false

A global (non-buffer-local, pattern `*`) TextChangedI autocmd owned by
image.nvim.

## Symptoms

- User sees: typing in the chat prompt feels unresponsive, specifically
  while it is their turn to type (no active stream).
- System reports: nothing -- no error, no warning. Silent per-keystroke cost.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366` sets the chat buffer's `filetype` to the
literal `"markdown"`:

    nvim.api.nvim_set_option_value("filetype", "markdown", { buf = buffer })

`~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/image.nvim/lua/image/integrations/markdown.lua`
registers image.nvim's markdown integration for `filetypes = { "markdown",
"vimwiki" }` (see `default_options.filetypes` in that file, wired up via
`document.create_document_integration`). That integration's
`query_buffer_images` function runs on every `TextChangedI` event: it calls
`vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf, "markdown")`, `parser:parse(true)`, and then
walks the full `markdown_inline` tree with two treesitter queries
(`(image (link_destination) @url) @image` and the shortcut-link variant),
looking for markdown image syntax to render inline in the terminal.

Because the chat buffer's filetype is the real `"markdown"`, image.nvim
cannot distinguish it from an actual markdown file the user is editing. It
therefore re-parses and re-queries the buffer's entire inline tree on every
character typed in insert mode, searching for images that don't exist and
never will in a live chat transcript -- pure, unconditional, per-keystroke
waste, scaling with growing transcript length as a session goes on.

`lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27` has the identical pattern
(`nvim.bo[buffer].filetype = "markdown"`) on a second buffer, but that buffer
is short-lived and not continuously growing/streamed like the chat buffer, so
it is noted here as the same root-cause class but not fixed by this bead.

## Why it was not caught

No test in the suite exercises interactive typing latency in the chat
buffer, or asserts anything about which global autocmds/integrations attach
to it. This class of defect -- a buffer silently opting into a third party's
filetype-keyed behavior it never intended to invite -- has no automated
signature; it only surfaces as felt input lag during real interactive use,
which is exactly how it was found here (user report, not a failing test).

## Fix direction

Give the chat buffer a distinct filetype (e.g. `"louiselm-chat"`) instead of
the real `"markdown"`, so filetype-keyed third-party integrations (image.nvim
today, anything else keyed on `ft=markdown` later) do not attach to it at
all, then explicitly re-attach markdown treesitter highlighting via
`vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")` (which takes the language
explicitly and is decoupled from `filetype`), so syntax highlighting is
preserved.

Rejected: asking image.nvim to opt out per-buffer instead. Would require
depending on that specific plugin's own opt-out mechanism (if any), and would
not protect against the next filetype=markdown-keyed plugin the user's config
gains later. Fixing the buffer's own identity is the narrower, more durable
fix and is entirely within this repo's control.

## Acceptance

- `nvim_get_autocmds({event={"TextChangedI","InsertCharPre","CursorMovedI"}})`
  filtered to ones matching the chat buffer's new filetype returns none from
  image.nvim (or any other third-party ft=markdown integration).
- The chat buffer still renders with markdown treesitter highlighting
  (verified via `vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[bufnr] ~= nil` after
  `Chat.new():open()`/equivalent).
- No existing test in `tests/` asserts the chat buffer's filetype is the
  literal string `"markdown"` (confirmed absent before this fix; grep
  `tests/` for `filetype.*chat\|chat.*markdown` stays empty after too).

## Not covered

- `lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27`'s identical pattern is not fixed
  here -- noted as the same root-cause class, lower priority given that
  buffer's short-lived usage pattern, left for a separate bead if it proves
  to matter in practice.
- Whether other globally-registered filetype=markdown integrations besides
  image.nvim (render-markdown.nvim, markdown linters, etc.) were also
  incidentally attaching -- render-markdown.nvim was directly confirmed not
  loaded in this session, but was not re-checked after the fix; not every
  possible third-party integration in the user's config was enumerated.
close_reason: Fixed: chat buffer filetype changed from the literal "markdown" to "louiselm-chat" (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366), with vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown") added explicitly to preserve highlighting independent of filetype. Root cause: image.nvim's markdown integration keys off filetype in {markdown, vimwiki} and re-parses/re-queries the whole buffer's markdown_inline tree on every TextChangedI event; the chat buffer no longer matches. Regression tests added: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'uses a distinct filetype, not the literal markdown third parties key off' (failed before the fix, confirmed) and 'keeps markdown treesitter highlighting despite the distinct filetype'. Full suite: 237/237 pass. luacheck: 59 warnings, all pre-existing, 0 introduced. stylua --check: clean. Not covered by this fix, as filed: lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27 has the same pattern on a different, short-lived buffer -- left open per the bead's 'Not covered' section.

title: Codex edit permissions are answered with a -32602 protocol error
description:
codex-acp sends edit permission requests with no reviewable payload at all:

  {"toolCall":{"toolCallId":"call_SObIFxWtTS90EE6K7JbBTfgX","kind":"edit","status":"pending"},"options":[...]}

(from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260717-163626-2991539-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log)

No rawInput, no content, no path. lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua from_acp therefore returns {kind = "file_edit", path = nil}, gates.check rejects it with "permission file edit must have a non-empty path", and lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_request answers the agent with JSON-RPC error -32602 instead of asking the user anything. The user never sees a prompt and codex sees a protocol error.

Separate from the claude case: there is nothing to review here, so the fix is not a better diff. A file-edit request that carries no path or reviewable text should fall back to the generic permission picker (allow/reject options are present in the payload) rather than being answered with a protocol error.

Found while fixing the claude payload bug; not verified live with codex, only from the logged payload and reading the code.
close_reason: Completed: pathless edit requests now reach the generic permission decision flow; regression and full suite pass

Regression test now proves it is normalized to {kind=unknown}, enters waiting_permission, and returns the selected advertised option. title: Malformed ACP file-edit permission request terminates session
description:
## Reproduction

In session codex/019ff53a-629d-71a3-a1de-1a2506b42912, the agent sent an ACP session/request_permission file-edit request without a non-empty path. louiselm reported:

`Error: invalid ACP permission request: permission file edit must have a non-empty path`

The invalid request currently calls the session fatal-error path, closes the ACP client, and prevents the grilling session from continuing.

## Expected

Reject only the malformed permission request with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error. Keep the ACP session alive so the agent can continue or retry with a valid request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A file-edit permission request with a missing or empty path receives an error response with code -32602 and the validation message.
- The session remains ready/waiting for subsequent work and does not emit a fatal session error.
- Existing valid permission requests and malformed fatal startup/update handling remain unchanged.
- Add deterministic regression coverage.
close_reason: Changed malformed ACP permission requests to receive JSON-RPC -32602 errors without terminating the session; added regression coverage. Verification: focused api_spec 17/17, full MiniTest 132/132, stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

It never consumes configured agents or skills.paths, so :LouiselmChat cannot launch the configured claude-agent-acp session or expose the central skill tree. A manual Session.new + Skills.discover + Skills.inject + Chat.new wiring was exercised successfully against claude-agent-acp 0.64.2. title: Investigate duplicate allow_always permission options
description:
## Observation

Screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260810_0558_1920x1200_1786334287.png` shows the LouiseLM command permission picker with four entries:

1. `allow_once`
2. `allow_always`
3. `allow_always`
4. `reject_once`

This appeared while running the commit/sync workflow in the Codex session.

## Question

Determine whether the two `allow_always` entries are intentional because they represent distinct permission scopes/operations, or whether the renderer is duplicating/collapsing distinct option labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- Trace the ACP permission options from the agent response through normalization and chat picker rendering.
- Identify the semantic difference between the two `allow_always` options, if any.
- If distinct, make the picker labels explain their scopes; if duplicate rendering is a bug, fix it.
- Add focused regression coverage for the resolved behavior.
- Preserve the existing allow/reject semantics.
close_reason: Confirmed duplicate allow_always entries are intentional: Codex uses distinct names and option IDs for session-scoped versus persistent permission grants. Fixed chat rendering to prefer ACP option names over generic kinds; added regression coverage. Verification: focused chat 31 passed; full mini.test suite 116 passed; stylua and lua-language-server passed.

title: QA round: session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring
description:
# Manual QA review — session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring

**Round closed 2026-08-20.** All ten cases (0–9) run. Six findings, two fixed
and verified during the round, four filed and deliberately left open. This is
the round's sole durable record; the working file it was written in has been
deleted, per `louiselm-ri1`.

**Build under test:** `ec19281..HEAD` (15 commits). The ones with testable
behaviour:

| Commit    | What changed                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `6167df0` | writefile errors in `Chat:to_markdown` (re-verify, `louiselm-dim`)   |
| `14dbab6` | tool-call blocks collapse to `<details>` in the markdown export      |
| `f0b4d9c` | blog fragments wired into built pages (re-verify, `louiselm-xrf`)    |
| `cd37ab2` | chat buffer filetype `markdown` → `louiselm-session` + explicit TS   |

Doc/bookkeeping only, nothing to test: `ec86d89`, `a515c01`, `e9d801a`,
`3140b93`, `b1f2781`, `a8af349`, `10ba83c`, `e0c6269`, `0d53644`, `9856288`,
`cd47617`.

**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the last round (`louiselm-vj0`) closed on build `4e4a58b`/`674939b` and
produced two fixes that were never re-driven by hand. Since then the chat
buffer's filetype changed under every filetype-keyed plugin the user has
installed, and the export format grew raw HTML — both changes whose real
consequences live entirely outside the test process.

## Status

| #   | Case                                                        | State                          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| 0   | `stylua --check .` on a clean tree                          | **found a defect** — see F1    |
| 1   | image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript             | **PASS** — 1.1/1.2/1.3 all confirmed, see below |
| 2   | Markdown highlighting survived the filetype change          | **PASS** — `:Inspect` shows `markdown` + `markdown_inline` captures |
| 3   | What else was keyed on `filetype=markdown`                  | **PASS** — options identical in both buffers, nothing lost |
| 4   | `:LouiselmToMarkdown` into a missing directory (re-verify)  | **PASS** — clean notification, no E482; `louiselm-euj` reconfirmed |
| 5   | Collapsed tool blocks in a real export                      | **2 defects, both fixed and re-verified** (`a6484ea`, `3d6557d`) — F4, F5 |
| 6   | `:lines: 1` placeholder fails loudly                        | **PASS** — exit 1 naming `blog.md:5`, nothing written, `myst.yml` untouched |
| 7   | Fragment reaches the built page, in a browser (re-verify)   | **PASS** — wiring verified, page looks right; width prediction refuted |
| 8   | Same under `myst start`, not just `myst build`              | **PASS** — excerpt renders in the dev server too |
| 9   | Re-run idempotency in the real repo                         | **found a defect** — see F6 (`louiselm-qcq`); `blog.md`/`myst.yml` stable, fragment is not |

## What the test suite already covers — skip these

- `render_entry`'s exact `<sub>`/`<details>` output and block ordering
  (`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`), and the same assertions end-to-end
  through the file (`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`).
- `Chat:to_markdown` returning `nil, "could not write markdown file: ..."` for a
  missing destination directory — the new test added by `6167df0`. Case 4 only
  covers what the *command* shows the user, which no test reaches.
- Buffer filetype is not the literal `markdown`, and a treesitter highlighter is
  active on the chat buffer (`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, both added by `cd37ab2`).
  They prove the two assertions in isolation; they cannot see any third-party
  plugin, which is the entire point of the change.
- Fragment bytes matching an independent TOhtml capture, three-way idempotency
  (fragments/blog.md/myst.yml), excerpt removal cleanup, and a real
  `myst build --html --strict` producing a page that references the fragment
  (`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`, parts 1–3). Cases 7–9 are what that
  suite structurally cannot reach: a browser, the dev server, and this repo's
  own `myst.yml` rather than a synthetic fixture root.
- Scaffold shape and marker-comment stubbing (`test-create-blog.sh`).

Baseline for this round: the full `mini.test` suite is green (0 fails, 0 notes)
at `cd37ab2`. `stylua --check .` is not — see F1.

## Setup

The installed plugin clone is already at `cd37ab2`, same as the repo, so there
is nothing to update before starting. Confirm and restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

After any fix I commit mid-round:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

then `:write` the buffer it opens, restart nvim, and re-confirm both commits
match.

Cases 7–9 need `nvim`, `node` (v24.16.0 here, CI pins node:24) and `myst`
(v1.10.1) on PATH — all three confirmed present.

Throughout, `<bufnr>` means the transcript buffer's number. Get it with
`:lua =vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()` while the transcript window is focused.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Carried from `louiselm-vj0` / `docs/example-workflow.md`: when the round runs
  inside louiselm's own session, the ACP log covers the whole conversation, not
  the turn being examined. Restrict the log's tool-call ids to the prefix ending
  at the last id that also appears in the export before diffing.
- Cases 1–3 share one open session on purpose (a fresh transcript has too
  little content for the perf question). Cases 4 and 5 are independent; run
  them in whatever order suits.
- Case 7 writes into `blog/` and `blog/myst.yml` in the real repo. That is
  deliberate — a fixture root is what the automated test already does — but see
  Cleanup, and do not commit any of it.
- **`:messages` is the wrong place to look for any louiselm notification on this
  machine.** louiselm surfaces user-facing errors and successes through
  `vim.notify`; snacks.nvim replaces `vim.notify` with `Snacks.notifier`, which
  renders floating windows and keeps its own history. Nothing it shows lands in
  `:messages`. Use `:lua Snacks.notifier.show_history()` (`<leader>n`) for every
  case in this file that expects a notification — 4, 5 and 6 all do. Cost of
  learning this the hard way: one round of case 4 where the expected evidence
  could not have appeared no matter what the code did.

## Cases

### 0. `stylua --check .` on a clean tree

Already run by me, before handing this over. Recorded here so the round's record
is complete.

```bash
git status --porcelain    # was empty at the time
stylua --check .; echo "exit=$?"
```

Result: `exit=1`, one diff, in `blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua`. See F1. The
tree is no longer clean after this — filing F1 wrote `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and
this file is untracked. Neither affects any case below.

### 1. image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript

Exercises `cd37ab2` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366`.

This is the whole reason the commit exists, and nothing in-process can assert
it. Parts 1.1–1.3 share one session; do not restart between them.

**1.1** "Transcript" here just means the conversation text that accumulates in
the louiselm window — header, then every user turn, assistant reply and tool
call, then the `> ` input line at the bottom. It is all **one buffer** (see
`Chat:attach`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1376-1378`), so the input line is
part of it too and you do not have to aim at a particular window: anywhere in
the louiselm window is the right place to stand.

So there is nothing to set up. Just use louiselm normally for a few turns —
ideally ones where the agent runs tools, since tool payloads are what make the
buffer grow fast — until it is long enough to scroll through. Length is the
whole point: a per-keystroke rescan costs nothing on a three-line buffer, which
is why a fresh session cannot show this bug.

Then, with the cursor anywhere in that louiselm window:

```vim
