## Findings this round

**F2 — Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it** (`louiselm-tcb`,
P1, open investigation, likely not ours). Reported mid-round as "neovim simply
crashed". It did not. `journalctl --user` shows all three
`app-ghostty-surface-transient-*.scope` units ending within one second at
05:14:18-19, then a fresh ghostty process at 05:14:27 — eleven seconds before
Neovim was relaunched at 05:14:38. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface, so
one death closes every window; Neovim was hung up, which is why there was no
deadly-signal banner. Ruled out: Neovim crash (no `ERR` in `nvim.log`), OOM
(`oom_kill 0` in the user slice), a Ghostty panic (no trace in a journal that
holds its full lifecycle), and `cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start` — the user's
config already ran `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so treesitter load
on that buffer is unchanged by the commit. Still open: the kernel log for an
AMDGPU reset, and whether image.nvim's kitty-graphics traffic is involved —
**which makes case 1.2 the discriminator, so run it.** Found by the tester when
the editor vanished, not by any case in this plan.

**F6 — `render-post` fragments are not byte-identical across runs**
(`louiselm-qcq`, P3, not fixed). `render-post.sh`'s header promises fragment
output is "a pure function of the current input" and that "running twice
against unchanged input is byte-identical". Ten consecutive runs on identical
input in an identical environment produced **four distinct fragments**; holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it, so it is run-to-run nondeterminism, not
environment sensitivity. The entire diff is CSS rule order and property order
within a rule (`.-conceal {}` moving position;
`.-markup-strong {color: …; font-weight: bold}` vs the reverse) — the `<pre>`
is identical every time and every variant renders the same, which is why case 7
looked fine. Origin is upstream: `:TOhtml` emits its `<style>` block from an
unordered table, and this pipeline preserves it verbatim by design.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs precisely the right check (`diff -rq` across
two runs) and passes anyway, because its fixture excerpts are 4–5 lines of
prose and a three-line Lua snippet — too few highlight groups for the order to
move. The real excerpt produces 11 rules. Not fixed because the obvious fix
(sort the CSS in `render-post.mjs`) collides with part 1's assertion that the
fragment matches an *independent* TOhtml capture byte-for-byte; that is a
design decision, written up in the bead.

**F5 — Single-line captions run to thousands of characters** (`louiselm-u1r`,
P2, **fixed in `3d6557d`**, closed). Exposed by F4's own fix: once captions
were one line, the longest in the verified export was **7319 characters** (then
6963, 6490) — whole `br create --description` invocations with the bead body
inlined. Correct but useless as a label, and a live risk to case 7, which
renders these exports through `:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme
fixes and does not expose. Bounded at 120 characters via
`strchars`/`strcharpart` rather than `string.sub`, since real titles carry em
dashes and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8 mid-character; the full
title is untouched in the `<details>` payload. Worth noting how this was found:
not by a case, but by measuring the artifact after a fix instead of declaring
victory on the assertion that the fix targeted.

**F4 — Multi-line tool titles break the export's `<sub>` caption and inject
fake `##` sections** (`louiselm-cmr`, P1, **fixed in `a6484ea`**, closed,
**verified** by re-export: 156 `## Tool` / 56 `## Assistant` / 17 `## User` and
no other `##`; 156 of 156 captions closing on their own line; zero multi-line
spans). Found by
case 5, and exactly the failure class the case was written for: fixtures use
short single-line titles, real payloads carry whole shell commands. In a 120
tool-call export, 12 captions span more than one line — the worst runs 150
lines — because `transcript.lua:182` interpolates `raw.title` into a
single-line string and `split_lines` then turns its embedded newlines into real
breaks. Everything between the unclosed `<sub>` and its `</sub>` lands in the
document as raw markdown, which added 28 fabricated `##` headings
(`## Observed`, `## Root cause`, …) leaked out of heredoc bead descriptions.
Older than `14dbab6` — the previous `## Tool: <title>` format split the heading
the same way — but the round found it while testing that commit. What passed:
the block counts balance exactly (120 `## Tool` / `<details>` / `<summary>` /
`</details>`), no title fell back to a raw tool id, and all statuses are real
(`completed` ×104, `failed` ×4).

**F3 — Skill discovery warns per symlinked subdirectory and scans whole source
repos** (`louiselm-msg`, P2, not fixed — out of scope). Surfaced by accident:
the snacks notifier history opened for case 4 also held
`louiselm: skill discovery found 31 issue(s)`. Thirty of those 31 are the same
"symlink resolves outside configured root" warning, fired once per symlinked
subdirectory on a stow layout where every skill is a symlink by design. The
check at `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:209` warns and then queues the
directory anyway, so it prevents nothing — and because `bvr`'s skill directory
symlinks to a whole Rust repo, discovery walks 3133 directories of which 2839
are `target/`. Measured in-process against the real config: `discover()` takes
381 ms, of which the `bvr` subtree alone accounts for 376 ms. `skills_spec.lua`
misses it because its fixtures build symlinks inside a temp root, so no case
models a symlink to a large real repository. Not fixed: nothing in
`ec19281..HEAD` touches skills, and the fix is a behavioural decision about
what "outside the root" should mean.

**F1 — `stylua --check .` fails on a clean tree** (`louiselm-d7l`, not fixed).
`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is not StyLua-formatted (single-quoted strings
where the repo config sets `quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`), so the gate
AGENTS.md §4 declares — `stylua --check .`, unscoped, whole repo — has exited 1
since `674939b`. Introduced by the blog pipeline commit, which the previous
round (`louiselm-vj0`) had in scope and did not catch, because that round tested
the pipeline's behaviour and never ran the formatter gate. Not fixed during the
round: it is a one-command fix, but it is out of scope for the cases below and
touching the tree mid-round invalidates case 0's clean-tree premise.

title: Grill-me needed: how should qa-review rounds be archived, and does beads belong in the loop
description:
Not actionable as-is — this is a seed for a future grill-me session, not a
spec to implement from. Surfaced at the close of the transcript-export/
blog-publishing QA round (2026-08-18), when a process question came up that
didn't fit anywhere in the existing skill chain.

## The open questions

- **Archiving authority.** Once a qa-review round closes, does the working
  file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) become the durable record of what was tested
  and found, or is it disposable scratch once findings are filed to beads?
  Right now nothing says either way, so rounds just accumulate as loose
  untracked files.
- **Where archiving sits in the qa-review process.** Should the qa-review
  skill itself have a defined "closing" step that decides what happens to
  the file (commit it, summarize it into beads, delete it), or is that
  always a manual call by whoever's running the round?
- **Could beads be leveraged more directly.** Instead of (or alongside) a
  markdown working file, could a qa-review round's cases/results live in
  beads itself — e.g. as a parent issue with the plan, sub-issues per case?
  Unclear if that's better or just adds ceremony to something that works
  fine as a file today.

## Why this doesn't fit the usual chain

Their standing workflow is grill-me -> to-beads -> tasks executed across
sessions ("skill chaining"). Within a qa-review round, a code bug correctly
triggers to-beads-bug — that chain already works. But this round produced a
different kind of finding: not a bug, a question about the skills/workflow
itself. There's currently no formalized way for a skill to route that kind
of self-reflective finding anywhere — it only survived this time because the
user happened to notice and say it was worth a grill-me session. Whether
findings like this should sometimes get folded directly into a skill's own
instructions (when concrete enough) versus always deferred to a grill-me
session (when still vague) is itself part of what's open here.

## A concrete proposal already on record

This question isn't new — the user raised it explicitly at the *start* of
this same QA round, in an earlier session (`claude/85f97534-8fa6-4d95-a05a-7c0851bec937`):
"while we do this i want you to think if those reviews conversation or
document you produce as part of the review could leverage beads for
historical / archiving purposes." That session's assistant answered with a
concrete sketch the user liked and wants preserved verbatim here for the
grill-me session to react to, not re-derive:

1. **One bead per round**, type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file QA_REVIEW.md`. The whole plan lands in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is committed — so the round becomes
   greppable history instead of an untracked file you have to decide about
   at the end. That's the exact question that ended the *previous* round
   (the permissions round) unresolved too: "commit it as a record, or
   delete it."
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>` — the graph then answers "which round found this?" and `br
   graph` shows a round's blast radius. This round's findings
   (`louiselm-dim`, `louiselm-euj`, `louiselm-d2o`, `louiselm-xrf`) are
   already beads but orphaned from the round that produced them — exactly
   the gap this proposal closes.
3. **Round-by-round narration goes in `br comments add`** — append-only and
   timestamped, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit). The
   markdown file stays the live scratchpad *during* the round since it
   churns every round; beads takes the final state on close.
4. **`--external-ref` holds the session id** (e.g.
   `claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384` for this round), which
   dovetails with the user's global commit-message rule (`Refs <id>` for
   named sessions/issues), and `br orphans` catches anything referenced in a
   commit but still open.

The convergence the prior session flagged as the nice part: the
transcript-export feature this very round was testing turns a session into
a publishable artifact. So under this proposal the bead becomes the index,
the exported transcript is the evidence, and a blog post (via the same
publishing pipeline, once `louiselm-xrf` is fixed) is the human-readable
version of the same round — three layers of the same feature set reused for
QA's own record-keeping instead of a fourth bespoke mechanism.

## Bigger context

Connects to a broader, previously-discussed wish: the user's own workflow
(grill-me/beads/session-chaining) eventually being expressible as a
configurable part of louiselm itself, not just a convention they follow by
hand. Not fully re-litigated here — worth pulling that thread in the
grill-me session too.

## Not covered

No decision on the concrete proposal above — it was well-received when
sketched, but never evaluated against the three open questions or actually
tried on a round (this round still used a plain `QA_REVIEW.md`). Left for
the grill-me session: whether to adopt it as-is, adapt it, or reject it in
favor of something else.
close_reason: Resolved via grill-me. Routed to feature louiselm-ri1 (Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads), with child tasks louiselm-ri1.1 (skill closing step) and louiselm-ri1.2 (retroactive close of QA_REVIEW.md and QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md, blocked on ri1.1). Adopted the concrete proposal on record as-is: one chore/qa-round bead per round via --description-file + --external-ref, findings as children via the existing to-beads-bug chain, cases stay flat (never beaded), narration via br comments, working file deleted on close. Bigger workflow-config-engine thread explicitly left out of scope per agreement.

title: Skill/file/buffer/selection context pickers are unreachable through the documented :LouiselmChat setup path
description:
The chat context-queuing API (`pick_skill`, `pick_file`, `mention_buffer`, `send_selection`) documented in README.md under "Chat context" is completely unreachable through the plugin's own documented setup path, so no user who follows the README can ever attach a file, skill, buffer mention, or visual selection to a prompt.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 while setting up a manual QA round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP skill invocation): asked the user to invoke the skill picker to test it, and they had never wired anything for it -- because there is nothing to wire it to.

`grep -rn "pick_skill\|pick_file\|mention_buffer\|send_selection" lua/ --include="*.lua" | grep -v chat/init.lua` returns nothing: these four `Chat` methods are defined in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and never called anywhere else in the tree -- not in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua (which backs `:LouiselmChat` and every other registered `:Louiselm*` command), not anywhere.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` registers 12 `:Louiselm*` ex commands (LouiselmChat, LouiselmNewSession, LouiselmResume, LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmRenameSession, LouiselmSessionId, LouiselmToMarkdown, LouiselmCloseSession, LouiselmCancel, LouiselmSessionOptions, LouiselmPermissions, LouiselmInline) -- none of them calls pick_skill/pick_file/mention_buffer/send_selection.

The `chat` object these methods live on is a local upvalue private to `Command.register()`'s closure (command.lua:194 `local chat`); nothing exposes it, and `Louiselm.setup()` (lua/louiselm/init.lua) returns only a boolean. So even a user willing to write their own keymap has no object to call these methods on unless they bypass `Louiselm.setup()`/`:LouiselmChat` entirely and hand-construct a second, parallel `Chat` instance via the low-level `require("louiselm.ui.chat").new(sessions, {...})` constructor -- which would not be attached to the same session as their real chat buffer.

README.md documents these four methods under "## Chat context" (around line 438) as plain Lua snippets (`chat:mention_buffer()`, `chat:send_selection()`, `chat:pick_file()`, `chat:pick_skill()`) with no indication that `chat` here is a user-constructed low-level object, not the one `:LouiselmChat` creates -- reading the README top to bottom gives no working path to ever call them.

## Symptoms

- Following the README exactly (`Louiselm.setup(config)` + `:LouiselmChat`), there is no command, keymap, or other UI affordance to pick a skill, pick a file, mention the source buffer, or send a visual selection.
- The entire native/inject skill-invocation feature (including the just-shipped louiselm-2w4) is unreachable in practice for the documented setup path.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua never registers commands for these four `Chat` methods, and never exposes the `chat` instance it privately constructs.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/context_spec.lua` call `chat:pick_skill()` etc. directly on a `Chat` object constructed in the test, which is exactly the low-level path the README also (accidentally) documents -- so the tests exercise the methods correctly but never assert that the *shipped, documented, high-level setup path* (`:LouiselmChat`) can reach them. No test covers `command.lua`'s command surface for context actions because there was never a command to cover.

## Fix direction

Add `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile` (optional root arg, `nargs = "?"`, mirroring `:LouiselmToMarkdown`'s optional-arg pattern), `:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, and `:LouiselmSendSelection` to command.lua, following the existing `if chat == nil then report_error("no chat session is open") ... end` pattern used by `:LouiselmCancel`/`:LouiselmSessionOptions`/`:LouiselmCloseSession` (these need an already-open session to queue context onto, unlike `:LouiselmChat`/`:LouiselmPermissions` which use `ensure_chat()` to open one on demand). Update README's command list (around line 269) and the "Chat context" section to stop implying the low-level constructor snippet is reachable from the documented setup path.

## Acceptance

- New `:Louiselm*` commands registered and covered by a test in tests/ui/command_spec.lua that drives them through the real `:LouiselmChat` + `Command.register()` path (matching the file's existing "through the normal chat path" test style), not just calling the Chat method directly.
- README updated to list the new commands and no longer implies the raw snippets are usable from a documented setup.

## Not covered

- Whether default keymaps (not just ex commands) are also warranted -- left as a separate decision; this bug is about there being no path at all, not about ergonomics beyond a command existing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e553a1. Added :LouiselmPickSkill, :LouiselmPickFile [root], :LouiselmMentionBuffer, :LouiselmSendSelection to lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua, matching the existing chat==nil guard pattern used by :LouiselmCancel/:LouiselmSessionOptions. Tests: command existence check, a combined 'no chat session is open' case for all four, and a real end-to-end test driving :LouiselmMentionBuffer through :LouiselmChat + a fake ACP process, asserting the chip renders and the queued context is sent in the next session/prompt. Updated README's command list and Chat context section. Gates: full mini.test suite green, stylua and lua-language-server clean repo-wide (excluding a pre-existing unrelated blog/ script). Deferred: default keymaps beyond the ex commands, per the bead's own 'Not covered' note.

title: Investigate default availability of LouiselmResume
description:
## Goal

Determine whether the new `:LouiselmResume` command is available for a normal louiselm.nvim installation using the user configuration in `~/.config/nvim`, and make it available by default if it is not.

## Evidence

The previous commit `798712b` added `LouiselmResume` registration inside `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`, but registration appears to depend on an explicit `require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").register()` call. The repository test and manual init files call this explicitly; verify whether the production plugin entrypoint does so for ordinary Neovim startup.

## Scope

- Reproduce/check command availability from the normal plugin runtime path and from the user configuration path.
- Trace plugin load order and setup behavior, including whether `louiselm.setup()` is required before the command exists.
- If missing by default, add the narrowest production registration fix and update/extend headless behavioral coverage and documentation as needed.
- Preserve explicit configuration behavior and avoid duplicate-registration side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The task records the observed behavior and root cause for a normal installation.
2. `:LouiselmResume` and `:LouiselmResume!` are available after ordinary plugin loading, without requiring users to manually require/register the command.
3. Existing command registration remains repeatable and tests cover the production startup path.
4. Focused tests, the full mini.test suite, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks are run or their unavailability is reported.
close_reason: Registered all chat commands from successful louiselm.setup(), added a regression test proving LouiselmResume and bang support are available after setup, and updated README wording. Verification: focused setup test passed; full mini.test suite passed (126 cases, with swap files directed to /tmp); stylua --check passed; lua-language-server --check passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Show whose turn it is in LouieLM chat
description:
## Problem

During a LouieLM chat session, the top red header shows the session option, but it does not indicate whether the model is currently sending text or whether it is the user's turn to respond.

## Desired behavior

Add a visible status indicator in the chat header that distinguishes at least:

- Model is responding/sending text
- Your turn / waiting for user input

The indicator should update as the conversation state changes and remain consistent with the actual session state. Preserve the existing red session-option header.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A LouieLM chat session visibly shows whether the model is currently responding or it is the user's turn.
2. The status changes promptly when model output starts, finishes, or the session becomes ready for user input.
3. The indicator is understandable without relying on color alone (for example, include text or an icon with accessible labeling).
4. Existing session-option header behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Already implemented by commit 106aa9c: the window-local winbar persists Your turn and Model responding while scrolling, updates on lifecycle changes, and restores the previous winbar. Current chat coverage also exercises Waiting for permission, Starting, Stopping, Error, and Unavailable labels; the latest full MiniTest run passed 185/185.

title: Add root MIT LICENSE and reconcile licence metadata
description:
Add the root `LICENSE` file and make every licence declaration in the tree agree with it.

## Steps

1. Create root `LICENSE` with the standard MIT text, correct copyright holder and year.
2. Grep the tree for licence declarations and reconcile them. Known: `capture-service/Cargo.toml` already declares `license = "MIT"` — this was a scaffolding default that happens to be correct, so it is ratified, not changed. Check the Android/Gradle side and any packaging metadata for declarations that disagree or are missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root `LICENSE` exists, is MIT, names the right holder.
- Every licence field in the repo says MIT or is absent; none contradicts.
- No file claims Apache-2.0. Apache is specifically rejected because its §3 patent grant would give away the one instrument that reaches independent reimplementation.

## Do not

Do not add SPDX headers to every source file. Not wanted, high churn, no benefit at this stage.
close_reason: Completed root MIT licence and reconciled project licence metadata; preserved third-party Gradle wrapper notices.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Scope correction from repository scan: android/gradlew and android/gradlew.bat are Gradle-generated third-party wrapper scripts and retain their upstream Apache-2.0 copyright/SPDX notices. Removing or relabelling those notices would be incorrect; they license Gradle wrapper code only and grant no rights in LouiseLM. The acceptance criterion is therefore applied to LouiseLM-owned files and project/package licence declarations. capture-service/Cargo.toml is MIT; Android build and manifest files contain no project licence declaration.

comments.text: Added root LICENSE using standard MIT text: Copyright (c) 2026 euri10. Verification: exact heading/holder and 21-line canonical structure checked; capture-service/Cargo.toml declares MIT; Android build/manifest metadata has no licence field; repository scan finds no conflicting project-owned declaration; Apache appears only in untouched Gradle-generated wrapper notices; git diff --check passed. No automated tests run because this is documentation/metadata only.

title: Standing review: relicense tripwires and shelved AGPL payload
description:
## Standing review, not a task to close

This bead exists so a decision made deliberately in 2026 survives into the year it matters. It is not ready-for-agent and should not be picked up as implementation work. It stays open until one of the tripwires below fires.

## Why MIT was chosen, and the expiry condition built into it

MIT was chosen on a **ubiquity** theory of change: LouiseLM's political effect comes from reach, from being the harness that mediates human-agent work in many environments, and friction is the enemy of reach. Copyleft was rejected because it taxes reach.

That argument has an expiry condition inside it. The moment LouiseLM **has** reach and someone is enclosing it, reach is no longer the binding constraint, and the reasoning that selected MIT has expired on its own terms. The trigger is not an arbitrary threshold or a mood — it is the falsification of the premise.

## Tripwires

Any one of these fires a **review**, not an automatic relicense:

1. A commercial product or hosted service materially derived from LouiseLM exists.
2. An entity in the named class ships something derived from LouiseLM. Named class: *entities deriving a majority of revenue from proprietary foundation models, or from the hardware they run on.*
3. An acquisition or exclusivity approach is made.

The review asks one question: **is ubiquity still the binding constraint?** If yes, nothing changes. If no, the payload below comes off the shelf.

## Shelved payload

Worked out in full during the licensing grill-me so that a future decision costs a commit, not a re-derivation.

**Licence:** `AGPL-3.0-only` — deliberately `-only`, not `-or-later`. `-or-later` delegates future terms to the FSF and is an irrevocable grant of that option; `-only` is reversible at will under sole ownership. The inbound compatibility cost of `-only` is near zero because `-or-later` code can always be used under v3 terms, and the outbound cost is irrelevant under the no-merge policy.

**Why AGPL and not GPL:** the network clause. Without it, a hosted LouiseLM owes nothing.

**Public rate card** — sold as a commercial exception, which only exists because sole ownership is intact:

| Who | Price |
|---|---|
| Individuals, non-profits, educational institutions, worker-owned co-ops | Free |
| The named class | Not available at any price |
| Everyone else | Revenue band, less an attested pay-ratio discount, or N public engineering days per year in lieu of money |

Design notes on the card:

- The free tier delivers the Peer Production License's entire politics as a *price tier* rather than a prohibition. That matters: a prohibition on capitalist users is self-defeating in a success scenario, because success in a capitalist world means most users are inside capitalist firms — so the restriction is either violated at scale and unenforced, or obeyed and the success never happened.
- Pay ratio is a **discount claimed by attestation**, never a price to be audited. Firms prove they are flat to pay less; nobody has to be audited to pay full price. This sidesteps the fact that CEO-to-median ratios are unpublished outside US-listed companies and are gameable via subsidiaries.
- Numbers stay deferred until a first real request. A published price set with zero market contact is fiction; the politically loaded rows (free tier, refusal) need no numbers and are complete without them.
- Publishing the card is deliberate: a price is a manifesto that costs money to disagree with, and it turns every procurement process into a forced encounter with the position. It is a norm, not a lock — revisable at any time, with running contracts simply finishing their term.

**Note:** a relicense does not retroactively affect already-released MIT versions; that grant is irrevocable. It works anyway because for infrastructure the value is in the maintained head, not the snapshot. A stale fork of an AI harness has a short half-life. This is the Redis / MongoDB / Elastic / Terraform / HashiCorp move, and it is legally available here only for as long as the no-merge policy keeps outside copyright out of the tree.

title: Establish LouiseLM licensing and retained-rights posture
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM has no `LICENSE` file. By default that means all rights reserved: nobody may legally use, fork, or redistribute it. That directly blocks the community goal stated in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which invites usage reports, workflow descriptions, provider implementations, and forks.

The licence choice is not a formality here. It is the instrument that decides who captures the surplus of the work if LouiseLM succeeds, and it is the only decision in the project that is cheap now and expensive later. Sole authorship is currently intact, so every option is open exactly once.

## Solution

Publish a deliberate licensing posture: **MIT**, with sole copyright retained and every non-copyright instrument held back rather than granted away.

The theory of change chosen is **ubiquity, not extraction**. A harness's political effect comes from being everywhere and shaping how human-agent work is done — local-first, legible, owned by the operator. Friction is the enemy of that effect, so the licence is optimised purely for reach and carries no politics at all. The politics live in the instruments MIT is silent about.

Deliberately **MIT and not Apache-2.0**: Apache §3 grants an explicit, perpetual patent licence to every user. Patents are the only legal instrument that reaches independent reimplementation of harness design, which is the form of value extraction copyright cannot touch. Apache would disarm that before it is ever needed. MIT's silence retains it.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want a clear `LICENSE` file, so that I can legally install, fork, and build on LouiseLM without guessing.
2. As a potential contributor, I want the copyright and relicensing position stated plainly, so that I can decide what to invest with accurate information rather than an assumption of perpetuity.
3. As the maintainer, I want trademark and patent rights retained and unstated in the licence, so that the instruments that actually reach a model provider remain available if LouiseLM matters.
4. As a reader of the project, I want the political reasoning published separately from the licence, so that the licence stays frictionless while the position stays legible.
5. As the maintainer, I want the licence choice framed as serving reach, so that revisiting it later is a disclosed term rather than a rug-pull.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a fresh clone, when a user looks for licensing, then a root `LICENSE` file states MIT with the correct copyright holder and year.
2. Given the repo tree, when licence metadata is checked across components, then every declared licence agrees with the root `LICENSE`.
3. Given `CONTRIBUTING.md`, when a prospective contributor reads it, then it states that copyright is held solely by the maintainer, that no outside code is merged, and that the maintainer retains the right to license future versions under different terms.
4. Given the README, when a reader reaches the licence section, then it states that the licence choice serves reach and will be revisited if reach stops being the binding constraint.
5. Given a published trademark policy, when an entity in the named class considers using the LouiseLM name, then the policy plainly refuses it.
6. Given the political statement document, when it is read alongside the licence, then the anti-capitalist position is legible without any of it appearing as a licence term.

## Implementation Notes

- Affected: root `LICENSE` (new), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, a trademark policy document, a political statement document, and licence metadata in `capture-service/Cargo.toml` and any Android/Gradle equivalent.
- `capture-service/Cargo.toml` already declares `license = "MIT"`. That was a scaffolding default, never a decision. It is now correct and needs ratifying rather than changing — but the tree should be checked for other declarations that disagree.
- **The no-merge policy in `CONTRIBUTING.md` is load-bearing and must not be silently relaxed.** It is what keeps outside copyright out of the tree, which is what keeps sole ownership intact, which is what makes a future relicense legally possible without a CLA. Any future change to merge policy is also a change to the licensing position.
- Named class, deliberately structural rather than a list of company names so it survives renames, subsidiaries, and a shifting landscape: *entities deriving a majority of revenue from proprietary foundation models, or from the hardware they run on.* Names go stale; a structure does not.
- The class refusal is enforceable through **trademark**, not through the licence. MIT grants everyone the right to use the code; it conveys no right to the name. Attempting a use restriction in the licence text would make it non-free, cost distribution channels, and buy nothing enforceable.
- Retained and intentionally not granted: trademark (the live instrument from day one), patents (latent, expensive, the only reach into idea absorption), and the right to license future versions differently.
- Transparency was chosen over concealment for the copyright position specifically. The reasoning: the no-merge policy already makes sole ownership publicly inferable, the community LouiseLM wants punishes ambush and forgives disclosed risk, and a pre-announced possibility converts an eventual relicense from betrayal into an accepted term. Elastic and HashiCorp took their damage for the surprise, not for the relicense.

## Testing Notes

- No automated tests. Verification is documentary: fresh-clone read-through, and a grep for licence declarations across the tree confirming they all agree.
- Confirm no document states or implies a perpetual open-source guarantee that would contradict the retained relicensing right.

## Out of Scope

- Registering a trademark or filing patents. Rights are retained by not granting them; formal registration is a later, funded decision.
- Any copyleft licence or commercial rate card. That payload is deliberately shelved, recorded in the standing licence review.
- Creating a foundation, steward-ownership structure, or purpose trust. Ownership stays personal by explicit decision, to keep the ability to change course.
- Any CLA or DCO process. Neither is needed while the no-merge policy holds.
close_reason: Published the complete MIT licensing and retained-rights posture; standing tripwire review remains open by design.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: All six acceptance criteria are complete: root MIT licence and metadata reconciliation; sole ownership/relicensing disclosure; README reach framing; trademark refusal; political statement. louiselm-licence-flip-review-42h remains open intentionally because its own contract says it is a standing review, not an implementation task to close.

title: Recover and resume ACP sessions
description:
## Problem Statement

Recovering an existing ACP conversation currently requires users to know the adapter name, exact ACP session ID, adapter configuration, and working directory, then execute Lua manually. Normal users need a discoverable resume flow without losing the current chat.

## Solution

Add a `:LouiseLmResume` flow that discovers recoverable sessions from configured ACP adapters, filters them to the current workspace by default, and loads the selected session into a separate chat buffer. Keep the public Lua load API as the underlying and advanced recovery path.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to pick a prior session from a list so I can continue work without remembering opaque ACP IDs.
2. As a user, I want the default list limited to the current workspace so unrelated sessions do not overwhelm me.
3. As a user, I want an explicit all-workspaces view so older sessions remain recoverable.
4. As a user, I want resuming to preserve my current chat and open the recovered conversation separately.
5. As a user, I want load failures explained without silently creating a new session.
6. As an advanced user, I want the Lua `load_session` API to remain available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given configured adapters that support session listing, the resume flow lists sessions with available adapter, workspace, display name, and activity metadata.
2. Given the default resume view, only sessions for the current workspace are shown; an explicit action reveals other workspaces.
3. Given a selected session, louiselm uses the current configured adapter definition and ACP `session/load`, then attaches it to a new chat buffer.
4. Given an existing attached chat, resuming does not replace or dispose it.
5. Given a missing, unsupported, or failed session load, the UI reports the specific failure and does not create a replacement session.
6. Given a loaded session, ACP-replayed history appears in the new chat before it is marked ready.
7. Given a session adapter cannot list sessions, exact-ID loading remains available through the public Lua API.
8. A lightweight local cache may accelerate discovery, but the ACP adapter remains authoritative; stale entries are handled as load failures and can be removed.
9. Session identity is scoped by adapter, ACP session ID, and workspace; old adapter commands are never reused.

## Implementation Notes

- Build on the existing session registry/API and chat attach lifecycle.
- Add ACP session-list support only where advertised; preserve graceful fallback for adapters without it.
- Keep discovery/cache state separate from conversation history.
- Use the existing asynchronous callback/event model and test production scheduling boundaries.

## Testing Notes

- Test listing/filtering and stable session identity across adapters and workspaces.
- Test successful load/replay/attach without disturbing an existing chat.
- Test unsupported listing, missing sessions, adapter failures, and no silent new-session fallback.
- Test the public Lua load path remains functional.

## Out of Scope

- Changing ACP persistence semantics or adapter storage.
- Reusing historical adapter commands.
- Automatically deleting adapter-side sessions.
- Reconstructing conversation history from louiselm cache data.
close_reason: Implemented discoverable ACP session resume flow; all 125 tests, StyLua, LuaLS, and diff check pass.

Updated the mock ACP agent and README. Verification: focused red-green tests, full mini.test suite 125/125, stylua --check ., lua-language-server zero diagnostics, and git diff --check all pass.

description: Confirmed compatibility gap during configured tree discovery. Skills.discover({"~/.config/agentskills"}) found the workflow skills but reported .system/skill-creator/SKILL.md and .system/skill-installer/SKILL.md as malformed YAML frontmatter because the parser rejects a nested metadata mapping. title: Permission evaluation calls sha256 in fast event
description:
## Reproduction

During an ACP command permission request, LouiseLM errors in the callback with:

`E5560: Vimscript function "sha256" must not be called in a fast event context`

Screenshot: ~/Pictures/scrot/20260815_1140_1920x1200_1786786845.png

## Cause

`lua/louiselm/permission/store.lua:176` calls `vim.fn.sha256()` from `Store:evaluate()`. ACP stdout/message handling runs in a fast event callback, and remembered-rule validation reaches `rule_id()` while reading permission state.

## Expected

Permission requests are evaluated and displayed without violating Neovim fast-event restrictions.

## Acceptance

- Add regression coverage for evaluating a persisted permission rule from a fast-event-like callback.
- Remove the `vim.fn.sha256()` fast-event violation without adding a dependency.
- Permission requests continue to fail closed on malformed state.
- Focused and full test suites pass.
close_reason: Fixed by deferring ACP agent request callbacks out of Neovim fast-event context in acp/init.lua; added regression coverage. Verification: focused ACP tests, full MiniTest suite (182 cases), stylua --check ., and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning pass.

title: blog/scripts/create-blog.sh: scaffold a post, optional session auto-export
description:
## Goal
One script that scaffolds a new blog post directory, and — when given session ids — also exports each named session into it and stubs a literalinclude block per session.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name> [session-id...]. Bare mode creates blog/post-<name>/{blog.md, conversations/} (blog.md empty, conversations/ empty). Session-id mode additionally exports each session into conversations/<session-id>.md via the same export path LouiselmToMarkdown uses (e.g. by driving headless Neovim to run that command), and appends one literalinclude block per session to blog.md pointing at ./conversations/<session-id>.md with a placeholder :lines: value.
- Out of scope: rendering excerpts through Neovim/Catppuccin (that is the render-post.sh task), MyST site config, choosing real line ranges (author does that by hand afterward).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given create-blog.sh <name> with no session ids: blog/post-<name>/blog.md (empty) and blog/post-<name>/conversations/ (empty dir) exist.
2. Given create-blog.sh <name> <session-id>...: the same scaffold exists, plus conversations/<session-id>.md for each session id (non-empty, matching LouiselmToMarkdown's output for that session), plus blog.md containing one literalinclude block per session id referencing ./conversations/<session-id>.md.
3. Running the script twice with the same name does not silently clobber an existing post directory (errors or requires an explicit flag).

## Testing
- Script-level test: given a fake/stubbed session export, assert the created directory structure and blog.md contents match expectations.
- No Neovim UI testing needed — this is a shell script invoking headless Neovim, testable by stubbing that invocation.

## Notes
- Depends on LouiselmToMarkdown existing (task above) for the session-id auto-export path — the bare-mode scaffold alone has no dependency, but this task ships both modes together since they are one script.
- Not a Neovim command; intentionally not part of the plugin's discoverable command surface (blog/scripts/, not lua/louiselm/).
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.

title: Migrate misfiled agent memory into the repo
description:
Move the repo content currently held in Claude Code's private project memory into the repo, and reduce that memory to only what is genuinely adapter-specific.

Depends on the destinations existing first: the `AGENTS.md` work-tracking section and the example workflow document.

## The routing test

For each note ask: *would this still be true if a different adapter did the work?* Then: *is it about louiselm, or about the maintainer?*

- About louiselm, adapter-independent → the repo
- About the maintainer, cross-project → that adapter's user-level instructions, which is legitimately per-adapter since each has its own mechanism
- About one adapter's harness quirks → that adapter's project memory

## What moves where

Applying the test to the seven notes currently held:

| Note | Destination |
|---|---|
| beads is the backbone | `AGENTS.md` work-tracking section |
| bv triage in-progress-first | `AGENTS.md` work-tracking section |
| qbr workflow-engine triage requirement | `br` comment on the workflow-engine issues |
| qa-review is a human loop | example workflow document |
| workflow skill-chaining vision | example workflow document |
| prefers ambitious builds | user-level instructions (about the maintainer, not the project) |
| politics and reasoning style | user-level instructions (about the maintainer, not the project) |

Five of the seven are repo content that landed in per-adapter memory because that was the path of least resistance and nothing pushed back.

## Expected end state

The project memory folder ends up empty or nearly so, and its index with it. That is the correct outcome of a rule that says repo-first, not evidence the rule is wrong — the folder should be small.

Migrate rather than duplicate. A note left in both places is a future divergence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every note listed above exists at its destination, with its reasoning intact rather than compressed to a headline.
- No note remains in project memory that would still be true for a different adapter.
- The memory index reflects the end state and does not point at files that no longer exist.
- Nothing was lost: each of the seven can be traced to a destination or to a deliberate decision to drop it.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: Render persistent telemetry and grouped session diagnostics
description:
## Goal

Keep live, actionable session telemetry visible throughout long conversations while preserving a complete, copyable diagnostic block at the top of the chat transcript. Preserve adapter-provided values quasi as-is and make ACP versus LouiseLM-derived information visually distinguishable for QA.

## Reference

The motivating session rendered one long wrapped heading containing the ACP report id, local session id, lifecycle state, skills state, five adapter options, context usage, and turn label. Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260816_0632_948x1084_1786854748.png.

This task supersedes the design scope left after louiselm-kuc, whose persistent turn label was already implemented by commit 106aa9c. It builds on the completed compact-header work in louiselm-dv9 without reopening that historical task.

## Persistent Winbar Contract

Use the existing window-local winbar as the single persistent surface. Render fields in this order when available:

    Your turn · context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the existing friendly lifecycle labels: Your turn, Model responding, Waiting for permission, Stopping, Starting, Error, and Unavailable.
- Give lifecycle states semantic ready/active/warning/error styling; semantic urgency takes precedence over provenance styling.
- Render adapter-reported context used/size quasi as-is with ACP provenance styling.
- Render only the LouiseLM-derived percentage in parentheses with derived provenance styling. Do not display the normal/elevated/high/critical pressure taxonomy.
- After a model change, retain the last context reading and append an explicit derived stale marker until a fresh adapter usage update arrives.
- Render cumulative cost quasi as-is only after the adapter reports it. Retain the last reported cumulative cost when later usage updates omit cost; remove it when the adapter explicitly clears it. Never invent zero, unknown, or unsupported placeholders.
- If context or cost has never been reported, omit that segment.
- Do not include session identity, model, mode, adapter options, or tool activity in the winbar. Tool activity remains in chronological transcript messages.
- Keep all telemetry on this one surface. Do not add a statusline, tabline, floating HUD, or pinned split.

## Transcript Diagnostic Contract

Replace the single unbounded heading with one contiguous, complete block using one compact logical line per category:

    # codex/ACP_SESSION_ID · session-1
    Session: status=ready · display=Your turn · skills=native
    ACP options: Mode=agent · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off
    Telemetry: context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the full ACP report identity and local session identity in the first line.
- Preserve both raw LouiseLM lifecycle status and its friendly display label so copied QA evidence exposes their mapping.
- Show the exact skills policy: native, inject, or off. Do not collapse native and inject into on.
- Preserve adapter option names, typed current values, and adapter order on one compact logical line. Allow normal Neovim wrapping; do not add width-dependent packing or one-option-per-line rendering.
- Deliberately duplicate context and cost in the diagnostic block and winbar. The winbar is the live HUD; the transcript block is the complete copyable snapshot. Both must render from the same session state and formatting logic so they cannot disagree.
- Keep the block current when lifecycle state, configuration options, context, cost, or stale state changes.

## Provenance and Rendering

- Use explicit section labels as the primary provenance signal: Session for LouiseLM state and ACP options for adapter configuration. These labels survive copying.
- In mixed telemetry, use named user-overridable highlight groups for ACP values and LouiseLM-derived values. Do not hard-code colors.
- Keep textual structure sufficient without color: raw counts remain separate from parenthesized percentage/stale annotations.
- Escape statusline syntax in all dynamic winbar segments before composing highlight directives. Adapter-originated text must not be able to alter winbar formatting.
- Do not let provenance coloring weaken semantic error or permission states.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Scrolling a long chat keeps the friendly lifecycle label, exact reported context counts, derived percentage, stale validity, and optional last-reported cost visible in the window-local winbar.
2. Adapters that omit context or cost produce no fabricated values or placeholders, and explicit cost clearing removes the persistent cost.
3. Context pressure words are absent from both persistent and diagnostic displays; the derived percentage remains.
4. The transcript starts with the four logical diagnostic categories above, remains contiguous and copyable, uses exact skills policy and ACP option order, and intentionally duplicates live telemetry.
5. Raw status and friendly display label update together for every lifecycle state. Header and winbar telemetry cannot diverge because they share canonical formatting.
6. Provenance remains understandable without color and is additionally visible through user-overridable highlight groups; dynamic winbar content is statusline-escaped.
7. Existing winbar save/restore, session switching, disposal, scheduling, and late-event safety remain intact.
8. Headless tests cover lifecycle changes, context and cost updates/omission/clearing, model-change staleness, exact skills policies, several ACP options, provenance highlights, statusline escaping, and restoration. Include a manual narrow-split smoke check rather than width-specific pixel assertions.
9. README documents the persistent telemetry, grouped diagnostic block, provenance meaning, optional adapter fields, and last-reported cost semantics.

## Out of Scope

- A session-info copy command; add it only after real QA copying friction.
- Persistent session identity, model, mode, configuration, or tool activity.
- LouiseLM context pressure classifications.
- Width-aware option packing, per-option vertical rows, a generic statusline framework, or additional sticky UI surfaces.
close_reason: Implemented the persistent lifecycle/context/cost winbar, grouped four-line session diagnostics, exact skills policy and ACP option ordering, model-change staleness, optional last-reported cost semantics, named provenance/semantic highlights, statusline escaping, README documentation, and behavioral coverage. TDD evidence: the grouped diagnostics/window-bar test failed against the previous single heading. Verification: focused chat 48/48 and session 21/21 within the full run; full MiniTest 189/189; stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; 40-column smoke passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Show whose turn it is in LouieLM chat
description:

title: Skill discovery warns per symlinked subdirectory and scans whole source repos
description:
Skill discovery follows symlinks that leave the configured root, warns about
each one, and then scans them anyway. On a stow-style skills layout — where
every skill is a symlink into a dotfiles or source repo — this produces a
warning per symlinked subdirectory on a completely healthy install, and walks
whole source repositories looking for `SKILL.md`. The user sees
"louiselm: skill discovery found 31 issue(s)" on every session start, and pays
~380 ms for a scan that is 91% Rust build artifacts.

## Observed

Found during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, on build `cd37ab2`,
2026-08-20. Out of scope for that round — nothing in the range touches
`lua/louiselm/skills/`. Surfaced because the notification appeared in the
snacks notifier history while verifying an unrelated case.

Real environment: root `~/.config/agentskills/generated`, 35 skills discovered,
31 diagnostics. All but one are the same warning:

```
⚠️ /home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/bvr/target: symlink resolves outside
   configured root: .../bvr/target -> /home/lotso/code/beads_viewer_rust/target
⚠️ /home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/bvr/.git: symlink resolves outside
   configured root: .../bvr/.git -> /home/lotso/code/beads_viewer_rust/.git
⚠️ /home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/br/references: symlink resolves outside
   configured root: ... -> /home/lotso/code/beads_rust/.claude/skills/br/references
   ... 27 more of the same shape
⚠️ /home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/lightweight-charts/SKILL.md: SKILL.md
   exceeds 500 lines
```

Only the last is a real authoring problem. The other 30 describe the layout
working as intended.

Measured, in-process, with the user's real config:

```
discover({generated}) -> 381 ms, 35 skills, 31 diagnostics   (361 ms on a warm second run)
discover({generated/bvr}) alone -> 376 ms
```

The `bvr` subtree accounts for essentially the whole cost. Directory counts
explain why:

```
find -L ~/.config/agentskills/generated -type d   -> 3133
find    ~/code/beads_viewer_rust/target -type d   ->  2839   (91%)
find    ~/code/beads_viewer_rust/.git   -type d   ->   173
```

`bvr`'s skill directory is a symlink to an entire Rust repository, so discovery
descends into `target/`, `.git/`, `benches/`, `tests/`, and
`legacy_beads_viewer_code/` looking for `SKILL.md` files that cannot be there.

## Symptoms

- A notification on every session start: "louiselm: skill discovery found 31
  issue(s); run :checkhealth louiselm for details", on an installation with
  nothing wrong with it.
- `:checkhealth louiselm` reports 31 warnings, 30 of them noise, which buries
  the one real finding (an oversized SKILL.md).
- ~380 ms of startup spent walking build artifacts.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:205-217` (directory branch) and `:218-229`
(SKILL.md branch). For a symlinked directory:

```lua
if entry.type == "link" and not is_within(canonical, canonical_root) then
  warn_outside_root(diagnostics, alias, canonical)
end
...
directories[#directories + 1] = alias   -- queued regardless
```

The escape check has no effect on control flow. It emits a diagnostic and the
directory is queued for scanning on the next line. So the warning neither
prevents traversal nor protects anything — it is a note about a situation the
code then proceeds into. There is also no prune list, so `.git`, `target`,
`node_modules` and similar are walked like any other directory.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/skills_spec.lua` has 27 cases and builds its fixtures inside a temp root,
so every symlink it creates either stays within the root or is deliberately
pointed outside to assert the warning fires. No fixture models the shape that
matters here: a symlink to a large real repository, where the warning is
correct in the letter and useless in practice. The suite asserts the diagnostic
is produced; it cannot assert that producing it 30 times is bad. Cost and
signal-to-noise are not properties a unit test was ever going to see.

## Fix direction

The decision is what "outside the root" should mean, and it is a decision, not
a lookup:

1. **Warn once per root, not per entry.** Smallest change; collapses 30
   diagnostics to one. Does nothing about the 380 ms.
2. **Do not descend into symlinks that leave the root** — make the check
   load-bearing, and record the skill by its alias without walking its
   subtree. Fixes both symptoms, but changes behaviour for anyone relying on a
   symlinked subdirectory *containing* a nested skill.
3. **Prune known non-skill directories** (`.git`, `target`, `node_modules`,
   `_build`) regardless of symlink status. Orthogonal to the above and worth
   doing either way; it is the part with no behavioural downside.
4. **Stop treating an out-of-root symlink as a problem at all**, and drop the
   warning. Defensible: the roots are user-configured, so a symlink escaping
   one is the user's own arrangement, not an attack.

Recommend 3 plus 1: prune the obvious build directories, and collapse the
warning to one per root. That removes the noise and most of the cost without
changing which skills are discoverable, which is the property most likely to
break someone's setup silently.

Rejected: leaving it and telling users to restructure their skills directory.
The layout here is stow, which is the normal way these trees are built.

## Acceptance

- A stow-style layout with every skill symlinked out of the root produces zero
  warnings, or one per root, rather than one per symlinked subdirectory.
- `discover()` on this user's real root completes in well under 380 ms, with a
  test fixture that includes a symlink to a directory containing a large
  non-skill subtree.
- The oversized-SKILL.md warning remains visible instead of being buried.

## Not covered

- Whether any real skill relies on a nested skill inside a symlinked
  subdirectory is unverified; option 2 would break that case.
- Timings are warm-cache on one machine; cold-cache cost is unmeasured and will
  be worse.
- The `lightweight-charts` SKILL.md exceeding 500 lines is a genuine, separate
  authoring issue in the user's own skills, not a louiselm defect.
close_reason: Pruned non-skill build trees and collapsed layout diagnostics per root; real discovery is ~20x faster with genuine warnings visible.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Post-prune measurement on the current real root: 23.0 ms cold-ish / 17.9 ms warm, 35 skills preserved (down from 381/361 ms), but diagnostics remain 31. Breakdown is now 29 healthy `.system/*` canonical-directory alias warnings, 1 out-of-root warning, and the genuine 500-line warning. Therefore pruning solves cost but not signal-to-noise. The same per-root collapse must cover traversal-layout diagnostics (outside symlinks, repeated canonical directories/cycles, and repeated canonical skill files), while configured duplicate roots and metadata warnings remain independent.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Fixed with the recommended narrow behavior: discovery prunes `.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, and `_build` subtrees unless the directory itself is a direct skill, and emits at most one traversal-layout warning per configured root across external symlinks, canonical aliases, duplicate skill files, and cycles. TDD fixture failed first by discovering a hidden target/SKILL.md and later by emitting a second canonical-alias warning; both pass after implementation, including a direct skill named target. Real-root verification preserves 35 skills, drops 381/361 ms to 22.5/17.3 ms, and drops diagnostics 31 -> 2 (one aggregate layout warning plus the genuine >500-line warning). Tests: focused 39/39 and full MiniTest 312/312 pass; changed-file StyLua and git diff --check pass. Whole-tree StyLua/LuaLS still fail only on pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua (louiselm-d7l; 9 LuaLS warnings there, none elsewhere).

title: Cursor lands before, not after, an automatically-queued context chip
description:
Any queued chat context — the automatic skill-catalog injection
(`skills.policy = "inject"`) or the new project-instructions
resource_link (louiselm-ce6.20) — left the cursor stuck at the
pre-chip column instead of after the newly written chip, so a user
landing on a fresh session's prompt line and starting to type
immediately typed in the middle of the `[context: ...]` marker
instead of after it.

## Observed

Live user report during manual QA of louiselm-ce6.20 (case 2, "visible
context chip on a brand-new session"): opened `:LouiselmNewSession`
with `context.instructions_file = "AGENTS.md"` configured; the
`[context: AGENTS.md]` chip appeared correctly, but the cursor sat
before it, not after.

Reproduced and captured as a failing test before the fix
(`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, case "positions the cursor after queued
context, not before it"):

```
Cause: different values at key 2, left = 1, right = 27
Left:  { 6, 1 }
Right: { 6, 27 }
```

`{6, 1}` is the stale cursor left over from `Chat:attach`'s initial
placement; `{6, 27}` is where it needs to be — end of the rewritten
prompt line, past the chip.

## Symptoms

- User types into a brand-new session with automatic context queued
  (skill catalog inject, or instructions resource_link) and the first
  keystrokes land inside the `[context: ...] ` marker instead of after
  it, corrupting the visible chip and/or the intended prompt text.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`: `Chat:attach` sets the cursor once,
unconditionally, to `{prompt_line + 1, 2}` (`ui/chat/init.lua:1441`,
right after `"> "`). `Chat:new_session` then queues any automatic
context (skill_context, and now instructions_context) via the local
`queue_context` function (`~ui/chat/init.lua:557` before the fix)
*after* `attach` returns. `queue_context` rewrites the prompt line to
prepend `"[context: <label>] "` via `set_line`, but never repositioned
the cursor — so it stayed at the column `attach` left it at,
regardless of how long the newly prepended chip text was.

## Why it was not caught

The automated test that exercises this exact call path
(`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, "queues context items as ACP text before
the user prompt") asserts buffer *line content* only, never cursor
position — a passing content assertion gives no signal about where
the cursor ends up. No existing test checked `nvim_win_get_cursor`
after `queue_context`; the one test that does check cursor
("focuses the prompt") only covers the pre-context `attach` state.

## Fix direction

Narrowest correct fix: in `queue_context`, after `set_line`, when the
chat buffer is the current buffer, call
`nvim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { view.prompt_line + 1, 2 + #view.context_prefix })`
— i.e. reposition to just past the full accumulated chip prefix. This
covers every caller of `queue_context` (automatic injection at
`new_session` time and any manual `Chat:queue_context` call from a
picker), not just the new instructions_context path.

## Acceptance

- `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`: "positions the cursor after queued
  context, not before it" — fails before the fix (`{6,1}` vs expected
  `{6,27}`), passes after.
- Full suite green: 267/267 mini.test cases.
- `stylua --check` and `lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning`
  clean on `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` and
  `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`.

## Not covered

Not yet committed as of filing — fix is staged in the working tree
alongside this bead. Manual QA case 2 (louiselm-ce6.20 round) still
needs to be re-run by the user against the fixed build to confirm the
interactive fix (only the mini.test harness's clamped-cursor proxy has
been verified so far, per the headless-mode caveat in the test's own
comment).
close_reason: Fixed in e15a846. queue_context now repositions the cursor to just past the full context_prefix after rewriting the prompt line. Confirmed live by user in session claude/8fe8fd28-ac0c-4293-bc77-5fc605d432ea: cursor lands after the [context: AGENTS.md] chip on a brand-new session, as expected. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'positions the cursor after queued context, not before it'. Gates: full suite 267/267, stylua --check and lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning clean.

title: Answering a diff review no longer returns to the previous buffer
description:
Regression introduced by the BufWipeout handler in 0ed18d0. Accepting or rejecting a review left the user in whatever buffer Neovim picked after the wipe instead of the chat.

clear() in lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua read self.previous_buffer AFTER calling Buffer.close(buffer). nvim_buf_delete runs BufWipeout synchronously, and that handler clears every field including previous_buffer, so clear() then saw nil and skipped nvim_set_current_buf.

Found by manual QA (case 3, session ade1d689-6c62-4753-ad00-4c78c995b1ef): the edit was allowed and applied correctly, but the chat buffer never came back.

Fixed by reading every field before closing the buffer. Regression test: tests/ui/diff_spec.lua "returns to the buffer focused before the review".
close_reason: Fixed in 348c6fc. Regression test added; full suite 201 cases, stylua and lua-language-server clean.

title: blog/scripts/render-post.sh: batch-render nvim-transcript excerpts to namespaced HTML/CSS
description:
## Goal
A batch script that renders every literalinclude block tagged :class: nvim-transcript in a finished post through the author's real Neovim config into namespaced HTML fragments, so the blog theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/scripts/render-post.sh <post-dir>. Parses blog.md for code blocks tagged nvim-transcript, extracts the referenced source file + :lines: range for each, opens the author's real Neovim config headlessly (not nvim --clean) once for the whole batch, renders each excerpt (via TOhtml / tohtml.tohtml()), extracts only the <pre> fragment and generated CSS from each, namespaces every generated selector under a wrapper class, deduplicates the CSS into one shared stylesheet file, writes fragment HTML files into the post directory.
- Out of scope: any MyST build-time plugin (rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design — not invoked from myst build/myst start); any interactive/visual-selection preview UX (explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is how line ranges get picked).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a blog.md with one or more nvim-transcript-tagged blocks, running the script produces one HTML fragment per block and one shared namespaced CSS file.
2. Generated CSS selectors are scoped under a wrapper class (e.g. .Comment becomes .nvim-transcript .Comment) — verified selectors cannot affect anything outside that wrapper.
3. Running the script twice against unchanged input is idempotent: byte-identical output both times.
4. The author's actual Neovim config (Catppuccin colorscheme, Tree-sitter highlighting) is what produces the rendering — not a generic/default Neovim config.

## Testing
- Focused test on the CSS-namespacing step: given sample TOhtml output, assert every generated selector is correctly prefixed.
- Idempotency test: run twice against the same fixture post, diff the outputs, assert no difference.
- No UI/buffer testing needed — headless tooling only.

## Notes
- Flagged in the parent feature as the highest-risk piece of this decomposition — may reasonably exceed typical task size given TOhtml extraction, CSS parsing/rewriting, and batch orchestration are all part of one coherent capability.
- No dependency on the other tasks — testable against hand-crafted fixture conversation files and a fixture blog.md, independent of create-blog.sh or LouiselmToMarkdown.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
close_reason: render-post.sh/render-post.mjs implemented and covered by 20/20 passing tests in test-render-post.sh (fragment content matches real TOhtml capture, idempotency across fragments/blog.md/myst.yml, cleanup on block removal, and a real 'myst build --html --strict' regression test proving the fragment is wired into the deployed page). Note: original AC #1/#2 (shared namespaced CSS file) were superseded per louiselm-xrf's investigation -- MyST's HTML build has no raw-HTML passthrough, so delivery moved to per-excerpt standalone documents via {iframe}, which makes CSS-selector namespacing unnecessary since each iframe already isolates its own styling. That supersession is documented and closed under louiselm-xrf. AC #4 (real Neovim config, Catppuccin/Tree-sitter) verified by test part 1's independent TOhtml capture comparison.

title: Separate the first assistant output from the user blockquote
description:
## Problem
The first assistant output after a submitted prompt is not visually separated from the user turn and can inherit the pink Markdown blockquote styling. This makes the first commentary and following tool-call line look like part of the user message.

## Reproduction
1. Open a LouiseLM chat buffer and submit a prompt.
2. Have the agent emit a text chunk as its first event, followed by a tool call.
3. Observe the boundary between the final line of the `> ` user prompt and the initial assistant commentary/tool timeline.

## Observed
- The initial assistant commentary begins immediately below the user prompt with no blank separator.
- The first tool-call line follows inside the same visually pink region.
- In `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png`, lines 4 onward initially appear attached to the user turn and inherit its pink presentation.

## Expected
Every assistant turn begins as a visually distinct transcript block. Assistant commentary and tool-call lines must not inherit the user prompt blockquote styling, regardless of which event arrives first.

## Likely Root Cause
`Chat:submit()` creates a single empty response placeholder immediately after the `> ` prompt. The first `chunk` event replaces that placeholder with response text instead of preserving a blank turn separator. With the chat buffer using Markdown filetype, text directly following a blockquote can be parsed as a lazy continuation, so the initial assistant content and adjacent tool-call lines inherit the blockquote highlight. This is a rendering-boundary issue; do not special-case tool colors unless investigation disproves it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A blank separator remains between each submitted user blockquote and the first assistant transcript content.
2. Initial assistant text and tool-call lines render outside the user blockquote/pink region.
3. The boundary is correct when the first event is a text chunk, tool call, error, or other transcript-producing event.
4. Streaming multiple chunks and updating a started tool call in place do not accumulate extra blank lines or disturb chronological order.
5. Existing prompt placement, cursor behavior, and subsequent-turn rendering remain unchanged.
6. Add a headless behavioral regression test that asserts the buffer lines for a submitted prompt followed by asynchronously scheduled chunk and tool events; exercise the real scheduling boundary rather than only invoking the renderer synchronously.

## Notes
Fix the shared transcript/turn boundary rather than applying presentation logic to one tool-call event. Buffer-line behavior is the primary assertion; no pixel test is required.
close_reason: Preserved assistant turn boundary before first streamed text or tool event

title: Collapse tool-call blocks in LouiselmToMarkdown transcript rendering
description:
## Goal
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` / `Chat:to_markdown` tool-call blocks take up huge vertical space (full `vim.inspect` dump always expanded) and visually compete with `## User`/`## Assistant` at the same heading weight. Make tool-call blocks compact and collapsed by default, without dropping any information.

## Scope
- In scope: `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` — `render_entry()` and its module doc comment (the "M.render turns a snapshot..." section describing tool block format).
- In scope: `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` — update the four assertions that do `markdown:find("## Tool: ...", 1, true)` to match the new multi-line shape.
- Out of scope: `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1549) and `transcript_export.lua` — both just call `Transcript.render`, no changes needed, no API change.
- Out of scope: fixing any blog-pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, MyST `:lines:` literalinclude ranges) friction this causes — explicitly deferred, see Notes.

## Agreed format (discussed with user)
Replace the current single line:
```
## Tool: <title> (<status>)

```
<vim.inspect dump>
```
```
with:
```
## Tool

<sub>**<title>** — <status></sub>

<details>
<summary>payload</summary>

```
<vim.inspect dump, unchanged>
```

</details>
```
- `## Tool` stays its own heading, same weight as `## User`/`## Assistant`.
- Title/status move to a `<sub>` line — smaller, one line, no expansion needed to see what ran.
- The full raw payload dump is unchanged in content, just wrapped in `<details><summary>payload</summary>...</details>` so it renders collapsed by default in GitHub/VS Code/Obsidian (falls back to expanded, not lost, in renderers without HTML passthrough).
- Fallback cases (`raw.title` absent → id, `raw.status` absent → "unknown") keep working the same way, just placed in the `<sub>` line instead of the heading.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `render_entry()` for a `tool_call` entry produces the new `## Tool` / `<sub>` / `<details>` shape described above, with the full `vim.inspect(raw)` dump byte-for-byte unchanged inside the `<details>` block.
2. `## User` and `## Assistant` blocks are unchanged.
3. `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` assertions updated to match (still checking title/status and full raw dump presence, just via the new shape — e.g. assert the `<sub>` line and `<details>`/`<summary>` markers appear, and the dump content is still present).
4. `busted`/test suite passes (`make test` or repo's standard Lua test runner).
5. Module doc comment in `transcript.lua` (lines ~19-24) updated to describe the new tool-block format instead of the old one-line heading.

## Testing
- Run existing Lua test suite for `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` (and `tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua`, `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` as regression checks — they should not need format-specific changes since they likely just check the file was written, but verify).

## Notes
- Risk, explicitly accepted by user: `transcript.lua's doc comment says this markdown format is a dependency of the blog-publishing pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, feature `louiselm-mia`), which uses MyST `{literalinclude}` with `:lines: N-M` ranges against these exported files. Adding multi-line `<sub>`/`<details>` markup shifts line numbers for any existing blog post literalinclude ranges pointed at old-format transcripts. User: "happy with both, it's alpha software so I'll fix it after if that creates friction with louiselm-mia." Do not attempt to fix the blog pipeline as part of this task — file a separate bug if/when it actually breaks something.

Updated tests/session/transcript_spec.lua and tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua assertions. All 3 quality gates pass: stylua --check clean, lua-language-server --check clean, full mini.test suite 235/235 (0 fails). title: Resumed sessions drop the user's own messages from the transcript
description:
After :LouiselmResume the chat shows the agent replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but none of the user prompts, so a resumed session reads as one-sided and anything the user wrote — a session id, a decision, a constraint — is invisible.

## Observed

Session claude/fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695, resumed 2026-08-17 08:50.

~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260817-085040-286753-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log replays both prompts before the session/load result:

  line 1  user_message_chunk  "commit and sync, those skills addition have been performed in claude/71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea"
  line 24 user_message_chunk  "sorry redo it i miscliked"
  line 37 session result for fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695

Neither line appeared in the resumed chat buffer. The text is intact in ~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-dotfiles-nvim--config-nvim/fa72dc03-....jsonl, so nothing is lost upstream; only the client drops it.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_notification dispatches update types at lines 184-209: agent_message_chunk, tool_call, tool_call_update, config_option_update, usage_update. user_message_chunk matches nothing and falls through silently.

claude-agent-acp is launched with --replay-user-messages, so the replay is expected behavior of the agent, not a quirk.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua "renders replayed assistant chunks before a new prompt" covers the resume path but only asserts the agent side, so the missing half of the conversation is invisible to it.

## Fix direction

Handle user_message_chunk and render it as a user prompt line in the transcript.

Check whether the chunk arrives outside replay before deciding where to render. Evidence so far: across every stored adapter log, user_message_chunk appears only in logs that include a session/load replay - claude, codex and the deepseek adapter all behave this way, and live turns in the same logs never emit it. If an agent does echo the prompt during a live turn, the chat would double-render it, because the chat writes the submitted prompt into the buffer itself.

## Acceptance

- A resumed session shows the user prompts interleaved with the agent replies in their original order.
- Submitting a prompt in a live turn still renders it exactly once.
- A chat_spec case asserts a replayed user chunk reaches the buffer.

## Not covered

Whether replayed prompts should be visually distinguished from newly typed ones, and whether replayed tool calls should be folded, are UX questions left open.
close_reason: Resumed user prompts now render in original order before replayed assistant replies; red-green UI regression coverage and full suite pass.

title: Write the political statement document
description:
Write the political statement document.

The licence deliberately carries no politics — that was the whole point of choosing MIT for reach. Which means this document carries all of it. Without it the position is invisible.

## What it should say

- Why the licence is permissive: reach is the mechanism. A harness's effect comes from being everywhere and shaping how human-agent work happens — local-first, legible, owned by the operator. Every install is a small decommodification of the means of producing software.
- What is retained and why: trademark, patents, and the right to relicense. Not granted away, and named as deliberate.
- What is refused: the named class, enforced through the trademark policy.
- The community position: AI removed the need to depend on other people for code, which is what used to create open-source community. The scarce contribution now is workflows, evidence, and judgment — which is what `CONTRIBUTING.md` already asks for. Community here forms around decisions, not patches.
- Honest about the limit: no licence ends anything. What a licence decides is who captures the surplus, and whether the tool spreads. Claiming more would be flattery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document exists, linked from README.
- Nothing in it reads as a licence term or a condition of use. It is a statement, not an obligation — that separation is the point.
- The reasoning is legible to someone who did not sit through the original session.
close_reason: Completed political statement and README link; documentary verification passed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Implemented POLITICAL_STATEMENT.md and linked it from README.md. The statement separates project intent from licence terms, explains reach as the permissive-licence mechanism, identifies retained trademark/patent/future-release leverage, states the structural named-class mark refusal, reframes community around workflows/evidence/judgment, and names the limits of licensing. Documentary verification: git diff --check passed; local Markdown targets POLITICAL_STATEMENT.md and CONTRIBUTING.md exist; no contradictory perpetual-open-source promise found.
