title: LouiseLM attention control plane: ideas into reality
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arrive faster than sustained human attention can evaluate and realize them. Existing agent tools automate isolated conversations and coding turns but do not make the whole workflow, its authority boundaries, or its human-attention gates observable.

## Solution

Build LouiseLM as an attention control plane that turns ideas into reality. It makes workflow topology explicit, automates work agents can safely perform, and surfaces only decisions where human judgment materially improves or unblocks the outcome. LouiseLM ships an explicit software-delivery reference preset while allowing other workflows to configure different stages and resolvers.

The first active vertical slice is durable speech capture from Android and Neovim into one local Linux inbox. Later idea modelling, triage, workflow history, attention visualization, sequential orchestration, and parallel workers remain dependency-shaped deferred features.

## Implementation Decisions

- Human attention is assigned per transition, never by one global human-or-agent rule.
- Declarative validated topology describes stages, transitions, triggers, and resolvers; typed providers perform effects.
- Raw capture is immutable and local-first. Android and Neovim speech are the first bundled capture providers.
- Neovim is the cockpit; a narrow Rust user service owns durable capture ingestion and transcription while the editor is closed.
- The reference workflow is triage -> human/agent grill -> automatic plan and critique -> tracker DAG -> policy-controlled execution -> automated evidence -> human outcome acceptance.
- Logical workflow threads outlive replaceable ACP sessions and preserve decisions, supersessions, questions, evidence, and handoffs.
- The live idea journey and its expanding task DAG are the primary visualization. Human gates are visually distinct.
- Beads is the tracker in the reference preset, not a core dependency or a second implementation inside LouiseLM.
- Sequential execution precedes the committed parallel-worker milestone.

## Testing Decisions

Each executable boundary has deterministic tests. The capture milestone additionally requires a physical Android-to-Linux-to-Neovim dogfood test and explicit human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

The first slice does not implement semantic idea segmentation, triage actions, workflow orchestration, graph UI, or parallel workers. Those remain visible deferred children with evidence-based entry criteria.

title: Durable speech capture from Android and Neovim
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arising away from the keyboard are currently kept in memory or Gmail drafts and can be lost. Capture must be faster than classification and must not require Neovim to remain open.

## Solution

Record short speech streams from Android and Neovim, preserve the original audio in a local Linux inbox, transcribe asynchronously, and expose quiet durable status in Neovim. Android saves first and syncs later; no project, title, or priority is requested during capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Multiple rapid Android recordings survive offline use, app exit, restart, upload retry, and duplicate delivery.
2. Android pairs to a Linux receiver using pinned TLS and a scoped revocable device credential.
3. Neovim records through a validated external command and ingests through the same capture contract.
4. Original audio and successful transcript are retained indefinitely by default and are never silently rewritten or deleted.
5. The Linux service transcribes with an explicitly configured provider while Neovim is closed.
6. A physical-phone gardening journey reaches the Neovim inbox without loss and receives human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Semantic idea extraction, triage, workflow topology, task planning, agent orchestration, graph UI, hosted sync, and local Whisper tuning.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
**Candidate requirement for this issue's design — not a settled decision.**

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should
default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even
when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human
operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot
express.

**Evidence.** `bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum over eight components.
Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for
`in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight. A
fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus
a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic
comfortably. Measured in this repo: a two-paragraph policy doc scored ~0.459
against ~0.405 for an in-progress epic covering an entire ACP client.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix this. `priority-first` raises
Urgency only to ~0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file.
So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration. It has to be
applied on top of its output — which is why it belongs in the engine that
consumes that output rather than in the scorer.

The sequencing policy is this issue's to define. This comment records why the
question exists and what the evidence was, so the design conversation does not
have to re-derive it.

title: render-post fragments are not byte-identical across runs; CSS rule order varies
description:
`render-post.sh` documents its output as "a pure function of the current input"
and promises that "running twice against unchanged input is byte-identical".
It is not. Ten consecutive runs against identical input, in an identical
environment, produced four distinct fragment files. The difference is CSS rule
ordering, so the rendered page is unaffected — but the contract is false and
the test that claims to check it passes anyway.

## Observed

Found by QA case 9 of the round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, on build `daf3dfc`,
2026-08-20. Real post, real conversation excerpt (`:lines: 1481-1522`).

`blog.md` and `myst.yml` are byte-identical across runs. The fragment is not:

```
run  1  942aeb6aa0d2bbc13473e42d635ea066
run  2  b357a62c877f12da018565305d648c68
run  3  b357a62c877f12da018565305d648c68
run  4  07d64a69bd68ef675f020bcacd527080
run  5  5e4da75d9e1bbcd9942792ffa7a53d1e
...
```

Four distinct outputs across ten runs. Not environment-dependent — holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it:

```
TERM=dumb run 1  5e4da75d
TERM=dumb run 2  942aeb6a
TERM=dumb run 3  5e4da75d
```

The whole diff between two variants:

```
10d9
< .-conceal {}
12a12
> .-conceal {}
16a17
> .-markup-strong {color: #e78284; font-weight: bold}
18d18
< .-markup-strong {font-weight: bold; color: #e78284}
```

Rule order within the `<style>` block, and property order within a rule. The
`<pre>` markup is identical every time; the CSS is semantically identical every
time.

## Symptoms

- Re-rendering an unchanged post rewrites its fragment with different bytes.
- Fragments are written into the post directory and referenced from
  `myst.yml` `static_files`, so they are committed alongside a post — every
  re-render therefore dirties the working tree with a semantically null diff.
- No visual difference. The published page is correct in every variant.

## Root cause

Neovim's `:TOhtml` builds its `<style>` block by iterating the highlight groups
it collected with `pairs()`, whose order is unspecified in Lua and varies
between processes. `render-post.mjs` extracts that block verbatim
(`extractTagBlock`, then `buildFragmentDoc`), by design — `render-post.sh`'s
header states the style and `<pre>` are taken "unmodified (no selector
rewriting)".

So the non-determinism originates upstream in `tohtml.lua`, and this pipeline
faithfully preserves it. The real excerpt produces 11 rules
(`.-spell .-conceal .-nospell .-none .-markup-raw .rainbow2 .Whitespace
.Special .-tag-delimiter .-markup-strong .-tag`), which is enough for the
ordering to vary.

## Why it was not caught

`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh` part 2 does exactly the right check —
`diff -rq "$run1_dir" "$run2_dir"` over fragments, `blog.md` and `myst.yml`.
It passes because its fixture is too small to expose the bug: the excerpts are
`:lines: 9-12` and `:lines: 16-20` of a hand-written fixture transcript that is
plain prose plus a two-line shell block and a three-line Lua snippet. That
yields a handful of highlight groups, and with few enough rules the iteration
order does not visibly change. The assertion is sound; the fixture is not
representative.

This is the same fixture-scale gap as louiselm-msg (skills discovery) and
louiselm-cmr (single-line tool titles): invented fixtures are well-behaved in
exactly the dimension the real data is not.

## Fix direction

There is a genuine conflict here, which is why this is filed rather than
patched.

Sorting the CSS is the obvious fix — normalise rule order and property order in
`render-post.mjs` before `buildFragmentDoc`. But `test-render-post.sh` part 1
asserts that the fragment's embedded `<style>`/`<pre>` match an *independent*
TOhtml capture byte-for-byte, and that capture would be unsorted. Sorting
therefore breaks part 1 unless part 1 normalises identically — at which point
"byte-for-byte against a real TOhtml capture", the property part 1 exists to
protect, is weakened to "byte-for-byte after our own normalisation".

Options, none free:

1. Sort in `render-post.mjs`, and normalise part 1's comparison the same way.
   Deterministic output; part 1 becomes a slightly weaker guarantee.
2. Sort in `tohtml-driver.lua` before the raw capture is written, so both the
   pipeline and part 1's independent capture see sorted input. Keeps part 1
   byte-exact against what the driver produces, but the driver is then no
   longer a transparent TOhtml wrapper.
3. Weaken the documented contract to semantic rather than byte equality, and
   compare parsed rule sets in part 2. Honest, but gives up the cheap
   `diff -rq` check and the "pure function of input" claim.
4. Fix upstream in Neovim's `tohtml.lua` and pin a version. Correct, slowest,
   outside this repo.

Recommend 1: it puts the normalisation where the pipeline already takes
responsibility for assembling the document, and the weakening of part 1 is
small and explicit. Whatever is chosen, `render-post.sh`'s header must stop
claiming byte-identical output until it is true.

## Acceptance

- Ten consecutive runs against unchanged input produce ten identical
  fragments.
- `test-render-post.sh` part 2's fixture is enlarged until it produces enough
  highlight groups to have caught this — otherwise the same gap remains.
- `render-post.sh`'s header contract matches the implemented behaviour.

## Not covered

- Whether `.rainbow2` and similar plugin-provided groups make the group set
  itself vary between runs (as opposed to only its order) is unverified; every
  observed variant had the same 11 rules, but that is 10 samples.
- Neovim's `tohtml.lua` has not been read to confirm `pairs()` specifically;
  the unspecified-order conclusion is inferred from the symptom.

title: Private blog-publishing pipeline for louiselm session transcripts
description:
## Problem Statement

Turning an interesting agent conversation into a blog post currently requires manual, repetitive steps: copying chat buffer text by hand into a markdown file (lossy — collapses tool calls to one-line summaries, truncates commands and output), hand-building a MyST project from scratch, and no way to render a quoted excerpt with the same Neovim/Catppuccin/Tree-sitter styling the author actually saw, while keeping the rest of the post in a separate blog theme.

## Solution

A private, louiselm-adjacent publishing pipeline for turning louiselm session transcripts into blog posts. One real plugin command (LouiselmToMarkdown) exports a session's full structured transcript (not a lossy buffer scrape) to markdown. A blog/ directory at the repo root (sibling to android/ and capture-service/, not documented as a plugin feature) holds a multi-post MyST site plus two private scripts: one scaffolds a new post (optionally auto-exporting named sessions into it), the other batch-renders every excerpt a finished post quotes through the author's real Neovim config into scoped, dual-theme-safe HTML fragments, ready for a plain myst build with zero Neovim dependency in CI.

## User Stories

1. As the author, I want to export any louiselm session's full transcript to markdown from its structured JSONL data (not the truncated chat buffer), so quoting a conversation in a post does not require re-digging through raw logs.
2. As the author, I want to scaffold a new post directory in one command, so starting a post from "I want to blog about lines X-Y in session A and lines Z-W in session B" does not require manually creating folders.
3. As the author, I want that scaffold command to optionally take session ids and auto-export plus auto-stub a literalinclude block for each, so the moment scaffolding finishes, every source I named is already present and ready to quote from.
4. As the author, I want a single batch step that renders every nvim-transcript-tagged excerpt in a finished post through my real Neovim config (Catppuccin, Tree-sitter) into namespaced HTML+CSS, so the published transcript looks exactly like what I saw on screen, without polluting the blog's own theme.
5. As the author, I want the rendered output committed and CI to just run myst build with no Neovim dependency, so publishing does not require reproducing my personal editor setup inside a CI container.
6. As the author, I want the finished site published at blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages from this same repo, so there is no second repo to maintain for a workflow that is fundamentally "I am already in louiselm."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a louiselm session id, running LouiselmToMarkdown produces a markdown file containing the full transcript reconstructed from the session's structured JSONL (full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries).
2. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name>, a blog/post-<name>/ directory is created containing an empty blog.md and an empty conversations/ folder.
3. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name> <session-id>..., the same scaffold is created, conversations/<session-id>.md exists for each session id (via the same export path as LouiselmToMarkdown), and blog.md contains one literalinclude block per session pointing at its exported file.
4. Given a blog.md with one or more code blocks tagged :class: nvim-transcript, running the batch render script produces fragment HTML for each block plus one shared, namespaced CSS file, using the author's real Neovim config — and running it again is idempotent (safe to re-run after editing line ranges).
5. Given the rendered fragments are committed, myst build --html succeeds using only MyST and Node — no Neovim process is spawned during the build.
6. The GitLab CI pipeline in this repo builds and deploys blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages on push, without requiring Neovim in the CI image.

## Implementation Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown follows the existing Louiselm* command registration pattern (alongside LouiselmResume, LouiselmSessionId, etc. in the chat command module) and reads from the same structured session/transcript data those commands already have access to, not the rendered chat buffer.
- blog/ is a new top-level directory, siblings android/ and capture-service/ — precedent already exists in this repo for non-Neovim-plugin material living alongside lua/.
- The scaffold and render scripts are plain shell/Node scripts under blog/scripts/, not Neovim commands — this tooling is intentionally not part of the plugin's discoverable command surface.
- The render script needs to invoke the author's real Neovim configuration headlessly (not nvim --clean) to get accurate Catppuccin/Tree-sitter output — reusing whatever TOhtml/tohtml.tohtml() wrapper already exists or building a minimal one.
- CSS namespacing (scoping generated Neovim highlight-group classes under a wrapper class) is required so the blog's own theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.
- MyST config (blog/myst.yml, blog/blog.css) should be structured as a real multi-post project from the start, not a single-page site — a second post is expected.

## Testing Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown output should be tested against a fixture session JSONL, asserting full tool commands/results appear (not truncated).
- The scaffold script's directory-creation and auto-stub behavior can be tested as a plain shell/script test (given a fake session export, assert the resulting blog.md contents).
- The render script's CSS-namespacing step is the highest-risk piece — worth a focused test asserting generated selectors are correctly prefixed and that two renders of the same input are byte-identical (supports the idempotency acceptance criterion).
- No UI/Neovim-buffer testing needed — this is headless tooling.

## Out of Scope

- Writing the first post's prose, choosing excerpt line ranges, and designing blog.css's actual visual theme — tracked separately, not part of this feature.
- Any interactive/visual-selection tool for previewing excerpts while authoring (considered and explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is sufficient for picking line ranges).
- Any MyST build-time JS plugin that renders excerpts live during myst build/myst start — rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design, to avoid needing Neovim in CI.
- Deploying/configuring anything at the bartab.fr root domain — this feature only concerns the blog.bartab.fr subdomain.

title: Make skill discovery deterministic and symlink-aware
description:
## Goal

Discover local skills predictably across configured roots while preserving useful paths and diagnosing duplicates or unsafe-looking topology.

## Scope

- In scope: process global skill roots in configuration order; within each root sort deterministically by skill name and configured path.
- In scope: first valid duplicate skill name wins, later names are reported as shadowed, and the same canonical file is deduplicated.
- In scope: expand absolute paths and `~`; resolve relative roots against the session working directory. Health checks resolve them against Neovim's current working directory and say so.
- In scope: support symlinked roots and skill directories, detect canonical cycles/duplicates, preserve the configured-root alias in advertised absolute locations, and warn when a symlink resolves outside its root.
- In scope: continue past unreadable or invalid individual skills with one deduplicated user warning and full details available to diagnostics.
- In scope: refresh discovery whenever the picker opens and read the selected file at selection time.
- Out of scope: automatic project-local roots, a trust database, policy transport, and catalog budgeting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root order, not global absolute sorting, decides duplicate-name precedence.
2. Discovery order and diagnostics are stable across runs.
3. Canonical aliases do not create duplicate skills or traversal loops.
4. Catalog/picker locations preserve the user-configured alias rather than exposing a canonical dotfiles target.
5. Escapes outside a configured root remain usable but produce a source-to-target warning.
6. Relative-root behavior is covered for both sessions and checkhealth.
7. MiniTest covers duplicate names, identical canonical files, symlinked roots/directories, cycles, outside-root targets, unreadable files, and picker refresh behavior.

## Testing

Use temporary directory fixtures with real symlinks where supported. Keep path-policy tests separate from YAML semantic fixtures.

## Notes

Configured skill roots are trusted prompt/plugin-like input. Diagnostics inform the user; they do not create a new authorization system.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic root-order discovery, canonical symlink traversal and diagnostics, session-relative picker refresh, selection-time reads, and checkhealth coverage

title: Add README licence section framing the choice as serving reach
description:
Add a licence section to `README.md` that states the choice and the reasoning behind it.

## Content

- LouiseLM is MIT licensed.
- The licence is chosen to serve reach: the project's usefulness depends on being installable anywhere with no friction.
- If reach stops being the binding constraint, the choice will be revisited.
- Link to the trademark policy and the political statement.

## Why the last point matters

Publishing the expiry condition is what makes a future relicense a disclosed term rather than a rug-pull. It costs nothing now and is the difference between a relicense that is legitimate and one that is radioactive.

## Acceptance criteria

- README has a licence section containing all four points.
- Wording does not promise perpetuity, and does not read as a threat either.
- Links resolve.
close_reason: Published the complete README licensing posture with valid policy links.

title: Make the repo the substrate for cross-adapter agent context
description:
## Problem Statement

louiselm is an interface to ACP adapters, not a Claude-only tool. But the durable context an agent accumulates while working on this repo — conventions, design decisions, the maintainer's workflow — has been landing in Claude Code's private per-project memory store. Any other adapter reading this repo sees none of it.

The inverse failure exists too. `AGENTS.md` is the adapter-neutral instruction file, and it is not auto-loaded by Claude Code: there is no root `CLAUDE.md` and no setting pointing at it. So the repo currently has one context store that only Claude reads and one that Claude ignores, and neither is a shared substrate.

Concretely: `AGENTS.md` is 214 lines across 11 sections and does not mention beads once, even though beads is the task graph the whole project runs on. An agent entering this repo cold has no way to learn that findings should be filed as beads. Meanwhile five of seven notes in Claude's project memory are repo content that was misfiled there purely because it was the path of least resistance.

## Solution

Make the repository the substrate for durable agent context, and reduce per-adapter memory to only what is genuinely adapter-specific.

The routing rule, by two axes:

- **About louiselm, adapter-independent** → the repo.
- **About the maintainer, cross-project** → that adapter's own user-level instructions.
- **About one adapter's harness quirks** → that adapter's project memory. Applied honestly this is nearly empty, which is the correct outcome and not evidence the rule is wrong.

Within the repo, placement follows the anchor:

- Anchored to a specific work item → a `br` comment on that issue, so it travels with the issue and needs no separate discovery mechanism.
- A standing convention true for every session → `AGENTS.md`.
- The maintainer's own workflow loop → an explicitly non-binding example document.

`AGENTS.md` becomes the single entrypoint. Every adapter is pointed at it rather than given its own parallel instruction file, because parallel instruction files diverge silently and the divergence surfaces at the worst possible moment.

## User Stories

1. As an agent entering this repo through any ACP adapter, I want the work-tracking conventions stated in the file I already read on entry, so that I file findings as beads instead of inventing my own process.
2. As the maintainer, I want a decision recorded during a session to survive regardless of which adapter recorded it, so that switching adapters does not silently lose context.
3. As a contributor or agent, I want the maintainer's personal workflow clearly marked as an example rather than a requirement, so that I can invent my own loop without believing I am violating a contract.
4. As the maintainer, I want my own loop written down as prose now, so that the future workflow-config feature has a spec to implement against rather than being reconstructed from memory.
5. As an agent picking up a deferred issue months later, I want design context attached to that issue, so that I do not need the conversation that produced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a fresh clone opened by any adapter that reads `AGENTS.md`, when the agent reads it, then the beads work-tracking conventions are present and stated in the file's own imperative register.
2. Given Claude Code opening this repo, when it auto-loads project instructions, then it is directed to `AGENTS.md` and no instruction content exists outside it.
3. Given the example workflow document, when any reader reaches it, then it self-identifies as a non-binding example, and `AGENTS.md` says the same where it links out.
4. Given the deferred workflow-engine issues, when someone opens them, then the in-progress-first triage requirement is attached as a comment.
5. Given Claude's project memory folder, when it is inspected after migration, then it contains only genuinely Claude-specific harness notes, and every repo fact previously held there exists in the repo.
6. Given `AGENTS.md`, when the workflow section is read, then it references `br robot-docs` for command syntax rather than duplicating a command cheatsheet.

## Implementation Notes

- Affected: `AGENTS.md` (new section, renumbering), a new root `CLAUDE.md` pointer, a new example workflow document under `docs/`, `br` comments on the deferred workflow-engine issues, and Claude's project memory store.
- **Do not use `br agents --add`.** It emits roughly 60 lines of generic beads tutorial in a `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v1 -->` block. Three problems: the register clashes with `AGENTS.md`, which is terse and imperative; it teaches command syntax discoverable from `br --help` while saying nothing about this project's actual conventions; and hand-edits inside a versioned generated block are destroyed by `br agents --update`, so the conventions would live in the one place designed to be overwritten.
- The workflow section is inserted as section 2, immediately after Project Scope, not appended at the end. Reading order should be *what this project is* → *how work is found and tracked* → *how code must be written*, because an agent finds work before it writes any. Renumbering the existing sections is mechanical churn and acceptable; section 1 already states breaking changes are fine and there are no external users.
- The example document lives at a `docs/` path rather than root. A root-level uppercase filename reads as normative regardless of any disclaimer it carries, which is the precise misreading to avoid.
- The `CLAUDE.md` pointer must stay a pointer. Real content in it beside a real `AGENTS.md` guarantees drift.
- The example workflow document is the first draft of the workflow-config that louiselm intends to ship as an example. It should be written knowing that, without over-committing to a config schema that does not exist yet.

## Testing Notes

- No automated tests. Verification is documentary: read `AGENTS.md` top to bottom as if entering cold and confirm the work-tracking conventions are learnable; confirm the example document is unambiguously non-binding on first read.
- Confirm no instruction content is duplicated between `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
- Confirm nothing was lost in the memory migration by checking each migrated note has a repo destination.

## Out of Scope

- Cross-adapter portability of *session/conversation history*. That is a much larger problem already implied by the attention-control-plane roadmap, and is not solved as a side effect of relocating notes.
- Any wrapper script around `br`/`bv`, and any project-scoped skill override for them. Both were considered and rejected: they relocate a personal preference into the repo without it becoming a real louiselm capability.
- Building the workflow-config engine itself. This feature produces the prose spec, not the implementation.
- Resolving how completed QA review rounds get archived. Tracked separately; it wants full attention rather than being decided in passing.

title: Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads
description:
## Problem Statement

A `qa-review` round produces a working file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) that
accumulates the plan, case-by-case results, and narration for the round. When
the round ends, nothing decides what happens to that file — commit it, fold
it into beads, or delete it. This has now happened twice in a row
(transcript-export/blog-publishing round, then the permissions round), each
time ending with the same unresolved question and an untracked markdown file
left sitting in the repo root. Findings filed during a round (via
`to-beads-bug`, which already works correctly) also end up orphaned from the
round that produced them — nothing records which round found which bug.

Resolved via grill-me session against `louiselm-iyy`, which had a concrete
proposal already on record from an earlier session; this feature adopts that
proposal.

## Solution

A `qa-review` round closes into exactly one bead, which becomes the round's
sole durable record:

1. **One bead per round.** Type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file <working-file>` so the round's plan/results become the
   bead description, and `--external-ref <session-id>` so the round is tied
   to the session that ran it.
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** Continues using the existing,
   already-working `to-beads-bug` chain: `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>`. This makes "which round found this?" answerable from the
   graph.
3. **Cases stay flat.** Individual test cases inside the round are never
   promoted to their own beads — they aren't independently actionable, have
   no lifecycle of their own, and beading them would add ceremony for no
   graph benefit. Only findings (bugs) get promoted.
4. **Narration goes in `br comments add`** on the round bead as the round
   progresses, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit).
5. **On close, the round bead is authoritative.** The working markdown file
   is deleted, never committed — a second, uncommitted-but-lingering copy of
   the same round is exactly the failure this feature removes.
6. **The closing step is mandatory**, built into the `qa-review` skill
   itself as a defined step, not a manual call left to whoever is running the
   round. Two rounds in a row already skipped it by default; an optional step
   is not a fix.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer running a qa-review round, I want the round to close
   into a bead automatically, so that I don't have to remember to decide the
   working file's fate every time.
2. As an agent picking up a bug found during a past round, I want to see
   which round produced it, so that I have the round's full context without
   reconstructing it from a conversation.
3. As an agent or maintainer looking at repo history, I want closed rounds to
   be greppable via `br`/`bv`, so that "what did we test and find in round
   N" doesn't require finding an untracked file that may not exist anymore.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a qa-review round following the (updated) skill's closing step, when
   the round ends, then exactly one `chore`/`qa-round` bead exists with the
   round's plan/results as its description, `--external-ref` set to the
   session id, and the working markdown file is gone (not committed,
   deleted).
2. Given findings filed during a round, when the round closes, then each
   finding bead is a child of that round's bead (`--parent <round-id>`).
3. Given the `qa-review` skill's own instructions, when an agent reads them
   top to bottom, then the closing step reads as mandatory, not optional or
   merely suggested.
4. Given the two rounds currently sitting as untracked files in this repo
   (`QA_REVIEW.md`, `QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`), when this feature
   ships, then both have been retroactively closed under the new rule: round
   beads created, their already-filed findings re-parented under the correct
   round bead, and the two files deleted.

## Implementation Notes

- Skill file: `/home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/qa-review/SKILL.md`
  (and its `TEMPLATE.md`) — add the closing step here.
- `--external-ref` dovetails with the maintainer's existing global commit rule
  (`Refs <id>` for named sessions/issues in commit messages).
- The transcript-export/blog-publishing round's findings are:
  `louiselm-dim` (closed), `louiselm-euj` (open), `louiselm-d2o` (open),
  `louiselm-xrf` (open) — all currently un-parented, all belong under that
  round's bead.
- The permissions round (working file: `QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`,
  origin `louiselm-4wx`) reports "all six cases passed" with three
  in-round fixes (commits `a57cee2`, `348c6fc`, `c0ae0aa`) — check whether
  those fixes have their own bead IDs to re-parent, or whether the round bead
  is created with no open children if they were fixed without being filed
  separately.
- Convergence noted during the grill: the round bead becomes the index, an
  exported transcript (once the export pipeline is wired up) is the
  evidence, and a blog post is the human-readable version — reusing the
  transcript-export/blog-pipeline feature set for QA's own record-keeping.

## Testing Notes

- No automated test surface (this is a documentation/process change to a
  skill plus one-time data migration). Verification is documentary: read the
  updated `qa-review` skill cold and confirm the closing step is
  unambiguous, then confirm via `br show` that both retroactively-closed
  rounds have the right shape (round bead, parented findings, no stray file).

## Out of Scope

- The "maintainer's workflow as louiselm configuration" thread
  (workflow-config engine) — raised as bigger context during the grill but
  deliberately not pulled in here; it's a separate, much larger question.
- Rejected: keeping the working markdown file committed alongside the round
  bead as a second durable copy (two sources of truth for one round drift
  silently).
- Rejected: leaving the closing step optional/manual (the exact failure mode
  that produced this feature).
- Rejected: giving individual test cases their own child beads (not
  independently actionable, adds ceremony for no graph benefit).
close_reason: Both children complete. louiselm-ri1.1: qa-review skill now has a mandatory closing step (dotfiles commit 29e76e0). louiselm-ri1.2: both stray rounds retroactively closed into louiselm-vj0 and louiselm-aib, findings reparented, working files deleted.

title: Add mandatory closing step to the qa-review skill
description:
## What

Add a mandatory closing step to the `qa-review` skill
(`/home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/qa-review/SKILL.md`,
alongside `TEMPLATE.md`) that runs at the end of every round:

1. Create one bead: `br create -t chore --labels qa-round --description-file
   <working-file> --external-ref <session-id>`.
2. Re-parent (or newly create, if not yet filed) any findings from the round
   under that bead: `br create -t bug --parent <round-id>` for new findings;
   `br update <finding-id> --parent <round-id>` for findings already filed
   during the round.
3. Append round narration to the round bead via `br comments add` as the
   round progresses (not just at the end).
4. On close: delete the working markdown file. Never commit it.
5. State explicitly that individual test cases are never beaded — only
   findings are.

This step must read as required, not optional — the skill has twice let
rounds end without deciding the working file's fate.

## Why

Parent feature: louiselm-ri1. Full rationale, rejected alternatives, and
acceptance criteria live there — this task is the skill-file change only.

## Acceptance

- The `qa-review` skill's closing step is unambiguous on a cold read: an
  agent running a round for the first time reaches it and cannot mistake it
  for optional.
- `TEMPLATE.md` (if it currently ships a working-file template) reflects
  that the file is scratch, not a committed artifact.

title: Native skill picker never resolves against the real Claude ACP adapter (exact description match rejects its scope-annotation suffix)
description:
Native skill invocation via the picker never resolves against the real Claude Code ACP adapter, because Claude appends a scope annotation to every advertised command description and the correlation code requires exact equality.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 during a qa-review round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP command invocation, commit 763ba78), before any human test case was run -- by inspecting a pre-existing real ACP debug log on this machine (louiselm.nvim itself is run through claude-agent-acp for this very session).

Log: ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-100019-702281-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log, line 3 (session/update, sessionUpdate=available_commands_update). The "grill-me" entry:

  "name":"grill-me","description":"Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (user)","input":null

The local SKILL.md at ~/.config/agentskills/generated/grill-me/SKILL.md has description:

  Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

-- identical text, but the advertised one carries a trailing " (user)" that the local one does not.

Checked systematically: parsed all 76 entries in that available_commands_update payload. Every command whose name matches a configured local skill path (br, bvr, caveman, caveman-commit, caveman-help, caveman-review, grill-me, htmx, karpathy-guidelines, lightweight-charts, playwright-cli, playwright-qa-review, ponytail*, qa-review, rscss, rtk, rust-architecture, terraform-skill, to-beads*, write-a-skill -- 27 total) ends with " (user)". Claude's own built-in/plugin commands in the same payload (compact, config, model, doctor, mcp, loop, schedule, security-review, etc.) do not have this suffix.

## Symptoms

- User picks a configured skill via the native picker, types a task, submits.
- louiselm silently notifies "louiselm: advertised command '"'"'<skill>'"'"' description does not match the skill" and does not send the prompt; typed text and the skill chip are preserved (per louiselm-2w4 AC7), so it looks like a transient hiccup rather than a permanent break.
- This happens for every skill, every time, against the real Claude adapter -- native mode is a no-op for Claude in practice, despite ~40 unit/mock tests passing.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua, description_matches() (around line 45): compares the whitespace-normalized advertised description to the whitespace-normalized local skill.description (or skill.short_description) with `==`. Real claude-agent-acp always appends " (user)" (or, presumably, another scope word for project/plugin-scoped commands) to the description of any command sourced from a user-configured skill path, so the strings are never equal even though the command is a correct, unambiguous match. The $-prefixed (Codex-style) tier is unaffected since it never checks description.

## Why it was not caught

Every existing test (tests/skills_spec.lua resolve_command cases, tests/ui/chat_spec.lua native-picker cases, tests/mock/agent_spec.lua) constructs its own advertised-command fixtures with hand-typed descriptions that exactly echo the local skill's description -- none of them models the real adapter's annotation behavior, because that behavior was never observed before this bead was implemented. The acceptance criteria for louiselm-2w4 specified "the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description" without anticipating an adapter-appended suffix.

## Fix direction

In description_matches(), treat the advertised (normalized) description as matching when it *starts with* the local skill's normalized description or short_description, not only on exact equality -- tolerating a trailing annotation without weakening the $-tier or the ambiguity/duplicate rules (those are untouched). Reject anything where the local description is not a prefix of the advertised one, so an unrelated built-in that merely shares a name still fails to match.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/skills_spec.lua using the real captured pair (grill-me description with and without the trailing " (user)") that fails before the fix and passes after.
- Existing exact-match cases keep passing (equality is the size-27-prefix special case of starts-with).

## Not covered

- Whether Codex's $-tier ever needs a similar tolerance -- not verified; no codex-acp session in the available debug logs got far enough to emit available_commands_update. Left as a follow-up if codex turns out to need it too.
- Whether Claude ever uses a different annotation word (e.g. "(project)", "(plugin)") for non-user-scope local skills -- not directly observed, but the starts-with fix is annotation-word-agnostic so it should not matter.
close_reason: Fixed in c230f8c. Root cause: description_matches() in lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua required exact whitespace-normalized equality; real claude-agent-acp appends a scope annotation (" (user)") to every command sourced from a user-configured skill path. Changed to starts-with matching against the local description/short_description. Tests: new resolve_command case using the real captured grill-me description pair (tests/skills_spec.lua), plus full existing resolve_command suite re-verified green. Gates: full mini.test suite green (287 cases), stylua and lua-language-server clean. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria. Codex's $-tier tolerance remains unverified (no codex-acp session reached available_commands_update in available logs) -- left as a known gap, not blocking this fix.

title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm formalize a persisted project vocabulary from grill-me sessions
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as explicit "food for thought" on 2026-08-20. Originally noted only in
an agent's private memory; migrated into beads on 2026-08-20 alongside
louiselm-3od once it was pointed out that louiselm is cross-adapter by
design, so a note only one adapter can see is exactly the kind of context
AGENTS.md says does not belong there.

## The question

Should louiselm (or its workflow) formalize a persisted "project vocabulary" --
a working glossary that accumulates meaning from `grill-me` sessions over
time, so each term embeds context that would otherwise need re-explaining --
and if so, what does that mechanism look like here?

## Context

The user referenced a video by mattpocock (the original author of the
`grill-me` skill/pattern) describing that a grill-me session's real product
is shared understanding, and that over time this naturally produces a working
vocabulary for a project. The user recalled mattpocock built this into one of
his own skills: a mechanism that persists the accumulated vocabulary to a
markdown file rather than letting it live only in conversation history. The
user wants something equivalent for their own workflow here, and floated
possibly integrating it with beads -- the local issue tracker this project
already leans on heavily (`br`/`bvr` triage, the `to-beads-*` skill family).

## Threads worth pulling

- Whether this lives as its own artifact (a `VOCABULARY.md` or similar) or as
  structured beads content (e.g. a dedicated issue type, or metadata on
  existing issues).
- How it interacts with the `to-beads-*` skill family, which already turns
  grill-me sessions into beads work -- is vocabulary a byproduct of that
  same pipeline, or a separate one?
- A concrete instance of the problem this would solve already exists in this
  project: "chat" vs. "session" naming drift (caught and corrected once, but
  only recorded in an agent's private memory before this migration) -- a
  persisted vocabulary mechanism would presumably have caught or prevented
  that drift on its own.
- Worth checking mattpocock's public work (skills, videos, blog) for the
  specific mechanism he built, if the user references it again, rather than
  reinventing it blind.
- Related, separately filed thread: louiselm-3od (documentation strategy) --
  not the same question, but a persisted vocabulary could plausibly feed or
  overlap with an agent-legible documentation artifact. Worth deciding during
  either grill whether they should be one session or two.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.

title: Picker view shows only one visible entry despite multiple items
description:
## Summary

The picker view appears to contain only one visible entry, although its item count indicates that multiple items are available.

## Expected behavior

The picker should render enough of its list content for the available entries to be visibly distinguishable, with normal scrolling/navigation exposing the remaining items.

## Actual behavior

The view looks as if it has only one entry. The picker reports more items than are visibly displayed. The content rendered for an item may be too long and could be consuming the available display area.

## Ownership hypothesis

This may not be a louiselm rendering bug. Investigate whether the behavior comes from the snacks.nvim picker configuration/layout, item formatting, wrapping, height, or preview settings before changing louiselm.

## Reproduction

Open the affected louiselm picker and compare the visible entries with the picker-reported item count.

## Acceptance criteria

- Determine whether the root cause is louiselm or snacks.nvim configuration.
- If louiselm owns the issue, make multiple available entries visibly usable without breaking navigation.
- If snacks.nvim configuration owns it, document the required configuration change and avoid an unnecessary louiselm workaround.
notes: Root cause confirmed outside LouiseLM: the active Snacks configuration sets picker.win.list.wo.wrap=true globally. LouiseLM passes distinct choices through vim.ui.select; wrapped long rows consume the select layout height. README documents a picker.sources.select win.list.wo.wrap=false override, verified against the installed Snacks config merge. No provider-specific LouiseLM workaround added.
close_reason: Confirmed Snacks list wrapping as root cause and documented the source-scoped configuration fix

title: Restyle README hero with mural print aesthetic
description:
## Goal
Restyle the existing README hero so it uses the supplied mural reference visual language while preserving the current LouiseLM composition, spirit, and symbols.

## Scope
- In scope: replace `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` in place, using `/home/lotso/Downloads/1786245984429.jpg` as the visual reference.
- Preserve the existing landscape composition and recognizable motifs: the central portrait; connected mesh; people writing, coding, organizing, and speaking; the books, cubes, leaf, microphone, waveform, raised fists, megaphone, birds, and building.
- Apply a strict white, black, and red treatment: a clearer neutral or slightly warm white instead of the current beige/parchment cast; dense near-black ink; and vivid deep-red accents.
- Give the black artwork the reference mural character: rough hand-printed woodcut or engraved linework, cross-hatching and stippling, imperfect ink coverage, distressed contours, and slight registration/edge irregularity. Keep enough contrast and detail for README display size.
- Retain subtle physical surface or print texture, but do not let it muddy the white ground or read as yellowed paper.
- Out of scope: changing README copy, image placement, alt text, core composition, adding unrelated symbols, or turning the scene into a photograph of a building/mural.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` is replaced at the same path and remains a valid WebP with an approximately 2:1 landscape aspect ratio, so the existing README reference needs no change.
2. The original image narrative, layout, central figure, and listed symbols remain immediately recognizable; the work is a stylistic revision rather than a redesign.
3. The visible palette is limited to bright neutral/slightly warm white, dense black, and deep red. The dominant cream/sepia cast is gone and white areas read noticeably whiter than in the current asset.
4. Black figures and marks consistently resemble aged mural/woodcut ink: irregular, tactile, strongly hatched or stippled, and less digitally clean, without losing legibility.
5. Red remains an accent that guides the eye and does not overpower the black linework or white ground.
6. The image renders correctly from `README.md` at full size and thumbnail size, with no accidental cropping, illegible key motifs, or unrelated asset changes.

## Testing
- Open the final WebP directly and render `README.md`; inspect both full-size and typical repository-page display sizes.
- Verify the output format, dimensions/aspect ratio, and unchanged README asset path.
- Compare side by side with the existing hero and `/home/lotso/Downloads/1786245984429.jpg` against every visual acceptance criterion.

## Notes
- The reference image is a local, untracked visual source. Its relevant traits are recorded above so the task remains actionable if that file is unavailable.
- Favor a focused image edit/style transfer over regenerating the scene from scratch, because symbol and composition preservation is the primary constraint.

title: Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it; louiselm attribution unproven
description:
The Ghostty terminal emulator died at 2026-08-20 05:14:18, taking all three of
its surfaces — and every Neovim inside them — with it. Neovim did not crash.
Attribution to louiselm is UNPROVEN and currently looks unlikely; this bead
exists so the next occurrence is diagnosable and so the round's record is
honest about what happened.

CORRECTION: this bead was originally filed as "Neovim dies with no crash
artifact". That was wrong, and the correction is the finding. Neovim was the
victim, not the subject.

## Observed

Session `cae87c06-bd44-429f-823e-6b18a361129f`, cwd `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`,
Neovim 0.12.2, Ghostty 1.3.1 (ReleaseFast, GTK 4.18.6, OpenGL renderer, AMDGPU
under gdm-x-session), build under test `cd37ab2`.

User's report: "i saw all nvim windows closing without me doing anything, that's
all, i didnt see a banner it was fast."

From `journalctl --user`:

```
05:02:28  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 481451)
05:02:29  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-481516.scope
05:04:29  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-483272.scope
05:10:20  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 488289)
05:10:20  Started app-ghostty-surface-transient-488332.scope
05:14:18  app-ghostty-surface-transient-481516.scope: Consumed 1.110s CPU, 48.8M peak
05:14:18  app-ghostty-surface-transient-483272.scope: Consumed 7.435s CPU, 299.4M peak
05:14:19  app-ghostty-surface-transient-488332.scope: Consumed 7.578s CPU, 305.3M peak
05:14:27  ghostty version=1.3.1                    (pid 491455)  <- fresh process
```

Three surface scopes terminating inside one second is the whole application
dying, not three windows being closed. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface —
confirmed at 05:16:59, where a new `ghostty` invocation (pid 493960) handed the
new surface to the already-running pid 491455 rather than starting its own.

Process start times agree: ghostty 491455 at 05:14:27, Neovim 491984 at
05:14:38 — the terminal came back eleven seconds before the editor was
relaunched inside it.

The agent side saw only the downstream effect
(`20260820-045809-478664-claude-agent-acp-stderr.log`):

```
Session cae87c06-...: query stream error: ACP connection closed
Error during cleanup: Error: Query closed before response received
```

with the JSON-RPC log ending on a pending `Edit` tool call
(`toolu_01K7RgEDmrCMf8NSaAEHEYLb`).

## Symptoms

- Every Neovim window vanishes simultaneously, instantly, with no message.
- No "Vim: Caught deadly signal" banner, because there was no deadly signal:
  Neovim's pty was hung up when its terminal died.
- Orphaned language servers accumulate (14 `copilot-language-server` at
  `ppid=1`, ~228 MB each) from instances killed this way.

## Root cause

Unknown for Ghostty. Established for Neovim: it was hung up, not crashed.

Ruled out by evidence:

- **Neovim crash.** No `ERR` in `~/.local/state/nvim/nvim.log` around
  05:08-05:14, only `tui_handle_term_mode` warnings. The surface scopes died
  first.
- **OOM kill.** `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/memory.events` reads
  `oom_kill 0`; `memory.max` is `max`; peak 13.1 GB of 27 GB. No cgroup in
  `user.slice` has a nonzero `oom_kill`.
- **Ghostty panic.** A Zig panic writes a trace to stderr, which reaches the
  journal — the journal has ghostty's full lifecycle for that window and no
  panic. Silent death points at a signal with no handler output.
- **`cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start`.** The user's config
  (`~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/treesitter.lua:138-151`) already ran
  `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so a markdown highlighter was
  attached to the chat buffer before the commit too. Net treesitter load is
  unchanged. Do not spend a round here.

Remaining hypotheses:

1. **Ghostty defect, unrelated to louiselm.** Base rate for this is high and
   nothing yet contradicts it. Discriminator: whether it recurs with no
   louiselm session attached.
2. **image.nvim's kitty graphics traffic crashing Ghostty.**
   `~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/image.lua` sets `backend = "kitty"`, so
   image.nvim writes kitty graphics escape sequences directly into Ghostty. The
   thread is thin: `cd37ab2` is supposed to have detached image.nvim from the
   transcript buffer, and the deaths happened on that build. It stays alive only
   if the detach is incomplete. Discriminator: QA case 1.2 of this round — list
   the chat buffer's autocmds and check for an image.nvim group. That case has
   not been run yet (it hit a recipe bug in the plan).
3. **GPU/driver fault.** AMDGPU with GLAMOR under X. `~/.local/share/xorg/Xorg.0.log`
   has nothing past boot, but a GPU reset lands in the kernel log, which is not
   readable here — the user is not in `adm`/`systemd-journal`, so
   `journalctl -k` returns nothing. Discriminator: `sudo dmesg | grep -i
   "amdgpu\|ring.*timeout\|GPU reset"` around 05:14.

## Why it was not caught

Not a test-suite gap — no suite can observe its own terminal emulator dying.
The real gap is that three of the four recording paths were off:

- `ulimit -c` is `0`, so neither Ghostty nor Neovim can write a core.
- `systemd-coredump` is not installed; `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` is the
  bare string `core`, so a dump would land in the process's cwd unnoticed.
- Neovim's deadly-signal message goes to stderr, i.e. the terminal that just
  died, and is never written to `NVIM_LOG_FILE`.

The path that *did* work — `journalctl --user`, which recorded Ghostty's whole
lifecycle — is the only reason this was diagnosable at all, and it was not
consulted first because the symptom was reported as a Neovim crash.

## Fix direction

Nothing in `lua/louiselm/` to change yet. In order:

1. `sudo dmesg` filtered for `amdgpu`/GPU reset around 05:14:18, to settle
   hypothesis 3 with the one log that was unreadable.
2. Run QA case 1.2 to settle hypothesis 2.
3. Install `systemd-coredump` (Debian) so the next Ghostty death leaves a
   stack, and set `ulimit -c unlimited` for interactive shells.
4. If it recurs and 1-2 come back clean, this is a Ghostty bug and belongs
   upstream, not here. Close it with the evidence rather than leaving it open
   in louiselm's graph.

Rejected: reverting or altering `cd37ab2` on suspicion. The evidence points
away from it, and it is the only build for which a full timeline exists.

## Acceptance

- Either a mechanism in `lua/louiselm/` with `file:line`, or a decision to
  close this as not-louiselm with the evidence that shows it.
- A recurrence after step 3 produces a durable artifact (coredump entry or
  captured stderr) rather than a silent disappearance.

## Not covered

- Whether the Neovim restarts at 05:08:39 and 05:11:02 were also Ghostty
  deaths is not established. The journal shows a ghostty start at 05:10:20 but
  the window before that is not reconstructed.
- The kernel log for 05:14 has not been read.
- The 14 orphaned copilot processes date from the previous evening's instances;
  they evidence unclean exits generally, not this specific death.
close_reason: Closed as not-LouiseLM: kernel log proves Ghostty renderer general-protection fault at the exact incident timestamp.

Next cheapest discriminator: that grep would not match a userspace segfault, which the kernel logs as 'segfault at'/'traps:'. Run: sudo dmesg | grep -iE 'segfault|traps|general protection|protection fault' -- a ghostty[488289] line near 05:14:18 would settle attribution outright.

title: agent process-handle return types annotated userdata? instead of vim.SystemObj?
description:
lua/louiselm/agent/spawn.lua (M.start), lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua (M.check),
and lua/louiselm/agent/init.lua (M.start, M.check) all annotate the
vim.system() process handle they return as `---@return userdata? handle`.
The real Neovim runtime stub (vim/_core/system.lua) declares vim.system's
async-form return type as `vim.SystemObj` (a plain Lua table with a
metatable), not `userdata`.

Evidence: adding a second `pcall(vim.system, ...)` call site in
lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua (for louiselm-2ce, the latest-version
staleness check) made `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`
newly report:

  lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:150:12 [Warning] Annotations specify that
    return value #1 has a type of `userdata?`, returning value of type
    `table` here instead. (return-type-mismatch)
  lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:193:10 [Warning] ... same ...
  lua/louiselm/agent/spawn.lua:49:10 [Warning] ... same ...

Bisected: the mismatch is pre-existing in spawn.lua's M.start and
health.lua's original (single-call) M.check — confirmed by reverting only
the new health.lua code and rerunning the check, which still flags
health.lua:102 (the untouched original --version call) and spawn.lua:49.
lua-language-server apparently didn't surface it before some threshold of
project analysis was crossed; it is a real annotation defect regardless of
when it is reported.

Fix: change `userdata?` to `vim.SystemObj?` in all four declarations so the
LuaCATS annotation matches vim.system()'s real return type.
close_reason: Fixed: changed userdata? to table? in lua/louiselm/agent/{spawn,health,init}.lua (matches pcall(vim.system,...)'s real inferred return type in this workspace's lua-language-server config, which doesn't expose vim.SystemObj). Also fixed a related latent duplicate-set-field warning uncovered by the same deeper analysis pass: converted direct 'nvim.system = ...'/'nvim.fn.executable = ...' stub reassignment to rawset() in tests/capture_spec.lua, tests/session/api_spec.lua, and tests/ui/command_spec.lua, matching the codebase's existing rawset(nvim, "notify", ...) convention. lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning now reports the same 9 pre-existing problems as a clean main checkout (all in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua, unrelated), confirmed stable across repeated runs.

title: Publish trademark policy with named-class refusal
description:
Publish a trademark policy for the LouiseLM name.

Under MIT this is the **only instrument that bites from day one**. MIT grants everyone the right to use the code; it conveys no right to the name. The policy is where the political line is actually drawn and enforced.

## Content

- The LouiseLM name and any associated marks are not licensed by the MIT grant and are reserved.
- Forks may say they are derived from LouiseLM. They may not present themselves as LouiseLM.
- Named class refusal: no permission to use the mark will be granted to *entities deriving a majority of revenue from proprietary foundation models, or from the hardware they run on.*
- Individuals, non-profits, educational institutions, worker-owned co-ops, and community projects are welcome to use the name to refer to the project.

## Why a class and not a list of companies

A list of company names is precise today and stale in eighteen months, and it is defeated by a rename or a subsidiary. A structural definition catches successors, cannot be gamed as easily, and states a principle rather than a grudge — which is also the difference between an anti-capitalist position and a feud with two firms.

## Acceptance criteria

- Policy document exists and is linked from README.
- The class is defined structurally, with no company named.
- The document is plain prose, readable in under two minutes. Precedents worth skimming for tone: Mozilla, Rust, Debian.
close_reason: Completed concise trademark policy and README link; documentary verification passed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Implemented TRADEMARK_POLICY.md and linked it from README.md. The 317-word policy reserves the LouiseLM marks, permits truthful reference and derived-from attribution, requires forks to use their own identity, states the structural majority-revenue class refusal without naming companies, and explicitly preserves identical software-licence rights for the refused class. Verification: git diff --check passed; Markdown targets exist; no named company appears in the policy.

title: Comment in-progress-first triage requirement onto workflow-engine issues
description:
Attach the in-progress-first triage requirement to the deferred workflow-engine issues as `br` comments, so it is discoverable from the issues themselves rather than from a conversation transcript.

## The requirement

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot express.

## The evidence behind it

`bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum across eight components. Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for `in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight, and a fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic comfortably. Observed in this repo: roughly 0.459 against 0.405.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix it. `priority-first` raises Urgency only to about 0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file. So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration — it has to be applied on top of its output, which is exactly why it belongs in the engine that consumes that output.

## Where it goes

Comment on the deferred workflow-engine issues — the ones covering persisted declarative workflows and sequential execution of beads graphs by policy-controlled agents. Both sit under the attention-control-plane epic.

Frame it as a **candidate requirement for that design conversation, not a decision already made.** The sequencing policy is the engine's to define; this records why the question exists and what the evidence was.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both relevant deferred issues carry a comment stating the requirement and the scoring evidence.
- The comment is explicit that this is input to a future design decision rather than a settled one.
- `br sync --flush-only` has been run so the comments reach JSONL and are committed.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: QA round: replayed user prompts on resume
description:
# Manual QA review — replayed user prompts on resume

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `110e357` (fix), on top of the permission-decision round
verified at `7d115d7`. `0dcdce5` (beads bookkeeping only) needs no testing.

Origin: `louiselm-pmr` — after `:LouiselmResume`, the chat showed the agent's
replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but silently dropped every
prompt the user had typed, so a resumed session read as one-sided. Root cause:
`lifecycle.lua` already turned the ACP `user_message_chunk` replay notification
into a `user_chunk` event (since `4e4a58b`), but `chat/init.lua`'s
`handle_event` never had a branch for it and dropped it on the floor. `110e357`
adds that branch, rendering each line prefixed `> `.

The unit test in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` proves the rendering logic against a
synthetic `fake_session` emitting a synthetic `user_chunk` event. It cannot
prove that a real adapter's replay actually looks like that, and it cannot
prove a *live* turn doesn't now render the user's prompt twice — both of
those only exist once a real `claude-agent-acp` process is in the loop.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls | **passed** — log + visual, see below |
| 2 | Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once | **passed** — log + visual, see below |

## Setup

The plugin is installed as a clone of this repo, so new commits are not live
until you update it:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

Confirm the clone matches the source, then restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

Both must print `110e357 fix(chat): show replayed user prompts`.

## Ground rules learned the hard way (carried over from prior rounds)

- Say the tool name and give absolute paths in prompts, or the model reaches
  for the wrong tool / does a `find` first and you burn a round trip.
- Start each case in a fresh session — a prior denial or detour in the same
  session makes the model hedge on the next one.
- Pin the adapter log by session id, not by mtime — the newest log file is
  whatever session you're talking to me in right now:
  ```bash
  L=$(grep -l "<session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
  ```
  The session id is in the chat header, or via `:LouiselmSessionId`.
- **That grep pollutes itself.** If *I* run it to pull evidence, my own bash
  command containing the session id gets logged into whatever log file is
  currently open for *this* conversation — `tail -1` then picks my own
  self-reference instead of the real target log. Fix: search all matching
  files, not just the last one, and eyeball which one actually has protocol
  content (`session/update` with real `sessionUpdate` kinds) rather than a
  `rawInput`/`toolCallId` echo of the grep command itself. Hit this pulling
  evidence for case 1.

## Cases

### 1. Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls

Exercises `110e357` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1305` against a real
`claude-agent-acp` replay, which is the exact shape the original bug report
had: two user turns with agent activity (including a tool call) between them.

Steps:

1. Start a **fresh** session in this repo.
2. Send: `Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md, then reply with just the word "ack".`
3. Once it replies, send a second prompt: `Now reply with just the word "ack2".`
4. Note the session id (`:LouiselmSessionId`), then `:LouiselmCloseSession`.
5. `:LouiselmResume` and pick that session.

Expect: the buffer shows, in original order: `> Use the Read tool...`, the
tool call line for the Read, the assistant's `ack`, `> Now reply...`, the
assistant's `ack2` — both prompts visible, prefixed `> `, in the order they
were actually sent, not collapsed or reordered relative to the tool call.

Failure signature: either prompt missing from the replay, both prompts shown
adjacent to each other instead of interleaved with the reply/tool call, or
prompt text without the `> ` prefix (i.e. the old "renders replayed assistant
chunks" behavior, meaning the fix didn't ship).

**Result: passed.** Session `claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`,
user reported the buffer looked right. Log evidence from
`20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` (the resume,
2 minutes after the original turn) confirms the wire order matches exactly
what case 1 predicted:

```
user_message_chunk "[@AGENTS.md](...)"
user_message_chunk "Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read ... ack"
tool_call Read AGENTS.md (pending)
tool_call_update (completed)
agent_message_chunk "ack"
user_message_chunk "Now reply with just the word \"ack2\"."
agent_message_chunk "ack2"
```

Both prompts present, correctly interleaved around the Read tool call, in
original order. Combined with the user's visual read of the buffer, this
closes the "does a real adapter's replay actually look like the synthetic
unit-test fixture" question the unit test structurally can't answer.

### 2. Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once

Exercises the regression the bead flagged as unverified: `handle_event` now
has a branch for `user_chunk`, so this checks a *live* `claude-agent-acp` turn
never also emits `user_message_chunk` (which `submit_prompt` already writes
into the buffer directly — a second write would duplicate it).

Steps:

1. In any session (resumed or fresh), submit: `Reply with just the word "once".`

Expect: the prompt line `> Reply with just the word "once".` appears exactly
once in the buffer, followed by exactly one `once` response.

Failure signature: the prompt text appears twice (once from `submit_prompt`,
once from a `user_chunk` event the live turn shouldn't have produced).

**Result: passed.** User ran this in the same resumed session
(`claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`, reusing the adapter process
from case 1) and confirmed the buffer looked right. Log evidence from the
same `20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`, appended
after the case-1 replay (lines 9-17, the live "once" turn): `agent_message_chunk
'once'` and nothing else — no `user_message_chunk` for the "once" prompt.
Grand total `user_message_chunk` count for the whole file stayed at 3 (the two
replayed prompts plus the AGENTS.md attachment chunk from case 1's replay),
confirming the live turn added zero. That's the precondition for a duplicate
being structurally absent, matching what case 1's earlier partial evidence
(the pre-resume live log) already suggested — now confirmed end-to-end with
both the wire log and the user's own read of the buffer.

## Evidence check

```bash
L=$(grep -l "<session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
grep -c '"user_message_chunk"' "$L"
```

For case 1: confirms the real adapter did send `user_message_chunk` during
replay (proves the fixture actually exercised the code path) — cross-check
against what the buffer shows, since the log doesn't tell you what got
*rendered*, only what the agent sent.

For case 2: on the resumed-session log, count should be ≥1 (replay only); on
a fresh live-turn log, count should be 0 outside any resume. Grep alone can't
prove the buffer's dedup — that's the visual check in the steps above.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures left in the repo (no files written). Nothing to revert.

## Reporting back

Send me which case, what you saw in the buffer, and the session id so I can
pull the log myself. If something's wrong I'll fix it and you'll need to redo
Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

None yet.
close_reason: Completed QA round: both real-adapter manual cases passed (resume replay preserves/interleaves user prompts; live prompt renders once), protocol-log and human visual evidence are recorded in the bead, and tests/ui/chat_spec.lua passes 74/74.

title: Single-line tool captions run to thousands of characters and overflow rendered excerpts
description:
Once louiselm-cmr made the `<sub>` caption a single line, that line could be
enormous: the longest in a real 156-tool-call export was 7319 characters, with
6963 and 6490 behind it. Correct, and useless as a label — and actively harmful
downstream, since the blog pipeline renders excerpts of these exports through
`:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme fixes and does not expose.

Filed during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD` rather than before the fix:
louiselm-cmr's close reason recorded this as deliberately deferred presentation
work, and the tester elected to take it immediately when the measured caption
lengths arrived. The evidence below is from the verified post-fix export.

## Observed

`/home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-1-20260820-062145.md`, exported on
build `a6484ea`, 6384 lines, 156 tool calls:

```
longest <sub> caption lengths, characters: 7319, 6963, 6490
```

Captions of that length are whole `br create --description "$(cat <<'EOF' ...`
invocations with the entire bead body inlined.

## Symptoms

- A caption that is a wall of text rather than a label.
- In a `<pre>` rendered by TOhtml, one physical line 7319 characters wide,
  overflowing horizontally inside a fixed-width iframe.

## Root cause

Not a defect in the collapsing itself. `render_entry`
(`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`) interpolated the full normalized title
into the caption with no length bound, because the title's natural size is the
size of a shell command.

## Fix direction

Bound the caption; keep the payload whole. The untruncated title is already a
few lines below inside `<details>`, which is what that block is for.

Rejected: wrapping the caption across lines. That re-creates exactly the
multi-line `<sub>` element louiselm-cmr just removed.

## Acceptance

- Caption truncated at a fixed character count with an ellipsis.
- Truncation counts characters, not bytes: real titles contain em dashes and
  other multi-byte characters, and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8.
- The full title still appears in the `<details>` payload dump.
- A title exactly at the limit is left untouched.

## Not covered

- The limit is a judgement, not a measurement; 120 characters is chosen to fit
  a conventional terminal width, not derived from the theme's iframe width.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d6557d. render_entry now passes the normalized title through truncate(), which cuts at CAPTION_TITLE_LIMIT=120 using vim.fn.strchars/strcharpart so multi-byte characters are never split, and appends an ellipsis. Tests: 'truncates an overlong title in the caption but keeps it whole in the payload' (400 x's -> 120 + ellipsis in the caption, full 400 still present in the <details> dump), 'truncates on character boundaries, not bytes' (400 e-acutes), 'leaves a title at the limit untouched' (exactly 120, no ellipsis). First two confirmed red before the fix; the third was green already and is a boundary guard against an off-by-one. Gates: mini.test 0 fails/0 notes across the full suite, stylua clean on both changed files, lua-language-server unchanged at 9 pre-existing problems all in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua. No deviation from the filed acceptance criteria. Tester re-export verification still pending.

title: Grill fold-based tool-call rendering UX
description:
## Question

Would native Neovim folds make LouiseLM's chronological tool-call timeline less cluttered without hiding active work, failures, or permission decisions?

## Scope

- Explore fold behavior separately for active versus completed calls.
- Decide whether adjacent calls should be grouped and what summary information remains visible.
- Cover failed calls, cancelled calls, permission prompts, nested/repeated calls, default open/closed state, discoverability, keyboard behavior, and mobile/narrow-window equivalents where relevant.
- Compare the proposal against the current one-line started-to-completed renderer.
- Prefer native Neovim behavior and the smallest viable design; do not assume a generic fold framework shared with prompt contexts.

## Desired Outcome

A grill-tested UX decision with concrete states, examples, accessibility/discoverability considerations, and—only if implementation is justified—small follow-up beads with acceptance criteria.

## Out of Scope

Implementing tool folds as part of the Agent Skills profile feature. This question has no dependency on that feature.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Grill-me session reached full agreement. Decision: fold-based rendering, scoped to within-turn clutter only.

- Fold unit = contiguous run of `completed` tool-call lines; any active, failed, or cancelled call breaks the run and is always rendered as a standalone visible line (never folded, never flagged-then-hidden).
- Trigger = superseded, mid-turn: a run folds the moment something follows it (new tool-call run, resumed assistant text, or `turn_done` as a force-close catch-all for a trailing run).
- Foldtext = Neovim default (first line + native line count), no custom renderer.
- Discoverability/keyboard = fully native (za/zo/zc/zR/zM), no new keymaps or foldcolumn.
- New fold state is separate from `context_folds` (different trigger/lifecycle) but mirrors its pattern (manual foldmethod, per-window tracking).
- Permission decisions are out of scope: they never render inline in the transcript today.
- Separately decided: live raw ACP payload access becomes on-demand only (not inline/folded) -- a new command/keymap on a `[tool]` line, decoupled from the fold mechanism.

Implementation split into louiselm-ufx.1 (fold rendering) and louiselm-ufx.2 (on-demand raw-payload inspector). Leaving this question open until both land -- br policy blocks closing a parent with open children, and that's the right call here since the decision is made but the work is not done.

title: Fold completed tool-call runs in the chat transcript
description:
## Goal
Reduce transcript clutter from many tool calls within one turn by folding contiguous runs of completed tool-call lines, using native Neovim folds.

## Scope
- In scope: new fold-tracking state in `louiselm.ui.chat` (separate from `context_folds`/`fold_counts`, same pattern: `foldmethod=manual`, `foldenable=true`, per-window fold-count tracking), applied in `handle_event`.
- A "run" is a contiguous stretch of tool-call lines whose terminal status is `completed` (see `lifecycle.lua:197`: `tool_call_finished` is only ever `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`).
- An active (started, not yet finished) or `failed`/`cancelled` call breaks the run and is never itself folded -- always a standalone visible line.
- Fold trigger is "superseded": a completed run folds the moment something follows it -- a new `tool_call_started` begins a new run, an assistant `chunk` resumes text, or `turn_done` fires (force-close catch-all so a trailing run is never left open across a turn boundary).
- Foldtext: Neovim's default only (first line of range + native line count). No custom `foldtext`.
- No new keymaps, no `foldcolumn` changes -- native `za`/`zo`/`zc`/`zR`/`zM` only.
- Out of scope: cross-session/history folding beyond one turn, folding or flagging failed/cancelled calls, any change to permission-decision UI, any inline raw-payload rendering (separate task).

## Acceptance Criteria
