```sh
  '' \
  'When explicitly selected, reply with VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL.' \
  > "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md"
```

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Cases do not share a session. A consumed catalog or a failed selection in one
  session must not influence the next case.
- Before sending anything in every new case, the session header must end in
  `skills=inject`. If it says `skills=native` or includes the normal-config
  `AGENTS.md` context, stop: the QA setup is not active and the case is invalid.
- Copy prompts from fenced blocks exactly. A leading `/` deliberately exercises
  a different submission path from natural language.
- The fold is ephemeral UI state. Transcript exports intentionally cannot prove
  its contents or open/closed state.

## Cases

### 1. Real-agent hidden catalog and slash deferral

Exercises `f2b9747` / `lua/louiselm/skills/inject.lua` and the first accepted
prompt path in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmChat` and wait for `Session: status=ready`. Confirm the header
   ends in `skills=inject`; otherwise stop without submitting either prompt.
2. Before typing, inspect the prompt. It must be plain `> ` with no
   `skill-index`, `<available_skills>`, or context chip.
3. Submit this command and wait for the turn to finish:

```text
/compact
```

4. The submitted slash command must have no context fold. Submit:

```text
Which advertised skill identifies the violet QA sentinel? Reply with only its skill name. Do not invoke or read it.
```

5. Expect the reply `qa-catalog-sentinel`. Immediately before the authored
   prompt there must be one closed fold whose summary contains only
   `skill-index`. Focus must end on the new editable `> ` prompt.
6. Without moving the cursor or running another command, write objective
   buffer/fold evidence:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-1.txt")
```

Expect: the real peer identifies the private fixture from the hidden catalog;
the slash turn does not consume or render that catalog; the natural-language
turn renders it once as a closed native fold; focus returns to the draft.

Failure signature: catalog XML or a `skill-index` chip is visible before send;
the slash command gains a fold; the model cannot name the sentinel; the fold is
open, has the wrong summary, or leaves the cursor inside submitted text.

7. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the copied id as the run id.

### 2. Multiple exact contexts, native folding, and no resend

Exercises `f2b9747` / accepted context rendering and picker-body capture in
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. If Neovim was restarted, rerun the QA setup command first. Start a fresh
   `:LouiselmNewSession`; the only configured agent must be `qa_inject`, and its
   ready header must end in `skills=inject`. Stop if DeepSeek/default appears.
2. Run `:LouiselmPickFile /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747`, then select
   `context.txt`.
3. Run `:LouiselmPickSkill`, then select `qa-catalog-sentinel`.
4. Confirm two compact chips remain on the editable prompt; the automatic
   catalog remains invisible. Submit:

```text
Read the attached file and selected skill. Reply only with their two uppercase tokens, in attachment order.
```

5. Expect `FILE-F2B9747-FIRST VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`. One closed fold must
   precede the visible user prompt. Its summary order must be `skill-index`,
   `file: ...context.txt`, then `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel`.
6. Put the cursor on the summary and press `zo`. Verify the file context shows
   the exact resource-link line
   `Referenced file: /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/context.txt` and the selected
   skill context shows the complete `SKILL.md` body. The user prompt must remain
   outside the fold. Press `zc` and verify it closes normally.
7. Submit `Reply only NEXT.` without selecting more context. No second context
   fold should appear and the reply should be `NEXT`.
8. Run `:LouiselmSessionId`, retain the run id, then capture evidence:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-2.txt")
```

Expect: normal fold commands work; opened contents show the exact transported
resource-link fields and selected-skill text in transport order;
closing/reopening presentation does not resend any context on the next turn.

Failure signature: chip order differs from fold order; the resource-link URI or
selected skill body is summarized, truncated, or reordered; `zo`/`zc` do not
work; the prompt is swallowed by the fold; the second turn gains a context fold
or sees an old token unexpectedly.

### 3. Selection-time skill read failure and retry

Exercises `f2b9747` / the real picker callback timing and local-failure
retention path in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. If Neovim was restarted, rerun the QA setup command first. Start a fresh
   `:LouiselmNewSession`; the only configured agent must be `qa_inject`, and its
   ready header must end in `skills=inject`. Stop if DeepSeek/default appears.
2. Run `:LouiselmPickSkill` but leave the picker open. In another terminal run:

```sh
mv /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md.off
```

3. Back in the picker, select `qa-catalog-sentinel`. A precise read error must
   appear, while a `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel` chip remains selected.
4. Type `retry preserved` and submit. It must fail locally: no agent turn, no
   submitted fold, and both the chip and editable text remain.
5. Capture the failed state:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); vim.fn.writefile(l,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-failure.txt")
```

6. Restore the file in the other terminal:

```sh
mv /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md.off /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md
```

7. Submit the unchanged prompt again. It should now be accepted, consume the
   selection once, create one closed context fold, and return focus to a clean
   prompt. Capture the final state:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-retry.txt")
```
8. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the run id.

Expect: a real filesystem race cannot lose the selection or draft, and retry
uses the restored exact body without requiring another picker activation.

Failure signature: the chip disappears on read failure; Enter sends a turn or
creates a fold while the file is absent; the draft changes; restoring the file
still cannot submit; retry attaches the skill more than once.

## Evidence check

After each case, from the repository root run:

```sh
sed -n '1,120p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-1.txt
sed -n '1,160p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-2.txt
sed -n '1,120p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-failure.txt
sed -n '1,160p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-retry.txt
```

The first evidence line must report `method=manual`; accepted-context snapshots
must report a positive closed range, while the case 3 failure snapshot must
contain the chip and draft but no `[contexts:` summary. The remainder proves
exact visible buffer contents and prompt separation. It cannot alone prove what
the remote model received; the sentinel response and run id settle that part.

This check uses the same `foldclosed()`, buffer-line, and cursor APIs validated
against known-good headless runs in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` (309-case full
suite passed on the build under test).

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close all QA chat sessions and remove `/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747`. No permission
rules or repository files should remain. The final QA record becomes one
`qa-round` bead; then delete this working file without committing it.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, case number, what you saw, and anything surprising. I will
pull the evidence files myself. If something is wrong I will file it before
fixing it, update this file, and tell you which cases need a fresh Setup rerun.

## Findings this round

No product findings yet.

## Results this round

- Case 1 passed on `qa_inject/01a01f16-84a9-78c2-a852-eef2c2be00c8`.
  Buffer evidence reports `skills=inject`, one closed manual fold at lines 9–20
  with summary `skill-index`, and the cursor on the final editable prompt. The
  pinned Codex rollout contains exactly one sentinel catalog block, paired with
  the natural-language prompt, followed by the exact `qa-catalog-sentinel`
  response. The preceding `/compact` transcript entry has no context fold.
- Case 2 passed on `qa_inject/01a01f1a-f56b-71e2-a2cd-a21580de1825`.
  Buffer evidence reports one closed manual fold at lines 6–27, exact summary
  order `skill-index`, file, skill, the transported resource-link URI, and the
  complete selected `SKILL.md` body. The authored prompt and later `NEXT` turn
  remain outside it, with the cursor on the final editable prompt. The rollout
  returns `FILE-F2B9747-FIRST VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`, then shows the second
  turn contains only `Reply only NEXT.` and returns `NEXT`.
- Case 3 passed on
  `qa_inject/01a01f2d-ca56-7320-bb6d-d9b26900984f`. The failure snapshot keeps
  the `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel` chip and `retry preserved` draft with no
  submitted context fold. The pinned rollout contains exactly one retry prompt
  and one selected-skill body, followed by `VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`, proving
  the failed local attempt did not reach the agent. The retry snapshot reports
  one closed manual fold at lines 6–25, exact `skill-index` then selected-skill
  order and body, the authored prompt outside it, and the cursor on the final
  editable prompt. A later typed `L` was present when the evidence command was
  finally captured, so initial draft cleanliness rests on the tester's manual
  observation rather than that delayed snapshot.

## Round conclusion

All three cases passed on build `f2b9747`; no product findings were discovered.
The round confirmed behavior the automated suite cannot settle alone: the real
Codex ACP payload shape, native Neovim fold interaction and focus, and a real
filesystem race between picker display and skill selection. The automated
309-case suite already covered the corresponding deterministic state and async
boundaries, which is why this round found recipe problems rather than product
gaps.

Cleanup: remove `/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747` after recording this round. The
tester should close the three ephemeral QA chat sessions; no repository code or

## Recipe corrections this round

- Case 1 attempt `codex/01a01f0d-a7c6-75d3-b749-a21b9d4f8d31` is invalid. Its

title: Health check reports 'no output' for subcommand-based agent CLIs
description:
`:checkhealth louiselm` reported "version command returned no output" for
any agent whose launch `args` represent a subcommand invocation rather than
a bare binary name (e.g. `acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek`, wrapped
by a debug script) — the installed-version check silently produced no
usable version, unlike sibling agents launched with a single-token args
array (`codex-acp`, `claude-agent-acp`), which worked correctly.

## Observed

Live user report, session `claude/e1118174-fdbe-4320-9086-4d4da9517f3c`,
after running `:checkhealth louiselm`:

```
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 (latest 1.6.0 available)
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — 0.66.0 (latest 0.70.0 available)
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh: version command returned no output
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh: version command returned no output
louiselm: codex is outdated (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 installed, 1.6.0 upstream)
louiselm: claude is outdated (0.66.0 installed, 0.70.0 upstream)
```

The two silent failures corresponded to the `deepseek` and `glm` agent
entries in `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`,
both configured as:

```lua
deepseek = {
  command = "/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh",
  args = { "acp-llm-adapter", "serve", "--backend", "deepseek" },
  ...
}
```

Reproduced directly on the command line:

```
$ /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek --version
(no output, exit 0)
$ acp-llm-adapter --version
acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2
$ acp-llm-adapter serve --help
Usage: acp-llm-adapter serve [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
Options: --backend <BACKEND>, --max-turn-requests <N>, -h/--help
(no --version flag on the `serve` subcommand)
```

## Symptoms

- `:checkhealth louiselm` shows "version command returned no output" for
  any agent whose `args` is a multi-token subcommand invocation.
- No outdated-version warning is possible for such agents even when one is
  warranted, since the installed version never resolves.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua` `M.check` (before the fix) unconditionally
built the version-query command as `{definition.command, ...definition.args,
"--version"}`. That assumes `--version` is a valid trailing flag for
whatever `args` represents. For a subcommand-based CLI, `--version` must
appear *before* the subcommand (`acp-llm-adapter --version`, not
`acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek --version`); the `serve`
subcommand's own flag parser has no `--version` flag, so clap accepts the
process launch, `serve` starts (a real ACP server reading stdio), and it
exits 0 with no stdout once its unfed stdin hits EOF under `vim.system`,
which the code correctly reports as "no output" rather than crashing — the
inputs to that classification were simply wrong for this shape of `args`.
This is a config-construction gap, not a logic bug in the no-output
classification itself.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/agent/health_spec.lua`'s "includes wrapper args before --version"
test (from the immediately preceding commit `6b2a69f`) only exercises a
wrapper forwarding a single-token binary name (`{"codex-acp"}`), which is
flag-compatible with a trailing `--version`. No test exercised a multi-token
subcommand `args` array, which is exactly the shape that breaks.

## Fix direction

Mirror the existing `latest` field's design (`command`/`args`/`env`,
verbatim, nothing auto-appended) with a new optional per-agent `version`
override, used in place of the `command args... --version` heuristic when
present. Same shape, same validation path (`agent/config.lua`), same
top-level `Louiselm.setup()` schema (`config.lua`). Deliberately not:
sniffing the CLI's argv structure, hardcoding `acp-llm-adapter` as a special
case, or dropping `args` from the default heuristic entirely (codex/claude
still need their single-token `args` forwarded to the wrapper script for
`--version` to resolve the right binary).

## Acceptance

- `tests/agent/config_spec.lua`: 6 new cases mirroring `latest`'s coverage
  for the new `version` field (accept, default args, leave nil, reject
  malformed, reject non-table).
- `tests/agent/health_spec.lua`: "installed-version override" group — uses
  the override verbatim instead of appending `--version` to the launch args;
  uses the override's own `env` instead of the agent's launch `env`; reports
  a missing override executable gracefully without spawning.
- `tests/schema/setup_spec.lua`: accepts/rejects the per-agent `version`
  override through `Louiselm.setup()`'s closed schema.
- Verified against the real binary: `acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter --version`
  → `acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2`, and `Health.check` with the override configured
  → `{ok = true, version = "acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2"}`.
- Full suite green: 277/277. `stylua --check` and
  `lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning` clean on all touched files.

## Not covered

The `deepseek`/`glm` "skill discovery found 31 issue(s)" notification in the
same `:checkhealth` output is unrelated (skill metadata parsing, not agent
version checking) — not investigated as part of this bug, left for separate
filing if it's still present after this fix.
close_reason: Fixed: added optional per-agent 'version' override (lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua, lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, lua/louiselm/config.lua), mirroring the existing 'latest' field's design — verbatim command/args/env, nothing auto-appended. Applied to the user's real dotfiles config (deepseek/glm now specify version={command=acp-debug.sh, args={acp-llm-adapter, --version}}). Verified against the real acp-llm-adapter binary through the real acp-debug.sh wrapper: Health.check now returns {ok=true, version='acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2'} instead of 'version command returned no output'. Tests: tests/agent/config_spec.lua (6 new cases), tests/agent/health_spec.lua ('installed-version override' group, 3 cases), tests/schema/setup_spec.lua (2 new cases). Full suite 277/277, stylua/lua-language-server clean.

title: Handle command and unknown permission requests in chat UI
description: Confirmed dogfood gap. The real claude-agent-acp file-edit probe emitted an ACP permission request and could be cancelled by a session event consumer. ui/chat/init.lua handles permission_requested only when operation.kind is file_edit; command and unknown requests are ignored, leaving the agent request unresolved in the interactive chat. Add a user-facing response path for every askable permission kind and cover a real fast-event-to-scheduled UI flow without auto-approving unscoped operations.
close_reason: Added scheduled command/unknown permission pickers, safe cancellation on dismissal and UI failure, disposal guards, tests, and documentation; all quality gates pass

title: GitLab CI: build and deploy blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via Pages
description:
## Goal
A GitLab CI pipeline in this repo that builds blog/ with MyST and deploys it to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages, with zero Neovim dependency in the CI image.

## Scope
- In scope: .gitlab-ci.yml job(s) running `myst build --html` against blog/ and publishing the result as a GitLab Pages artifact; a note on the one-time manual DNS/CNAME step needed to point blog.bartab.fr at GitLab Pages (DNS itself is outside this repo's automation).
- Out of scope: rendering nvim-transcript excerpts in CI (explicitly not done — that only ever happens locally, output is committed); anything at the bartab.fr root domain.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Pushing to the relevant branch triggers a pipeline that runs `myst build --html` against blog/ and succeeds without installing or invoking Neovim.
2. The build output is published via GitLab Pages and reachable at blog.bartab.fr (once DNS is pointed, noted as a manual prerequisite).
3. The CI job fails loudly (not silently) if blog/ fails to build — e.g. a broken literalinclude reference.

## Testing
- Pipeline run validation: a green pipeline with a published Pages artifact is the acceptance test here, not a unit test.

## Notes
- Depends on the MyST scaffold task (needs a buildable blog/ project to point CI at).
- Benefits from render-post.sh existing for a realistic end-to-end validation (a post with real rendered excerpts) but does not strictly require it — CI can be stood up and proven against the bare scaffold first.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
